# Welcome to Slate

Source: https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/index.md

Slate is one home for every AI coding tool you use. It shows every AI coding session on your Mac live, and gives all 16 agents one memory, one set of skills and rules, and one set of connections. Your work stays on your Mac.

It is for developers who use two or more AI coding tools, often at the same time. Each tool keeps its own sessions, memory, rules and connections, and none of them shows the others. Slate puts them in one place.

## What Slate does

* **Every session, live.** [Sessions](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/sessions.md) lists every AI coding session on this Mac, from any of the 16 agents, including the ones you started in your own terminal. The sessions that need you come first.
* **One memory for every agent.** What one agent learns, the next one recalls. Slate captures it from the sessions themselves, and every connected agent reads and writes it. See [Memory](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/memory.md).
* **Skills and rules, written once.** [Toolkit](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/toolkit.md) writes your skills and instructions into each agent's own setup.
* **One set of connections.** [Connect](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/connect.md) holds your agents, their accounts, MCP servers and integrations for every tool.
* **Your own agents, no API keys.** Slate runs the command-line tools you already installed and signed in to. See [Agents](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/agents.md).

Around these sit [Home](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/home.md), [Projects](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/projects.md), [Tasks](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/tasks.md), [Automations](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/automations.md), [Artifacts](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/artifacts.md), [Widgets](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/widgets.md) and [Activity](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/activity.md).

## Your work stays on your Mac

You sign in once, with Google or GitHub. The account holds your name, email and plan. Your docs, sessions and memory stay in files on your Mac. Your work leaves it only when you share a workspace, or when an agent you run sends it to that agent's own provider. See [Privacy and security](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/privacy-and-security.md).

Slate is free for individuals. Team plans, for sharing a workspace, are coming. See [Licensing and updates](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/licensing.md).

## Start here

* [Install and first ten minutes](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/overview/getting-started.md)
* [Core concepts](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/overview/concepts.md)

> **Note:** Slate runs on macOS 13.5 or later, with one app for Apple Silicon and one for Intel. See [Platform and availability](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/platform.md).

---

# Install and first ten minutes

Source: https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/overview/getting-started.md

This guide takes you from nothing to a connected agent, a first session and a first memory.

## Install

Slate needs macOS 13.5 or later, on Apple Silicon or Intel. Run this in Terminal:

```bash
curl -fsSL https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/install.sh | bash
```

The script downloads the app for your Mac's chip. It checks the download against its published checksum and checks Slate's own signature, and stops if either is wrong. Then it quits a running Slate, installs to `/Applications` and opens it.

Use the script, not a browser download. Slate is not notarized by Apple, so macOS blocks an app a browser downloaded.

You also need at least one agent: the command-line program of any of the [16 agents](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/agents.md), installed and signed in. Slate uses that sign-in, so there is no API key to enter.

## Sign in

The first launch asks you to sign in with **Continue with Google** or **Continue with GitHub**. Your browser opens; approve the sign-in there. This needs the internet once. After that Slate opens at once, even offline.

The account holds your name, email and plan. Your work stays on this Mac.

## The four setup steps

Setup has four steps: **Welcome**, **Agents**, **Integrations** and **Project**. **Skip setup** at the top leaves from any step. Setup does not come back on the next launch.

1. **Welcome** shows who is signed in and a short tour of four places in Slate.
2. **Agents** (*Connect your agents*) lists all 16 agents, in the same order as Connect.
   - An agent found on this Mac reads *On this Mac · uses your own sign-in*. Its switch connects it: Slate installs itself into that agent, so it shares one memory with the others. This is the only time Slate asks before it writes to another program's setup.
   - **Runs Slate's AI** picks the agent that answers in Home and Ask AI.
   - An agent that is missing reads **Not on this Mac** and offers **Install**, which shows how to install it.
   - Ten agents read **Beta** beside their name: Slate works with them, but nobody has run a session on them yet to check every part. Gemini reads *Needs a Gemini Code Assist licence or an API key*.
   - **Connect all** connects every agent found. The line *Start Slate in the menu bar when you log in* is ticked; untick it if you do not want that.
   - **Continue** waits until one agent is connected. **I'll connect one later** lets you go on without one.
3. **Integrations** (*Connect your integrations*) connects the apps your work lives in, such as GitHub, Linear, Jira, Slack and Notion. You can go on without any.
4. **Project** (*Choose your projects*) lists the git repositories in your home folder, most recently changed first, with none ticked. Tick the ones you work on, or press **Or choose another folder**. macOS may ask to let Slate see your Documents, Desktop or Downloads folder; Slate looks there only for git projects. If another memory tool is on this Mac, such as claude-mem or agentmemory, a line says what it holds, with **Preview** to bring it in. See [Import](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/connect/import.md).

**Open Slate** adds the projects you ticked and ends setup.

## Your first session and memory

Setup ends on **Sessions**. It shows every AI session on this Mac, live, even before an agent is connected. See [Sessions](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/sessions.md).

**Home** holds a **Set up Slate** card with three steps:

1. **Connect an agent**
2. **Start a session**: **New session** runs your agent in a folder.
3. **See your first memory**: **Open Memory** shows what a session decided or learned.

Each step ticks itself when it is done. The card goes away when all three are done, or when you press **Skip setup**.

Slate records only sessions that run in a project. To add one later, use **New project…** in the project picker at the top of Projects.

## Connect your other agents

Turn on more agents in **Connect → Agents**, and pick the account each one runs under. See [Connect](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/connect.md). To connect an agent by hand, see [Connecting your agents](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/mcp-server/connecting.md).

Using VS Code or Cursor? Add Slate to it in one click: [Install in VS Code](vscode:mcp/install?%7B%22name%22%3A%22slate%22%2C%22command%22%3A%22%2FApplications%2FSlate.app%2FContents%2FMacOS%2Fslate-mcp%22%2C%22args%22%3A%5B%5D%7D) or [Install in Cursor](cursor://anysphere.cursor-deeplink/mcp/install?name=slate&config=eyJjb21tYW5kIjoiL0FwcGxpY2F0aW9ucy9TbGF0ZS5hcHAvQ29udGVudHMvTWFjT1Mvc2xhdGUtbWNwIiwiYXJncyI6W119).

Once connected, an agent reads Slate's memory at the start of a task and saves what it learned at the end. See [Slate as an MCP server](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/mcp-server.md).

## Share a workspace

Sharing is not part of setup. Every account is on the Free plan: everything Slate does on this Mac, with no card and no time limit. Sharing a workspace needs the Team plan, which is coming. To hear when it is ready, press **Tell me when it's ready** in **Settings → Account**. See [Workspaces](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/workspaces.md).

## Where to go next

* [Core concepts](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/overview/concepts.md)
* [Keyboard shortcuts](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/shortcuts.md): press <kbd>⌘K</kbd> for the command palette
* [Privacy and security](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/privacy-and-security.md)

---

# Core concepts

Source: https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/overview/concepts.md

Slate rests on six ideas. Read them once and every screen makes sense.

## Sessions are what you see first

A session is one conversation with an agent, in one folder. [Sessions](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/sessions.md) shows every session on this Mac while it runs: the ones Slate started and the ones you started in your own terminal. A session waiting on your answer is marked **Needs you** and comes first.

## Agents are the tools you already have

An agent is an AI coding tool Slate connects to: Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, GitHub Copilot, Antigravity, OpenCode, Gemini, Cline, Grok Build, Kiro, Qwen Code, Droid, Hermes Agent, Goose, Kilo Code or Auggie. Slate runs each one's command-line program under the sign-in you already have. Slate ships no model and asks for no API key. See [Agents](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/agents.md).

## A project is a folder you open

A **project** is one folder, usually a git repository. A **group** is a set of projects you make and name; its memory and settings reach every project in it. Slate records the sessions that run in a project's folder. A session in any other folder shows in Sessions under **No project** while it runs, and is not kept.

Inside a project you keep **docs**: plans, designs, reviews, bug reports and notes. A git branch is a label on Slate's records, never a doc of its own. See [Projects](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/projects.md).

## Memory is shared by every agent

Slate keeps one memory for all your agents. It learns from the sessions it captures, and connected agents save to it with `remember` and read from it with `recall`. Memory is filed under the project or group it belongs to, so a session gets what applies to its folder. See [Memory](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/memory.md).

## Toolkit and Connect set up every agent at once

[Toolkit](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/toolkit.md) holds your skills, rules and instructions, and writes them into each agent's own setup. [Connect](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/connect.md) holds which agents each workspace uses, under which account, and the MCP servers and integrations they reach.

## A workspace is shared or private as a whole

A **workspace** holds projects, docs, memory and activity, in one file on your Mac. **Personal** is yours and starts private. A workspace you share is shared whole: everything in it is readable by its members. Nothing is shared doc by doc, so private work belongs in a workspace you have not shared.

Each doc has one writer, its author. A teammate's doc opens read-only. See [Workspaces](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/workspaces.md).

---

# Uninstalling

Source: https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/overview/uninstalling.md

One command removes Slate and takes back what it changed in your agents. Your workspace is kept.

```bash
curl -fsSL https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/uninstall.sh | bash
```

Use the command, not the Trash. Dragging Slate to the Trash leaves its entries in every agent it connected to, pointing at an app that is gone.

## See it first

`--dry-run` prints every step and changes nothing:

```bash
curl -fsSL https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/uninstall.sh | bash -s -- --dry-run
```

## What it removes

| What | Detail |
| --- | --- |
| Slate's entries in your agents | Its plugins, hooks and MCP entries, only in the accounts Slate wrote to. An MCP server you added yourself is never touched |
| `/Applications/Slate.app` | The app |
| Start at login | Slate's entry in System Settings → Login Items |
| Logs, cache and web view data | Three folders under `~/Library` that Slate rebuilds |

## What it keeps

Your data folder, `~/Library/Application Support/app.slate.workspace/`, stays. It holds your Personal workspace, one file for each shared workspace, this computer's settings, your sign-in and the backups. Reinstall Slate and it opens the same files.

What Toolkit wrote into your project folders (skill folders, instruction files) also stays. It belongs to the project.

## Remove your workspace too

```bash
curl -fsSL https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/uninstall.sh | bash -s -- --delete-workspace
```

**This cannot be undone.** It removes the whole data folder, and no other copy exists. Before you run it:

* Export what you want to keep: **Settings → Workspaces**, the workspace, **Storage**, **Export**.
* In a shared workspace, the rows you published stay for its members. Take them back first with **Stop sharing** or **Erase my work**. See [Workspaces](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/workspaces.md).

A Personal workspace you moved to another folder is not in the data folder, so it stays.

## Options

| Flag | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `--dry-run` | Print every step and change nothing |
| `--delete-workspace` | Also remove the data folder |
| `--keep-connections` | Leave Slate's entries in your agents alone |
| `--prefix <dir>` | Look for `Slate.app` in another folder than `/Applications` |

The script asks no questions, so the step that removes your data is a flag you type. It removes only Slate: if the app it finds is not Slate, it stops and removes nothing.

## If you already removed the app

The script still removes the logs, cache and web view data. It cannot remove Slate's entries in your agents without the app. They do nothing on their own. To remove them, install Slate again and run the uninstall command.

---

# Sessions

Source: https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/sessions.md

**Sessions** shows every session of your agents on this computer, live, so you see at a glance which one needs you and which is working. It covers all 16 agents and sessions in your own terminals too. Nothing to install: a session appears within seconds of starting.

With nothing selected, the main area shows the map, and the list runs down the left. Click a row to open the session in a tab. [The map and the list](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/sessions/list.md) explains each part.

## What you see

Each live session has one state:

| State | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| **Needs you** (amber) | The agent finished a turn and waits on you: it asks permission for a tool call, asks a question, or reports that it finished |
| **Working** (green) | The agent wrote to its session in the last 45 seconds |
| **Idle** (grey) | Quiet, and you spoke last. A session that only waits (a `sleep`, a scheduled wakeup) is idle too |

The header counts each state. **⌘⇧J** opens the session that has waited longest, then the next. When a session starts to wait for permission or an answer and Slate is not in front, macOS shows one notification. A finished turn posts none; it waits on [Home](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/home.md). Turn notifications off with **Tell me when a session needs me** in Automations › Built-in. How a state is worked out: [Status and flow](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/sessions/status.md).

A session that ended moves to **Just finished**, then **Earlier today**. Subagents are not sessions: the parent's row counts them.

## Narrowing to a workspace or a project

The picker above the list starts on **All workspaces**. Pick a workspace to keep only its sessions, in the list and the map. A session no workspace claims counts as Personal's. A second picker then narrows to one project (**All projects**). The choice lasts while the window is open.

## A session's pull request

Slate checks origin for pull requests, asking once a minute, and shows **#118** on the row when one points at the branch's tip. Slate opens no pull requests: push and open one on your code host.

## The keyboard

Tab reaches the list's rows and Enter opens one. With focus in the list:

| Key | Does |
| --- | --- |
| ↑ ↓ or **j** **k** | Move between sessions |
| **Home**, **End** | First or last row |
| **f** | Start a second agent in the row's folder |
| **s** | End the session (press twice within four seconds) |
| **Escape** | Back to the terminal |

From anywhere, ⌘K → **Focus the sessions list** puts focus on the first row. All keys: [Keyboard shortcuts](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/shortcuts.md#sessions).

## Ending a session

Point at a row and click **End**. It turns red and reads **End?**; click again, or press **s**, within four seconds. A Claude Code session that runs as a background job keeps its conversation, so you can attach to it again. Any other session ends. **End** works on sessions Slate did not start, such as a CLI in another terminal.

Quitting Slate ends the sessions it hosts, except Claude Code sessions, which keep running as background jobs.

## In the menu bar

The Sessions icon in the menu bar shows a count while a session needs you. Its panel lists the sessions that work or wait on you; click one to open it. It also has **Keep the computer awake**, **New session**, **Open Slate** and **Quit Slate**. Closing the window only hides Slate; ⌘Q quits.

## More about sessions

- [The map and the list](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/sessions/list.md): the map, a row, the row menu, parking, past sessions.
- [Start a session](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/sessions/start.md): **+**, New session, a folder, a doc, a Terminal.
- [Your terminal and Slate](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/sessions/take-over.md): continue a terminal session here, or hand one back.
- [Worktrees](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/sessions/worktrees.md): the new checkout every session on a git project gets.
- [Workers](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/sessions/workers.md) and [Ask Slate](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/sessions/ask-slate.md): a session that starts other agents.
- [Cloud sessions and phone](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/sessions/cloud.md).
- [The terminal and Conversation](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/sessions/terminal.md) and [The side panel](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/sessions/side-panel.md).
- [Tabs, columns and names](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/sessions/tabs.md).
- [Review the branch](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/sessions/review.md) and [Files, memories and editing](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/sessions/files.md).
- [Status and flow](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/sessions/status.md): how a state and a step are worked out.

---

# The map and the list

Source: https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/sessions/list.md

Sessions draws the same sessions twice: as a map in the main area and as a list on the left. Read on to tell a node, a row or a colour apart.

## The map

The map is a tree with this computer at the centre: **group → project → branch → session**. A session with no project hangs from **No project**. A node shows the most urgent state of the sessions under it. Pointing at a node lights its rows in the list, and pointing at a row lights its node.

- Click a group or project to centre it. The list narrows to its sessions, and a trail of names above it takes you back up.
- **All**, a click on empty space, or **Escape** returns to the whole computer.
- Click Slate Bot at the centre to [Ask Slate](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/sessions/ask-slate.md).
- Drag a node to reorder it; **Reset layout** undoes it.
- In a window narrower than about 1024 px the map is hidden and the list shows everything.

## The list

Sessions are grouped under their group or project. One outside every project goes under its git repository's name, or else **No project**. Sessions that need you come first, then working ones, then idle ones. The order holds still while the pointer is in the list.

A session is listed where its edits land. If an agent edits another worktree of the same project, its row moves under that worktree's branch and says *from \<folder>*.

## A row

| Part | Shows |
| --- | --- |
| Title | The branch checked out in the session's folder, with its checkout marks and pull request (`ui/hotfixes ↑4 #118`). With no branch: the session's name, else what it was asked |
| Second line | The question when it waits on you; what it said it is doing when it works; the next plan item when it went quiet with work left |
| Third line | The agent's mark, time since it moved, how it runs, context fill, and its [flow](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/sessions/status.md#flow) step (**Build**, **Check**, **Waiting**) |

A terminal glyph means Slate runs the session; an eye means it runs in your own terminal and Slate follows. Context fill reads `8% of 258k` when the agent states its window, else a count (`323k`).

**Colours.** Amber: needs you. Green: working. Grey: idle. Red: failures. Blue: live subagents.

**Checkout marks.**

| Mark | Means |
| --- | --- |
| `↑3` | Commits the branch has that its base lacks |
| `↓1` | Commits the base gained since |
| Grey ring | Uncommitted work |
| **missing** | git lists the worktree, but its folder is gone |
| **not read** | git did not answer in time |
| **owed** | The session did real work and saved nothing to memory yet |
| **Review · n files** | A branch waiting for you ([Review the branch](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/sessions/review.md#branches-waiting-for-review)) |

A worktree with nothing running in it reads *checked out, nothing running*. One where a subagent works reads *working · subagent of fix/login*.

A [Terminal](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/sessions/start.md#a-terminal) is a row too, always grey, titled by what runs in it now (`zsh`, `npm`), with its folder under it.

## Row actions

Click a row to open the session in a temporary tab, which the next click replaces. Double-click keeps the tab. Pointing at a row shows two buttons: **End**, which ends the session on a second click, and **⋯**, the menu:

| Item | Does |
| --- | --- |
| **Open beside** | Shows the session in a column beside yours (⌘-click does the same) |
| **PR #118** | Opens the pull request in your browser |
| **Hand back to my terminal** | On a Claude Code session Slate runs ([Your terminal and Slate](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/sessions/take-over.md)) |
| **Review & merge** | Opens the review of a waiting branch |
| **New session** | Starts a session in a new worktree of the project |
| **Copy path** | Copies the folder's path |
| **Make a project** | On a row under **No project**: makes its folder a project |
| **Copy resume command** | Copies the agent's resume command, such as `claude --resume <id>` |

A branch or project, on the map or as a heading, offers **New session** (+), **Branch changes** ([what the branch changed](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/sessions/review.md#reviewing-the-whole-branch)) and, on a checkout, **Run preview** ([Run preview](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/sessions/worktrees.md#run-preview)).

**Park** hides a worktree that reads *checked out, nothing running*. It moves to a **Parked · n** line at the end of its project, with **Unpark** beside each. Nothing on disk changes, and the choice is kept on this computer only.

## Finished and past sessions

**Just finished** sits at the foot of the list for ten minutes after a session ends. A tick means its last turn finished; *Stopped before it finished* means it was stopped mid-turn. Click one to open its record.

**Earlier today in \<workspace>** folds the rest of today's sessions. **All past sessions in \<workspace> →** opens the whole history, newest first; **Resume** on a row continues it on [Home](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/home/ask.md#resume-a-past-session).

Drag the list's edge to resize it. **⌘B** hides it.

---

# Start a session

Source: https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/sessions/start.md

Start a session where the work is, and it opens in Slate on the agent and account of that project or group. On a git project every session starts in a new [worktree](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/sessions/worktrees.md) of its own, so sessions never share a checkout with each other or with you. A folder that is not a git repository runs in place.

## From the map or the list

Point at a group, project or branch, on the map or in the list, and click **+** (**New session**). The session starts at once on the project's default agent, under its account, and opens. Nothing asks: the worktree gets the default name and the project's saved **Carry over**.

If the session cannot start, or the worktree cannot be made, the reason shows on its tab. Nothing starts in the main folder instead.

## New session

The **+** at the top of the list opens **New session**: one screen to start anywhere, on any agent. Only the project has to be chosen; everything else opens on your last answer.

1. **Session | Terminal**, at the top left. Leave it on **Session** for an agent, or pick **Terminal** for your own shell ([below](#a-terminal)).
2. **The project.** Search, or pick from your projects as **group → project → branch**. A click selects a row; it starts nothing. The last row, **Open folder…**, starts in any folder you pick ([below](#open-a-folder)).
3. **The agent** and **Where it runs**: **This computer** or **Cloud** ([Cloud sessions](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/sessions/cloud.md)). The agent list holds the agents connected in Connect → Agents for the project's workspace.
4. **Name** and **Carry over**, on a git project: the new worktree's branch name and the ignored files to copy into it ([Worktrees](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/sessions/worktrees.md#start-in-a-new-worktree)).
5. **On my phone**, for an agent that can continue on the phone ([On my phone](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/sessions/cloud.md#on-my-phone)).
6. **Start**, or **Create and start** on a git project. **Enter** starts too; **Escape** closes.

A session runs as the workspace its project belongs to, whichever workspace the window shows. A refused start says why at the top of New session.

## Open a folder

**Open folder…** starts a session in any folder. A folder another workspace holds opens there. Any other folder becomes a project in the workspace on screen first:

| Folder | Becomes |
| --- | --- |
| A worktree or subfolder of a git repository | That git repository's project |
| Already a project | That project; a project in Trash comes back |
| Inside a group | A project in that group |
| A plain folder that holds two or more git repositories | Each git repository becomes a project. Slate asks first: **Group them** puts them in one group, **Keep them apart** does not |
| Anything else | A project on its own |

Your home folder and the disk root are refused.

**A session in a folder no project holds is not recorded**: it shows while it runs, but gets no doc. Memories it saves still count, as global memory. A row under **No project** offers **Make a project** in its **⋯** menu; from then on its sessions are recorded, and so are earlier ones whose transcripts are still on disk.

## From a project

A group's or project's **⋯** menu in Projects has **Start session**. The session runs on the agent and account that group or project assigns, in a new worktree when the doc's folder is a git project.

The branch goal and the next unchecked plan item are typed into the agent's prompt (`Continue on feat/x: … — next: …`), never sent. Edit it and press Enter yourself. If the agent's startup screen swallows it, the terminal says so and offers **Insert it** or **Copy the goal**.

The doc's header lists the sessions working on it, marked *needs you*, *working* or *idle*. Click one to open it.

## A Terminal

A **Terminal** is your own login shell, with your shell and environment, hosted in Slate like a session. Open one from:

- **New session**, switched to **Terminal**. It opens in the project's own folder, with no worktree, because a worktree removed when the shell exits would take your work with it.
- **The Ask Slate box**, switched to **Terminal** ([Ask Slate](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/sessions/ask-slate.md#a-terminal-instead)).
- **⌃\`**, in the folder of the doc you are on, or your home folder. A folder's menu has **Open a Terminal here**.

A Terminal is a grey row in the list and a dot on the map. It has no status, account, side panel or hand-back, and no count includes it. **Ctrl+C** goes to the program running in it. Its row's **End** closes it.

---

# Your terminal and Slate

Source: https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/sessions/take-over.md

A session can move between your own terminal and Slate. Continue a terminal session here when you want Slate's panel and tabs around it; hand one back when you want it in your terminal again.

## Continue a session from your terminal

Click the session's row. Slate shows its conversation, live, read from its transcript, with its details in the side panel. Nothing on that screen types into your terminal. One button above the conversation says what continuing it would do:

| Session | Button | What happens |
| --- | --- | --- |
| A Claude Code background job, or a Cursor `persist` session | **Open in Slate** | The session itself opens in Slate. Nothing is copied or interrupted |
| Claude Code in a terminal, Codex, OpenCode | **Continue in a copy** | Slate starts a second conversation with the whole history. The original keeps running where it is |
| Cursor, Gemini | **Move here** | The original ends first, then the session continues here. Click twice, because a turn in progress is lost |

A copy has its own transcript, so the two never mix. Its row says **Copy in Slate**. The original's row offers **Open your copy** to read or stop it. Slate uses the session's own account, so the copy finds the same conversation.

## Hand a session back to your terminal

**Hand back to my terminal**, in a row's **⋯** menu, detaches a Claude Code session that Slate runs and leaves it running. Only Claude Code can do this.

1. Slate sends Claude Code its detach input and closes the session's terminal in Slate.
2. A message, **Handed back to your terminal**, gives the command to attach to it again, such as `claude attach <handle>`, with **Copy resume command**.
3. If Slate cannot name the command, the message says *It keeps running in the background*.

Run the command in any terminal to pick the session up.

---

# Worktrees

Source: https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/sessions/worktrees.md

A worktree is a second checkout of a project on its own branch, so an agent works without touching your main folder. Every session started on a git project starts in a new worktree of its own, however you start it. A folder that is not a git repository runs in place, and so does a worktree you pick on purpose.

## Start in a new worktree

On a git project, [New session](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/sessions/start.md#new-session) asks two things, then **Create and start**:

- **Name** names the branch and the folder. Left empty, it is `session-<today>`, such as `session-2026-11-18`, with `-2`, `-3`… when that branch exists. The branch starts from the project's trunk; the folder sits beside the project's folder.
- **Carry over** lists what the project ignores at its top level, such as `node_modules` or `.env`. Tick what the new folder needs. git copies only tracked files, so without this a fresh worktree has no dependencies or build output. On a Mac each folder is cloned copy-on-write: it costs no disk until a file changes, and changes never reach the original.

**Carry over** is saved on the project when you press **Create and start**, and every other start uses it. If a ticked path could not be carried, New session names it and offers **Start anyway**.

## The project's worktree commands

A project's **Settings** has a **New worktrees** section with three commands:

| Setting | Runs |
| --- | --- |
| **Set up** | In the new folder once its files are there: a build, codegen, a submodule fetch. Empty is normal |
| **Preview** | When you press **Run preview** ([below](#run-preview)) |
| **On remove** | In the folder just before the worktree is removed: stop a server, drop a local database. If it fails, the worktree stays and the error shows its output |

Commands run in `/bin/sh` with your login shell's `PATH` and environment.

If carry-over or **Set up** fails, the new worktree is removed again and the error shows the command's output. Fix the cause and press **Create and start** again with the same name.

## Ports

Each worktree Slate makes gets a free port from 4100 to 4999, kept until the worktree is removed. It is `SLATE_PORT` in **Set up**, **On remove** and every session terminal in that folder, so two worktrees can each run `vite --port $SLATE_PORT`. The row shows it as `:4101`.

## Run preview

**Run preview** starts a checkout's dev server, such as `yarn dev`. Find it on a branch's row or map node.

1. Its terminal opens beside the session, so a failure says why.
2. When the server prints a local address, such as `http://localhost:5173`, it opens as a **Preview** tab.
3. The tab can **Reload**, **Open in your browser** or **Stop the preview**, which ends the server.

The first run on a project asks for the command; **Save and run** stores it.

**Pick an element** (the crosshair) turns the preview into a picker. Point at anything, click, and its description is pasted at the prompt of the session in that folder: the address it is on, a CSS selector, its size and position, its styles and its HTML. Nothing is sent: add what to change and press Enter. Click the crosshair again (**Stop picking**) to leave.

## A session's worktree ends with it

When a session that started in a new worktree ends (you exit the agent or press **End**; closing its tab is not an end), Slate cleans up:

| State | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Nothing uncommitted, branch merged or empty | Folder and branch are removed |
| Commits not merged | Folder is removed, the branch stays |
| Uncommitted changes | Slate asks once: **Keep worktree** or **Delete forever** |

First, the processes Slate started in that worktree (a dev server, a watcher, a test run) are stopped. A process you started elsewhere is never touched. A message says what was freed, such as **Cleaned up · stopped :3000 · 11.2 GB freed**.

Slate never removes a worktree it did not make for a session.

**Remove a worktree yourself** with the trash icon on a branch row in New session's list. It asks before discarding uncommitted work, and can delete the branch too.

To review and merge a finished branch, see [Review the branch](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/sessions/review.md).

---

# Workers

Source: https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/sessions/workers.md

A session can split its work and hand pieces to **workers**, so several agents work on one job at once. A worker is an [agent run](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/tasks/agent-runs.md): its own branch, its own worktree and a terminal you can see. The session that started it is its **coordinator**. Any agent can coordinate and any can work: a Claude Code session can start a Codex worker and a Cursor worker.

Slate does not plan the work. Ask your session in your own words, such as "fix these three issues, one worker each". It starts each worker with Slate's `start_agent_run` tool and waits for them with `wait_for_runs` ([MCP tools](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/mcp-server/tools.md)).

## Where workers show

- **Sessions.** Workers are listed under their coordinator, behind a line such as **3 workers · 2 working · 1 waiting on you**. Each is a full session row, with its terminal, status and controls. A worker that has not started yet shows **Starting**.
- **The side panel.** The coordinator's Details starts with **Workers**: how many are done, a bar with one segment per worker, and a row per worker with its step.
- **Home.** A waiting worker's card says **Worker of** its coordinator.

## Approve a worker

A worker stops for you at the same two points as any agent run: its plan and its ship. In the coordinator's Details, the worker that needs you opens by itself, with one line of what it found, **Approve plan**, **Plan** to read its steps, and **Send back** to write a note. Click another worker's row to open it.

The coordinator cannot approve for a worker. A worker's questions and permission prompts come to you.

## How a worker starts

The session asks, and Slate makes the run: its branch, worktree and rules. The open Slate window then opens the worker's terminal. If Slate is closed, the worker waits and starts when Slate opens. If its terminal cannot open, the run offers **Resume**.

## Limits

- **At most 3 at once.** A fourth worker is refused until one finishes.
- **One level.** A worker cannot start workers.
- **The open workspace.** The window opens workers of the workspace it shows.

Each worker costs what any session costs: a CLI, a worktree and the model's usage.

---

# Ask Slate

Source: https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/sessions/ask-slate.md

**Ask Slate** is one box for work when you do not want to pick a project first. Type what you want done; Slate starts a session on your own agent, and that session finds the right project and starts the work there.

## Ask

1. Click Slate Bot beside Search in the top bar or at the centre of the Sessions map, or press ⌘K and choose **Ask Slate…**.
2. Type what you want done. **Shift+Enter** adds a line; **Esc** closes.
3. Press **Enter**. Slate starts a new session on the workspace's default agent, under its account, with your words as the first prompt, and opens it in Sessions.

Each Enter starts a new session, so several can run at once. Sessions lists them under **Slate**. Slate adds no AI of its own: the session is your agent.

## What the session does

Slate tells the session that it coordinates work across your projects, which projects Slate knows in every workspace, and where each one's folder is. Then:

- **Work in a project** is done by a [worker](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/sessions/workers.md) the session starts in that project. The session never changes a project's files itself.
- **A question** that changes no project, such as "what is running?" or "what is on my plate?", it answers itself with Slate's tools.
- **Two projects that could fit**: it asks you which one.

The session runs in a folder Slate makes for each ask. That folder holds no code, never becomes a project and gets no worktree.

## Which agents

| Agent | Your words | On my phone |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Claude Code | Passed at launch | On, when the account allows it |
| Codex, Cursor, OpenCode | Passed at launch | Not offered |
| Gemini, Copilot and the other agents | Typed into the terminal once it is up; press Enter there | Not offered |

## A Terminal instead

At the box's top left, **Session | Terminal** switches what the box starts. It opens on **Session** each time. On **Terminal**, **Enter** opens a new [Terminal](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/sessions/start.md#a-terminal) in your home folder and runs your words as its first command. An empty Enter opens a plain shell.

## Limits

- A worker starts only in a git project.
- A session has at most 3 workers at once.
- Every worker's plan and ship still wait for your approval.

---

# Cloud sessions and phone

Source: https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/sessions/cloud.md

A cloud session runs on your agent vendor's computers, so it keeps going while yours sleeps. A phone session runs here, and you continue it in your agent's phone app. Both start from **New session**.

## Cloud sessions

**Claude Code** and **Codex** can run cloud sessions. Gemini and OpenCode cannot ([Features by agent](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/agents/features-by-agent.md)).

1. Open **New session** and set **Where it runs** to **Cloud**. The list then shows git projects only, because the cloud works on a copy.
2. Pick a project and write the **Task**.
3. Press **Start in cloud**.

What leaves your computer depends on the agent:

- **Claude** clones the project's GitHub remote at your current branch, so push first. With no GitHub remote it uploads the history and uncommitted changes to tracked files.
- **Codex** runs in an *environment* you set up for the project at chatgpt.com/codex, on its GitHub remote at your current branch. Type the environment's name; the last one used for the project is filled in.

The session runs under the project's account. Claude needs a claude.ai sign-in: an API key, token, Bedrock or Vertex account cannot start one, and the form says so. Codex needs a ChatGPT sign-in.

**Find it** in the list under its project, with a cloud where the status dot sits. A Codex row says **Working**, **Ready**, **Applied** or **Failed**. Claude keeps no list Slate can read, so its row says the status is on claude.ai.

**Open it** to see what you asked and every message since:

| Agent | Controls |
| --- | --- |
| Claude | **Send** a follow-up; Claude queues it and answers on claude.ai. **Bring back** opens the session in a new worktree with its whole conversation, as a normal session on this computer |
| Codex | **Show diff** (read-only). **Apply in a worktree** puts the changes, uncommitted, into a new worktree |
| Both | **Open on** the vendor's site; **Remove from Slate** (it stays on the site). Neither agent can stop a cloud session from Slate |

**Started somewhere else.** A Claude cloud session that another Claude Code session started, such as a scheduled task, appears within 15 seconds while the window is open. Its row says **started by a scheduled task** or **started from another session**. Cloud sessions started on the web or the phone are not listed.

A running cloud session cannot reach Slate's memory. A brought-back Claude session is recorded like any session once you send it a message.

## On my phone

A session can continue from your phone while it runs here. Slate has no phone app: you pick the session up in your agent's app. Today that is **Claude Code**, in the Claude app (**Code** tab) or at claude.ai/code.

- **Start on the phone**: tick **On my phone** in New session, above **Start**.
- **Move a running session to the phone**: press **On my phone** at the top of the session.

Either opens a card, **Ready on my phone**, with three steps and the session's link to copy or open. The same button, now blue, opens the card again; **Stop phone access** turns it off. A phone mark shows on the row, and the header counts the sessions **on my phone**. A session you put on the phone with `/remote-control` in your own terminal shows the mark too.

| Session | On my phone |
| --- | --- |
| Claude Code running in Slate | Works |
| Claude Code in your own terminal | Type `/remote-control` there |
| An account that cannot (API key, token, Bedrock, Vertex, or turned off by your organization) | Greyed out, with Claude's reason |
| Codex, Cursor, Gemini, OpenCode | Not available |

The session still runs on this computer, so Slate records it as usual. While it is on, Anthropic keeps the conversation.

---

# The terminal and Conversation

Source: https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/sessions/terminal.md

A session Slate runs lives in a real terminal, so the agent's CLI looks and behaves as it does in Terminal.app. **Conversation** reads the same session back as messages and steps, for when you want to read rather than watch.

## The terminal

The agent runs with its full screen: colours, spinners, menus. Slate supplies the folder, account and context and stays out of the conversation. Claude Code sessions start as background jobs, so they keep running after you quit Slate and any terminal can attach to them. Leaving the tab or reloading the window never ends a session; coming back replays what it printed.

Above the terminal, one line shows where the session stands, such as **Working · Check**, and its plan progress. Click it to open Details in the [side panel](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/sessions/side-panel.md). Beside it are **On my phone** ([Cloud sessions and phone](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/sessions/cloud.md#on-my-phone)) and the **Terminal | Conversation** switch. Every session opens on **Terminal**; picking Conversation holds for that session only.

**Focus mode**, **⌘⇧M**, hides the top bar, the list and the panels, leaving only the session. The same keys bring them back.

### What the terminal does

| Feature | Behaviour |
| --- | --- |
| Keys | ⌘F finds in the scrollback. ⌘C copies, ⌘V pastes, ⌘+ ⌘− ⌘0 zoom (remembered). Shift+Enter adds a line. Option is Meta: ⌥← and ⌥→ jump a word. App keys such as ⌘K, ⌘P and ⌘W reach Slate. All keys: [Keyboard shortcuts](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/shortcuts.md#terminal) |
| Ctrl+C | In an agent's session it asks first, as closing the tab does ([Close a session's tab](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/sessions/tabs.md#close-a-sessions-tab)). In a Terminal it interrupts at once |
| Mouse | Selecting copies; the middle button pastes. Right-click: **Copy**, **Paste**, **Select all**, **Clear** (⌥⌘K), **Remember on** the session's doc |
| A selection | A bar offers **Copy** or **Remember**, which saves the selection as a memory under the session's doc |
| Scrolling up | Output keeps arriving; **Newest output** takes you back down |
| Links | A local address (`http://localhost:5173`) opens in a tab beside the session; other web links open in your browser. A printed path such as `src/x.ts:42` opens that file at that line. A `slate://` link opens that doc beside the session |
| Pictures | A picture the CLI draws (sixel, or the `imgcat` protocol) shows in place, up to 32 MB per terminal; past that the oldest become placeholders |
| Scrollback | 5,000 lines. A terminal you cannot see keeps 1,000, and its full scrollback returns when you look again |

## Conversation

**Conversation** shows the session in order: each prompt, what the agent said, and every tool step on one line with its target (a file, a command, a search).

- Click a step for its output. An edit opens on the lines it changed. A failed step says *failed*.
- The agent's plan sits on top, with done items ticked.
- The last 60 turns show. A step's output over 4,000 characters keeps its first and last 2,000.
- A picture a tool returned, such as a screenshot, shows under its step; click it for full size. A turn keeps about 4.4 MB of pictures; past that the step says how many were not kept.
- An image the agent saved and named in its reply shows from disk, up to 8 MB. An image on the web shows as a card you click to open.
- A ```` ```mermaid ```` block is drawn as a diagram. Links open as in the terminal.

Type at the foot to message the session. **Enter** sends it to the terminal's prompt; **Shift+Enter** adds a line. **/** lists the skills the agent loads in this folder and **@** names a doc, session, memory, task, automation or report, as on [Home](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/home/ask.md#skills-and-mentions). A file dropped on the box is attached the same way.

Menus and permission questions the agent draws itself show only in **Terminal**. When the session waits on one, a bar above the box says so; **Open Terminal** switches.

Claude Code, Codex, Gemini and OpenCode record each step with its output. Cursor records the steps only, and the view says so.

---

# The side panel

Source: https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/sessions/side-panel.md

The panel on the right of Sessions shows what the session in your active column did and changed, so you can follow it without reading the terminal. It is open by default and follows the column with the blue line on top.

- **⌥⌘B**, or the button at the end of the tab row, hides and shows it. The choice is remembered.
- Drag its left edge to resize it, from 280 px to 640 px and never past 60% of the window. Double-click the edge for 320 px.

It has a tab for each view:

| Tab | Shows |
| --- | --- |
| **Details** | Where the session runs, what it made, how far it has got. **⌥⌘I** opens it, and so does a click on the status line above the terminal |
| **Changes** | What the branch holds that its base lacks, with commit and sync. Its icon counts the files waiting to commit. See [Source control](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/sessions/review.md#source-control) |
| **Turns** | Every prompt, newest first |
| A widget | Only while a widget is made for Sessions ([Widgets](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/widgets.md)). It reads the session open beside it |

## Details

Details has these sections, top to bottom. A section with nothing to show is left out.

| Section | Shows |
| --- | --- |
| **Workers** | The session's [workers](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/sessions/workers.md): how many are done, and a row per worker with its step |
| **Environment** | The agent, project, branch and folder, and how many other agents work there |
| **Outputs** | What the session published in Slate, newest first, as cards with a picture |
| **Progress** | The session's [flow](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/sessions/status.md#flow): its step, such as **Check · 4 of 5**, the time it has run, and a bar |
| **Context** | How much of the agent's context window is used, such as *120k of 200k tokens* |
| **Links** | What the branch is attached to: its pull request, an issue, and its doc in Slate |

**Outputs** shows eight cards, the rest behind **Show N more**. A card opens the artifact beside the session, at half the window, while the session stays where it is. Its header has **Open in Artifacts** and **✕**, which goes back to Details. **Escape** closes it too.

**Links** reads `PR #142 · #138` when closed. Open it for a row per link; click one to open it. The pull request's number comes from your remote with no sign-in. Its title, checks (**checks passing**, **checks failing**, **checks running**), reviews and state are read with your own `gh` once you connect GitHub in Connect. A branch named for a Jira or Linear key (`SLT-138-…`) links that item from Tasks.

## Turns

**Turns** lists every prompt the session was given, newest first, with when. Click one to scroll the conversation to it, or find it in the terminal's scrollback. A prompt that changed files shows how many; open it to list the files, and click one to see what that turn changed.

Before each prompt, Slate takes a checkpoint of the session's folder: its tracked and untracked files, but not what the project ignores. Checkpoints never move your branch, staged changes or stash, and are hidden from `git log` and `git push`. The newest 100 are kept for each branch and worktree. A turn that changed nothing takes none.

---

# Tabs, columns and names

Source: https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/sessions/tabs.md

Every session you open is a tab, in the same strip as your docs and files. Columns put several side by side, and a name makes one easy to find.

## Tabs

A session's tab shows its status dot and name. Files, a branch's changes and previews open as tabs in the same strip. Every open tab stays alive, so switching tabs never stops a terminal.

Clicking a row in the list opens a **temporary** tab (in italics) that the next click replaces. A session you start gets a tab that stays. A session whose temporary tab was replaced keeps running and reads **In Slate · no window** in the list; click its row to bring the tab back.

**Escape** returns to the map without closing anything. Tab keys and gestures: [Search and command palette](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/search.md#tabs).

## Close a session's tab

Closing an agent's tab ends the session, after asking. The ×, a middle-click, ⌘W and Ctrl+C in its terminal all ask **End \<name>?**:

| Choice | Does |
| --- | --- |
| **End session** | Stops the agent, closes its terminal and takes it off the list |
| **Close tab only** | Closes the tab; the session keeps running as **In Slate · no window** |
| **Cancel** | Keeps the tab |

**Close others**, **Close to the right** and **Close all**, in a tab's right-click menu, ask once, naming every session they would end. A session in your own terminal is not Slate's to end: closing its tab leaves it running. Closing a Terminal's tab asks **Close this Terminal?**, because anything running in it stops.

## Columns

**⌘-click** a tab, or choose **Open beside** in a row's **⋯** menu, to open it in a new column beside yours. The main area holds up to **4 columns**; with four, Open beside adds a tab to the column next to yours.

- Each column has its own tabs. The column you work in has a blue line on top; click another to work there. The list marks each session on screen with its column: **left**, **middle**, **right**, or **column 1** to **column 4**.
- Drag the line between two columns to widen one; double-click it to make all equal. Widths are saved per workspace.
- **Unsplit**, at the top of the last column, or **⇧⌘\\**, returns to one column and keeps every tab.

## Name a session

Right-click a session's tab and choose **Rename…**. **Enter** or a click away keeps the name; **Escape** keeps the old one. A name is one line of up to 80 characters, and shows on the tab, the row and the session's doc.

A session with no name shows **\<Agent> session in \<project>**.

Slate passes the new name to the agent, so its own resume list shows it too:

| Agent | How |
| --- | --- |
| Claude Code, Codex, Cursor | Slate types `/rename <name>` when the session is free: the last turn ended and nothing is half-typed |
| OpenCode | Slate asks OpenCode's own server |
| Gemini | Gemini keeps no names; Slate keeps it |

Until it lands, the tab is dimmed, and pointing at it reads *Renaming in \<agent> when the session is free*. A `/rename` you type in one of these agents renames the tab and row too.

A Terminal can be renamed the same way. Slate keeps the name while the Terminal runs; clear it and the tab shows what runs in it again (`npm · Nimbus`).

## Agents that know about each other

With two or more sessions in one project, Slate tells each agent once, at the start of a turn, that the others are there: their agent, branch, state, what each was asked and its last message. The list says so under the group: **Told about 1 other session here**.

An agent can leave a note for the others, or for one of them; they see it once, on their next turn. Slate assigns no work: the agents decide.

---

# Review the branch

Source: https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/sessions/review.md

When an agent finishes on its own branch, Slate lists the branch as waiting for your review. Read every changed line, comment, then merge, keep or discard it. The **Changes** tab of the side panel commits and syncs as you go.

## Branches waiting for review

A worktree branch is waiting when its agent has finished and the branch has commits `main` lacks. Its row in the list carries a tag: **Review · n files**, **behind n** when `main` has moved past it, and how long it has waited. The header of Sessions counts the branches that can merge now (**n branches not merged**); click the count to open the one that has waited longest.

A branch `main` moved past cannot merge until its session rebases. With nothing running in it, it folds into a **Behind main · n** line at the end of its project.

Click the tag, or **Review & merge** in the row's **⋯** menu, to open the review. It opens in Projects' Code, with the branch's worktree selected. Above the review:

| Action | Does |
| --- | --- |
| **Merge into main** | Moves `main` forward to the branch, then removes the worktree and the branch. No merge commit is made. Refused while the worktree has uncommitted work or an agent is mid-turn there, or when the branch gained commits since the review was drawn |
| **Ask to rebase** | Replaces Merge when `main` moved. Pastes *Rebase this branch on main and run the tests again.* at the session's prompt, without sending it |
| **Keep** | Leaves the branch, and its tag becomes **Kept**; **Unkeep** undoes it. New commits make it wait again |
| **Discard** | Lists every commit that is on no other branch and will be lost, then removes the worktree and the branch |

After Merge or Discard, the next waiting branch opens, oldest first. The project's main branch is never merged or discarded here.

## Reviewing the whole branch

Click **Branch changes** on a branch, or the branch name in the Changes tab, to read the branch as one document: every changed file's lines in turn. The header counts files and lines added and removed. Changes are counted from where the branch left its base, and include uncommitted work.

- **The file list** on the left holds every changed file; click one to scroll to it.
- **Fold** a file by its arrow, or use **Fold all** and **Unfold all**. At most 2,000 changed lines open at first; later files start folded. A binary file or a very large one is listed with a note instead.
- **Viewed** folds a file and counts it (*3/12 viewed*). If the agent changes it again, it is unmarked.
- **Comment**: click a line number, write, and press **Add**. **Send to the session** pastes all your comments as one message at the prompt of the session in that folder, without sending it.
- **Revert hunk** undoes one change; **Revert file** puts the file back as the branch found it. A checkpoint is taken first. Both are refused while an agent works in that folder.

The review reads again when a session in that folder acts, or when you come back to the window.

## Source control

The **Changes** tab works like VS Code's Source Control, and Slate runs the git. It shows the worktree of the session you work in; with no session selected, each worktree with a session is one line you can open.

| Part | Does |
| --- | --- |
| The count | Files waiting to commit, on the tab's icon and the title |
| Message box | **Message (⌘↵ to commit)** |
| Main button | **Commit N files**, with **Commit & Push** in its menu. With everything committed: **Sync changes**, which pulls, then pushes. On a branch never pushed: **Publish branch**. With nothing to do: *Nothing to commit, and up to date.* |
| A file row | Its name and git letter (M, A, D, R). Click it to see the change. Pointing at it shows **Open file** and **Discard changes** |
| Folded below | **Outgoing**, **Incoming**, and **This branch vs main** |

A commit takes every file listed, except ones you untick. Files that can hold a secret, such as `.mcp.json` and `.claude/settings.json`, start unticked.

While an agent works in the worktree, every button that writes waits: *Claude Code is working here — waits for its turn to end*.

Sync never forces. If the branch and its upstream both moved, Sync shows git's message and changes nothing; merge or rebase in the terminal. Slate fetches by itself when you open Changes and the last fetch is over five minutes old.

---

# Files, memories and editing

Source: https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/sessions/files.md

A file opens as a tab beside the session, so you can read what the agent changed, tell it what to fix, or fix it yourself.

## Open a file

- Click a file in the side panel's **Changes** or **Turns**, or a path the agent printed (`src/x.ts:42` opens at that line).
- **⌘P** finds a file by name in every project and each of its worktrees, grouped by checkout and branch (`FILES · acme · main`). Ignored files such as `node_modules` are left out. **⌘⇧F** searches the text inside them ([Search](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/search.md)).

Code opens highlighted and numbered. Markdown opens rendered, with **Read** one click away. Images are drawn. When the file changes on disk, an **updated** pill says so.

Up to 1 MB of text or 8 MB of image opens. A larger file, a binary, or a file that is not UTF-8 text says why and offers **Open in Finder**.

## Reading a file

The bar at the bottom shows the branch, **worktree** when the file is in one, and the file's path.

| Control | Shows |
| --- | --- |
| Margin marks | The branch's changes: green added, blue changed, a red notch for removed lines. Click one to see the change |
| The cursor line | When the line last changed, and in which commit |
| **Blame** | Every line's commit down the left, older commits fainter |
| **Show changes** | The file against **Where the branch began** or **The last commit** (pick under **against**). **Back to the file** or **Esc** leaves |
| **Now** | The file over time: pick a commit to read the file as it was, read-only. **Back to now** or **Esc** returns |

**[** and **]** step through changes; **⌥H** opens the file's history.

**Comment for the agent.** In **Show changes**, put the cursor on a line or select several, click **Comment on line 88**, write, and press **Add** or ⌘Enter. **Send N to the session** pastes all comments as one message at the prompt of the session working in that folder, without sending it. With no session there, the message is copied instead.

## What agents know about the file

A dot in the margin marks each line a memory cites. Point at it to read the memory. The header counts them: *4 memories · 2 told to agents who touch it*, or *No memories yet*. The second number is the lessons and decisions Slate gives an agent that reads or edits this file ([Lessons](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/memory/recall-remember.md#lessons)). Click it, or a dot, to open the card.

Each memory on the card shows its claim, its lines, how often sessions used it, and a check: *Matches the code*, *The code changed since — still true?*, or *Not checked against the code*.

| Action | Does |
| --- | --- |
| **Confirm** | Counts it confirmed and checks it again against the code as it reads now |
| **Correct** | Edit the claim; the new words replace the memory and cite the same lines |
| **Retire** | Stops it reaching sessions |
| **Remember line 7** | Write what agents should know about the selected lines; saved as your own memory citing them |
| **Ask an agent about line 7** | Pastes the lines and their memories at the prompt of the session in that folder; add your question and press Enter |

Your other acts count too. **Merge into main** of a reviewed branch confirms the memories its sessions cited; **Revert hunk**, **Revert file** and **Discard** count against them. If you save an edit to cited lines, the card asks *You edited these lines: still true?*

## Editing

At **Now** the file is editable, as in VS Code: changed lines are amber in the margin, the bar counts unsaved lines with **Revert** and **Save** (⌘S). The editor uses VS Code's keys ([list](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/shortcuts.md#files-and-the-editor)).

The agent writes the same files, so:

- **Save waits while an agent works in that folder** (*Waiting for Claude Code*). Keep typing; it saves when the turn ends.
- **Every save can be undone.** Slate takes a checkpoint before it writes, and the *Saved* notice offers **Undo**, which puts the file back as it was before the save, unless you have typed since.
- **A change on disk under your unsaved lines is merged.** If it touches other lines, both are kept. If it touches the same lines, choose for each place: **Keep yours**, **Keep theirs** or **Keep both**. Nothing is written until you save.
- **The agent reads the disk, not your screen.** A line says when it cannot see your unsaved lines yet.

Files are saved as written: line endings, indentation and a byte-order mark are kept, and nothing is reformatted. Unsaved text survives closing the tab and quitting Slate. A past commit, **Show changes** and **Blame** are read-only.

---

# Status and flow

Source: https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/sessions/status.md

Every session has a **status**, which says whether it needs you, and a **flow**, which says which step of its work it is on. Slate reads both from the session's transcript and git. The agent reports nothing.

## Status

| Status | When |
| --- | --- |
| **Needs you** | The agent finished a turn and waits: on permission for a tool call, on an answer, or with a finished report. Home shows each as a card ([Home](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/home.md)) |
| **Working** | The agent wrote to its session in the last 45 seconds |
| **Idle** | Quiet, and you spoke last |

A session needs a running process to be live. A quiet transcript with no process is a closed conversation: it leaves the list and never shows as **Needs you**.

A session that only waits is **Idle**, however fresh its transcript: its newest step is a running `sleep`, a shell loop that sleeps until something is ready, or a scheduled wakeup. The wait must be the whole command: `sleep 30 && npm test` is work.

For a Claude Code tool call with no result yet, the session is **Working**, with three exceptions that read **Needs you**: a question to you, once 45 seconds have passed; any call quiet for more than 30 minutes, which is a prompt nobody answered; and, in a session Slate runs, a quiet call while its terminal shows nothing new.

### What Slate cannot see

- A permission prompt in a session Slate does not run reads as **Working** for Claude Code, for up to 30 minutes, and as **Idle** for other agents. The exception is a Claude Code session that Claude Code itself reports as waiting: that reads **Needs you** at once.
- "Waiting for permission" and "answered, waiting for your next prompt" both read **Needs you**.

## Flow

The flow shows on the row (a bar and a word, **Check**), above the terminal (**Working · Check**), and in Details under **Progress**.

A build has five steps: **Overview**, **Plan**, **Build**, **Check**, **Land**. Research has three: **Asked**, **Published**, **Decided**.

**The word is the step the session is on now; the bar is how far it has got.** A session that ran its tests and went back to editing reads **Build** again, while its bar stays filled through Check. When the latest step only waits, the word is **Waiting**.

The bar has one colour: done steps are solid, the current step is lighter, steps ahead are grey. Only three things change a segment's colour:

- **Red** on Check when the session stopped on a failed check. The word reads **Check failed**.
- **Amber** on the current step while the session waits on you.
- **Green** on every step once the work is on the default branch.

| Step | Lights when |
| --- | --- |
| **Overview** | The session started and is reading |
| **Plan** | A plan was approved or a to-do list written, or an approved brief opened the session |
| **Build** | A file in the session's own checkout was edited |
| **Check** | Tests or the project's checks ran |
| **Land** | The work is on the default branch, on origin or locally |
| **Asked**, **Published**, **Decided** | Research was asked; it published a doc or artifact; you replied after it published |

A skill names its steps in its `SKILL.md` frontmatter, such as `flow: overview plan edit check land`, where `edit` shows as Build. With no skill, only the steps that happened show.

**The goal** at the top of Progress is the first Slate finds: a brief the first prompt names, the issue in the branch name (`fix/<n>-…`) or the prompt (`#<n>`), the branch's plan doc in Slate, or else the first prompt, marked *as asked*.

---

# Home

Source: https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/home.md

**Home** is where Slate opens. It shows what needs you, one card at a time, so you answer the most urgent thing first. Under the cards is a box where you ask your own agent to find or do anything in the workspace ([Ask from Home](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/home/ask.md)).

## The cards

The headline counts the cards: *Three things need you.* When finished sessions are among them, the line under it splits the count: *Two to answer, one finished — look when you can.* Cards are ordered by kind, the ones that block you first. An amber dot means the card blocks on you now; grey means it can wait.

| Card | What it is | Buttons |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Needs permission** | An agent waits for your yes on a tool call. The card shows the command | **Open to allow**, **Later** |
| **Asks you** | A session's last turn ends on a question | A reply box with **Send** and **Open**, and **Later**. For a session in a terminal Slate does not own: **Open session** and **Later**, and you answer there |
| **Automation asks** | An automation's rules held a call ([Automations](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/automations.md)) | **Yes, do it**, **No** with an optional reason, **Open the thread**, **Later** |
| **Review asked** or **Task** | A task in Tasks needs you | **Open in Tasks**, **Open in** its app (such as GitHub), **Later** |
| **Reminder** | A reminder you set on a task is due | **Open in Tasks**, **Done**, **Later** |
| **Finished** | A session's turn ended with a report; nothing blocks | **Open session**, **Mark seen**, **Later** |

The card's title is the question the reply ends on, or its first sentence. A card that waits on you says how long: *waiting 2 min*, *waiting 3 hours*. A worker's card says **Worker of** the session that started it.

- **Send** answers the session and removes the card; you stay on Home. For an agent Slate cannot send to, the answer is typed but not sent: *Typed — press Enter in the session to send it.*
- **Later** sets a card aside until you restart Slate. A session set aside comes back when it says something new. **Mark seen** does the same for a finished session.
- Move between cards with the arrows, the dots, **←** and **→**, or a sideways swipe. The line under the dots says where you are: *4 of 7 · Automation asks*.

With nothing waiting, the headline says **All clear.**, the line under it says what is still running, and the box moves to the middle. If you set cards aside, **Bring them back** returns them.

If Home could not read everything that waits, it says so under the headline, with **Try again**, and never says **All clear.**

Sessions that are working and need nothing are not on Home: see [Sessions](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/sessions.md).

## Widgets on Home

Your [widgets](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/widgets.md) for Home sit between Home's parts, each at the size chosen for it in Widgets. They read what Home shows: today's sessions in every project of the workspace. To add or move one, open it in Widgets.

## Set up Slate

**In a workspace with no agent**, Home reads *\<workspace> is ready for an agent.* One card shows the 16 agents and what connecting one unlocks, with **Open Connect**. Beside it, what works now without AI: Tasks, Projects and Artifacts.

**Once an agent is set**, Home starts with a **Set up Slate** card of three steps:

| Step | Button | Done when |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Connect an agent** | **Connect an agent** | This workspace has an agent |
| **Start a session** | **New session** | A session has been recorded |
| **See your first memory** | **Open Memory** | A memory is saved |

A step done elsewhere ticks itself. The header counts progress (*1 of 3 done*). The card goes when all three are done, or on **Skip setup**, and does not come back in that workspace.

## More about Home

- [Ask from Home](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/home/ask.md): the box, a past session, files, skills and mentions.
- [Approvals, Stop and agent differences](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/home/approvals.md): how Home's agent asks before it acts.

---

# Ask from Home

Source: https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/home/ask.md

The box at the foot of Home asks your own agent anything about the workspace: find a doc, sum up a day, write a plan, change a file. It runs on the agent and account the workspace assigns, and reaches every project in the workspace, its docs, memory and activity, and the MCP servers your agent connects.

## Ask

Type in **Ask, find, or make anything…** and press **Enter**. The chat opens over Home, and the reply streams as it is written.

- **Home**, at the top left of the chat, goes back to the cards and keeps the chat. **Back to the chat** returns to it. Sending a message also returns to it; a streaming reply does not pull you back.
- **New chat** starts over.
- Before the agent edits a file or runs a command, it asks: [Approvals, Stop and agent differences](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/home/approvals.md).

There is no project to pick: the agent's searches, the memories Slate gives it and the widgets on Home cover every project in the open workspace. The workspace switcher picks the workspace.

## Resume a past session

1. Open [Sessions](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/sessions.md) and choose **All past sessions**.
2. Press **Resume** on a row. A click on the row opens its record instead.
3. Home opens with that session's conversation loaded, and the agent continues it.

The chat starts with what you first asked and, under **Summary**, what Slate saved of the session. **Start fresh instead** opens an empty chat.

## Attach a file

Drop a file on the box, paste it, or use **Attach files**. An image shows as a thumbnail, and the agent gets its path; an attached image unused for 30 days is removed. A text or code file is put into the message under its name, cut at 20,000 characters.

An image can be up to 8 MB and a text file up to 1 MB. A larger file, a binary such as a PDF or a zip, or a file that is not UTF-8 text is not attached, and a message names it.

The same works in a session's **Conversation** box.

## Skills and mentions

**/** at the start of the box lists the skills your agent loads here: the project's own skills, its commands, and your personal and plugin skills. Matches by name come first. A pick waits as a chip; on send, the agent is told to read that skill and follow it. After Claude Code has answered once, its own commands are listed too.

**@** anywhere names something in the workspace. The menu shows up to five of each kind whose name holds what you typed. A pick is a chip; on send, its content goes before your message:

| Kind | Sent |
| --- | --- |
| Doc | Its text, cut at 8,000 characters |
| Session | Its agent, folder, branch and id |
| Memory | The claim, why it was written, and its source |
| Task | Its state and link |
| Automation | Its steps |
| Report | Its text |

If Slate cannot read one, the message is sent without it and says so. **/** and **@** work in a session's **Conversation** box too.

---

# Approvals, Stop and agent differences

Source: https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/home/approvals.md

Home's agent runs on your own agent's CLI, and it asks before it edits a file or runs a command. Below: the approval card, how much to let it do alone, and Stop.

## The approval card

Before a call that changes something, the agent shows an amber card with the call and its whole argument, such as the full shell command:

| Answer | Effect |
| --- | --- |
| **Approve** | Runs this one call |
| **Always allow** | Runs it and stops asking for the same call. Claude Code saves the rule to the project, and the card shows the rule first. Codex stops asking for the rest of the session. Cursor and OpenCode keep it in their own allowlist |
| **Skip** | Refuses, and tells the agent why. A box beside it takes an optional reason |

- **Always allow** appears only when the agent offers a rule.
- Several calls queue and show one at a time.
- Slate's own tools, such as reading docs or saving a memory, skip the card. Everything else asks, MCP servers you connected included.
- An automation's run shows no card. A call its rules hold waits on Home as an **Automation asks** card.

## Autonomy

The autonomy pill sets what skips the card. The ⌘J panel and Home share it.

| Setting | The agent |
| --- | --- |
| **Ask first** | Asks before every file edit and command |
| **Auto-edit** | Edits files in the project; asks before a shell command |
| **Full auto** | Asks about nothing |

A click moves one step. **Full auto** needs a second click. **New chat** goes back to **Ask first**. A change applies to the chat you are in, with no restart. **Create an automation** and **Run an automation** always ask, whatever the pill says.

## A plan or a question

- **A plan**: the agent shows its whole plan before touching anything. **Approve** starts it; **Skip** keeps it planning.
- **A question**: each answer the agent offers is a button.

## Stop

**Stop** ends the turn and keeps the agent running with its connections, so your next message needs no new sign-in. Stop also declines every waiting card, and an interrupted step reads **Stopped.**

## What Home shows about the agent

- The reply streams as it is written.
