- **Context**: how full the agent's context window is, as a share and a bar, darker from 75%. With no known window size it shows tokens only.
- **The tools chip** in the top bar: *connecting MCP servers…* during the first turn, then how many MCP servers the agent connected, with their names on hover and *· 1 failed* in amber when one did not connect.
- A hook that blocks a turn is reported in the chat, with its name and reason.

## What differs by agent

| | Claude Code | Codex | Cursor, OpenCode |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Approval card | Yes | Yes | Yes |
| **Always allow** | Saves a project rule | For the session | Their own allowlist |
| A question with buttons | Yes | Yes | No |
| A plan to approve | Yes | No | No |
| Its own commands in **/** | Yes, after the first reply | No | No |

Codex also asks before it leaves its sandbox, and passes on questions from its own MCP servers.

Cursor and OpenCode follow the pill: **Ask first** shows a card for each call, **Auto-edit** allows edits, reads and searches, and **Full auto** allows everything.

**Gemini**: Slate cannot yet ask Gemini for permission, so its pill is off and Gemini runs pre-approved.

**GitHub Copilot** runs in Home, but its approval card is not yet tested. **The ten agents marked Beta** (Antigravity, Cline, Grok Build, Kiro, Qwen Code, Droid, Hermes Agent, Goose, Kilo Code, Auggie): Home, Stop and the approval card are not yet tested with them. Full table: [Features by agent](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/agents/features-by-agent.md).

---

# Tasks

Source: https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/tasks.md

**Tasks** lists what you owe: the issues assigned to you, the pull requests to review, the
messages to answer, and the lines you write yourself. Open any of them and run one of your
automations on it. Tasks belongs to the workspace picked on the rail.

## The four sections

| Section | Holds | From |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **To-dos** | Lines you wrote | Slate only ([To-dos, reminders and meetings](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/tasks/todos.md)) |
| **Issues** | Issues and tickets assigned to you, and unassigned issues on repositories you own | Jira, Linear, GitHub, GitLab, Azure DevOps, Asana, ClickUp, monday.com, Notion, Trello, Shortcut, YouTrack, Basecamp, Todoist, Plane |
| **Reviews** | Reviews asked of you, pull requests assigned to you, your open ones, and unclaimed ones on repositories you own | GitHub, GitLab, Bitbucket, Azure DevOps, Gitea, Gerrit |
| **Messages** | Chat and email waiting for your answer | Slack, Microsoft Teams, Discord, Google Chat, Zoom, Mattermost, Zulip, Rocket.Chat, Gmail, Outlook |

How each tool is read, and how to change what it sends, is in
[Where tasks come from](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/tasks/sources.md).

**Reviews** is grouped by the pull request's state: **To review** (asked of you or assigned
to you), then your own: **Changes asked**, **Checks failing**, **Ready to merge**,
**Checks running**, **Waiting on review**; and last **On repositories you own**, for
pull requests nobody took. **Issues** is grouped by each tool's own status names.

## The side panel

- **Overview**: its number is what needs you now: a review asked of you, a direct message,
  a reminder that rang.
- **To-dos**, **Issues**, **Reviews**, **Messages**, each with a count.
- The **+** in the title row adds a to-do.
- The sync line says when your tools were last read (**Synced 2 min ago**), or which tool
  needs sign-in (**Jira needs sign-in**). Click it to read your tools now.

A task with an agent run working on it shows a live dot and its step on its row, such as
**Reviewing** or **Building**. **Needs you** (amber) means it waits on you, **Stopped** that
it stopped.

Above a section's list, one chip per tool filters to that tool. The **⋯** beside the chips
offers **Manage in Connect**, and **Disconnect <app>** for an app connected from Slate or
**Hide from Tasks** for any other. A hidden app is listed in Connect → **Integrations**,
with **Show**. A tool Slate cannot reach keeps its last tasks, under **Cannot reach <tool>**.

Drag the line between the list and the open task to widen the list, from 320 to 640 px.
Double-click the line to reset it.

## The Overview

The Overview draws your work as one picture: your tools on the left, each with what waits
there and **Sign in** when it needs it, **You wrote** for your to-dos, and
**Connect an integration** last; then the four sections; then Slate, with how much needs
you. Click any of them to open its list. When your calendar is connected, today's meetings
sit above it ([Today's meetings](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/tasks/todos.md#todays-meetings)). Click a tool to choose what it sends
([Choose what Tasks shows](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/tasks/choose.md)).

On a first day, with nothing connected, the Overview shows the most used integrations and
**See all N integrations in Connect →**. A tool your agents already reach is offered as
**Use from your agents**.

## A task

Click a row to open it beside the list. It shows where it came from ("GitHub assigned this
to you"), its comments and project, and:

- **Slate remembers**: up to three memories about the task, first those that name its key
  (`PROJ-123`) or pull request number, then those about the same topic in its project.
- **Run <automation>**: runs one of your automations on it ([Run an automation](#run-an-automation-on-a-task)).
- **⋯**: **Open in <tool>**, **Remind me…**, **Change what <tool> sends**,
  **Stop showing these**, and **Hide from Tasks**.

**Hide from Tasks** takes the task off this list only; nothing changes in its tool. It
comes back if the tool reports a newer change. Each section has a **Hidden (N)** line with
**Unhide**.

The description and comments stay in the tool: open the task there to read them.

## Run an automation on a task

Tasks runs your [automations](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/automations.md); the automation holds the process.
The **Run <automation>** button names the automation, such as **Run Fix a bug**. Its
chevron lists the automations that take this kind of item, yours first, then Slate's
starters, and the agent to use for this run. The first run of a starter adds it to
Automations.

The run happens in a session you can see, and stops for your approval before it plans and
before it ships. See [Agent runs](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/tasks/agent-runs.md) and
[Which automation runs](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/tasks/workflow.md).

When your pull request still waits for a review or for checks, one line says there is
nothing to run yet.

## More

- [To-dos, reminders and meetings](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/tasks/todos.md)
- [Where tasks come from](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/tasks/sources.md) and [Choose what Tasks shows](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/tasks/choose.md)
- [How Slate learns an app](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/tasks/learning.md)
- [Agent runs](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/tasks/agent-runs.md) and [Agent run rules](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/tasks/agent-run-rules.md)
- [Receipts](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/tasks/receipts.md)

---

# To-dos, reminders and meetings

Source: https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/tasks/todos.md

**To-dos** are the lines you write yourself in Tasks, such as "call the accountant". A
reminder brings a to-do, or any task, back to you at the time you pick. Today's meetings
sit above the Overview.

## Add a to-do

1. Click **+** in the Tasks panel's title row.
2. Type the line and press Enter. The box stays open for the next line; Esc closes it.
3. To set a reminder first, use **Remind me** beside the box.

A to-do never syncs and never leaves on its own. No tool writes to **To-dos**, and nothing
you write lands in **Issues**, **Reviews** or **Messages**. On the Overview, your to-dos
come from **You wrote**.

Your agents can read your list and add or change your own lines with Slate's `my_tasks`
and `update_my_task` tools ([MCP tool reference](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/mcp-server/tools.md)).

## Work through them

To-dos are grouped by when they are due: **Overdue**, **Today**, **Tomorrow**,
**This week**, **Later** and **No time**. **Done today** sits at the bottom, struck through,
until the next day.

- **Tick the box** to finish a to-do. Tick it again to undo.
- **Double-click the title** to rename it.
- **Run <automation>** runs one of your automations on it. A to-do is a question, so
  **Research** fits it ([Which automation runs](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/tasks/workflow.md)).

## Reminders

**Remind me…** sits on a to-do, and in the **⋯** menu of any task. Pick **In an hour**,
**This evening**, **Tomorrow morning**, **Next week**, or **Pick a time…**.

When it is due, a notification shows the title, and the task moves to **Needs you** until
it is done. Set a new time to snooze it. **Clear the reminder** removes it.

- Slate must be running. A reminder that came due while Slate was closed rings once when
  you open it, and says when it was due.
- A reminder that came due while the computer slept rings within 5 minutes of waking.
- **Reminders** in Automations › **Built-in** turns them all off. The times you set stay.

For a reminder that repeats, make an [automation](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/automations.md).

## Today's meetings

When a connected work gateway carries your calendar (Google Calendar or Outlook), a
**Today's meetings** row sits above the Overview:

- the next meeting: **in 25 min**, or **now**, its name, and **Join** when it has a video
  link;
- a line for the day with a mark per meeting, dashed when you have not answered;
- the sums: meetings, all-day events, and free time left in gaps of 45 minutes or more.

Point at a meeting for its card, with **Join** and **Open in <calendar>**. A meeting whose
title names a task key or a pull request lists that task under **About**. Declined and
cancelled meetings are left out. With no calendar there is no row.

---

# Where tasks come from

Source: https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/tasks/sources.md

Tasks reads each of your tools directly. A sync runs no model and spends no tokens, and
Slate only reads: it never writes to a tool while syncing.

## How each tool is read

| Tools | How Slate reads them | Connect it |
| --- | --- | --- |
| GitHub | The GitHub CLI, `gh`, as each account you signed in with | **Connect** on GitHub's card in Connect → **Integrations**. Signed out: run `gh auth login` |
| GitLab, Jira, Linear, ClickUp, monday.com, Notion, Trello, Plane, Mattermost, Shortcut, Basecamp, Todoist | The app's official server, signed in as Slate | **Sign in** in Connect → **Integrations** |
| Jira, Slack and Gmail through your agents | The MCP servers your agents already use | **Use from your agents** |
| Bitbucket Cloud, Gitea, Forgejo, Gerrit, YouTrack, Zulip, Rocket.Chat | Their web API, with a token you paste | Connect → **Integrations** |
| Any other tracker | A read Slate learned ([How Slate learns an app](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/tasks/learning.md)) | Connect it, then teach it |

**Sign in** opens the tool's sign-in page in your browser. Tasks shows
**Waiting for you to sign in to <tool> in your browser**, checks every 4 seconds, then says
**Signed in to <tool>.** After three minutes with no answer it asks you to try again.

**GitHub.** With several `gh` accounts, each workspace reads as the account that owns its
git repositories. GitHub is read when you open Tasks, and again when you come back to the
window after a minute. A workspace whose projects have no GitHub git repository shows no
GitHub row.

**Through your agents.** Slate looks in the settings of Claude Code, Cursor, Gemini,
Codex and OpenCode, only for the accounts this workspace runs under. It signs in to a web
server as itself and never reads your agent's own sign-in. Only read-only tools are called.

## Choose what Tasks shows

What each tool sends to Tasks, and from where, is yours to change
([Choose what Tasks shows](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/tasks/choose.md)).

## When a tool holds more

Slate reads up to 1,000 items from one tool. When a tool holds more, the list says so above
the rows, such as **1,000 of 3,400 from GitHub. Narrow by project or label, or open the
full list in GitHub.**, with **Open the full list in GitHub**.

A group shows its first 100 rows, then **Show 100 more of N**. A group with items from more
than one tool or project is split under a heading for each, such as
**GitHub · acme/api**. Click a heading to fold it.

## When a tool is down, or goes away

An outage or a rate limit never removes tasks. The tool's row says **Unavailable** or
**Cannot reach <tool>**, and its last tasks stay until the next good read.

When a tool really goes away (you disconnect it, or switch `gh` accounts), its tasks leave
the list. A task you hid or set a reminder on comes back with the same choice if the tool
returns. Reconnecting a tool starts no automation for the tasks it brings back.

## Messages stay in this workspace

A message is shown only when it names something this workspace works on: a group or
project in your tree, or a project key, name or git remote from your **Issues** and
**Reviews**. A Slack message also stays when it comes from someone in those tasks. A
workspace with no groups, projects, issues or reviews shows every message.

| Tool | What it reads |
| --- | --- |
| Slack | Direct messages and mentions from the last 7 days that you have not answered |
| Gmail | Unread mail from the last 7 days, up to 30 |
| Zulip | Unread direct messages and mentions, one row per conversation |
| Rocket.Chat | Rooms with unread direct messages or mentions, one row per room |

---

# Choose what Tasks shows

Source: https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/tasks/choose.md

Each tool sends Tasks a few lists, such as the reviews asked of you or the issues assigned
to you. Slate picks sensible ones at first. This panel shows what a tool sends and lets you
change where it looks and what it brings.

## Open the panel

Click a tool on the Overview to open **From <tool>**, such as **From GitHub**. In Connect,
point at a working app and use **Choose what Tasks shows**. The first line says what the
tool sends, such as **Sends 11 issues and 2 reviews to Tasks.**

## 1. Where

One tick per git repository, project, channel or kind of mail:

| Kind | Step 1 lists | Slate ticks at first |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Code**: GitHub, GitLab, Bitbucket, Gitea, Forgejo, Gerrit | **Git repositories** | The ones this workspace works in |
| **Tracker**: Jira, Linear, ClickUp, monday.com, Notion and the others | **Projects** | The ones your current tasks come from |
| **Mail**: Gmail | **Which mail**: **From people** you work with, each label, and **Anything else that names a project** | The first and the last |
| **Chat**: Slack, Zulip, Rocket.Chat, Mattermost | **Channels** | The ones your current messages come from |

Until you change a tick, Slate works its choice out at each sync, so a new git repository
or project still comes in. Untick them all and the tool sends nothing.

## 2. What to bring

One tick per list Slate reads from the tool, with its count, such as
**Reviews asked of you** or **Issues assigned to you**. Below them are the lists you can
add, each a sentence with a word to fill in, such as **Issues in <project> labelled
<label>**. Tick it and fill the word to add it. You can add up to 5 per tool. **Remove**
takes away one you added; Slate's own are turned off, never removed. A list that failed
says **Did not answer: <reason>** and keeps its last tasks.

## Other ways

For GitHub, Jira and Gmail: type your own search, see how many items are open and how
many are already in Tasks, then **Add to Tasks**.

The footer says **As <login> · checked <time> · read only**. A change starts a sync at
once.

Until you open a tool's panel, a line under the Overview says
**Slate chose what Tasks takes from <tools>. Click a logo to change it.** **Hide** dismisses
it.

---

# How Slate learns an app

Source: https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/tasks/learning.md

Slate can read your tasks from a tracker it was not built for, as long as the app offers
read-only tools. It learns the read once, then reads the app like any other: no model, no
tokens.

## On its own

During a sync, a connected tracker that Slate cannot read yet gets one try a day, with no
model:

1. Slate picks the app's read-only tools whose names say tasks, issues, items, tickets,
   cards or stories, and that return yours or take an assignee.
2. It finds your id in the app, through the app's own "who am I" tool where it has one.
3. It calls the best of them, at most 6 calls, and keeps the first that returns a list of
   tasks with a title and a status.

Finished items are left out, in English and in your team's language (Done, Erledigt,
Terminé, 完了). A status Slate cannot read stays open.

An app that has nothing of yours yet is tried again the next day. Connecting or
disconnecting an app, or a sync you start, tries again at once.

## Teach it

An app in Connect → **Integrations** that Slate cannot read shows **Not read yet** and
**Slate hasn't found your tasks in it yet.** Click its tile to teach Slate. It reads
**Learning how to read your tasks in <app>…** while your agent looks at that app through
Slate's tools, with no shell and no web. This takes a few minutes, and apps go one at a
time.

Slate tries what the agent found and keeps it only if it returns a list. After that, no
agent and no tokens are used. When nothing is found, the tile says
**Could not find your tasks in <app>.** Slate never retries on its own; teach it again when
you want.

## Only read-only calls

Every tool is checked when it is picked, when it is kept, and on every read. A tool is
refused when its name holds a write word (send, create, update, remove, add, move, post,
reply, comment, merge, close, assign, set, mark, upload, write and about fifty more) or
when it belongs to another app. A filter word passes: `get_assigned_issues` is read,
`assign_issue` is not.

## What Tasks keeps

- **Each task**: one line with its tool, key (`acme/api#412`), title, state, person, link,
  a few counts, its type (Bug, Story) and its reminder. Never a description, a comment or a
  message's text. Tasks are kept in the workspace on this computer and never shared, even
  in a shared workspace.
- **Calendar meetings**: never saved. They stay in memory until the day ends or Slate
  quits.
- **Each learned app**: the tool, its arguments, your id in that app, and where each field
  sits in the answer. Never the answer.

Sign-ins are kept in private files on this computer that only your user can read. A token
you paste is never logged and is sent only to its own server. **Disconnect** removes it.

---

# Agent runs

Source: https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/tasks/agent-runs.md

An agent run carries one task through an automation's steps (read, plan, build, check,
ship) in a session you can see, with your approval before it plans and before anything
leaves your computer. Only your click starts one. **Agent runs** in Automations ›
**Built-in** turns them on and off.

## Start a run

Open a task and press **Run <automation>**. It says **Starting…**, then **Running**. The
run starts at once when nothing needs you: the project is certain, an agent is set, and
the project's folder is a git repository.

The chevron beside the button picks the automation and **Runs with**, the agent for this
run only. **Default** marks the agent used when you pick none. **Edit in Automations**
opens the automation, where its steps and stops are changed.

When your agent last reported that the task's tracker needs signing in, one line under the
button says so, such as **Jira needs sign-in**, with **Sign in to Jira in Claude Code**. It
never blocks the run: without it, the run hands you the ticket update to copy.

## The start dialog

It opens only when something needs you, and shows only that:

- **An unknown project.** Slate picks the project only when it is certain: the item's own
  git repository, the project a to-do names, the project you said the item's source works
  in, or your only project. Otherwise it asks once, such as
  **Which project does Jira PROJ work in?**, and remembers the answer. The project's
  **Settings…** lists these under **Work from**; remove one and the dialog asks again.
- **A block**, with its fix: **Connect an agent for this project**, or
  **This folder is not a git repository**. **Run it** stays grey until it is fixed.

## What the run does

1. It makes a branch named after the task, such as `fix/proj-12-short-title`, in a folder
   of its own, and runs the project's **Set up** command there.
2. It starts your agent there, with the task's card
   ([A session started from a task](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/memory/session-start-brief.md#a-session-started-from-a-task)).
3. Each step the agent reports shows in the task's timeline. While it works, the last entry
   says so with a live dot, such as **Claude Code is reviewing…**. You never need the
   terminal; **Open session** shows it.

After each step the run waits for **Next**.

## Approvals

- **After the plan**: **Approve plan** or **Send back** with a note. **Save as Plan doc**
  keeps the plan as the project's Plan doc for the branch.
- **Before anything leaves your computer**: **Approve to ship** shows the commits, the
  changed files, and the exact pull request, ticket update, review or reply, each with
  **Copy**. For a review you choose **Post comments**, **Request changes** or **Approve**.
- Approving lets exactly what you approved through, once. Merging and closing are always
  refused ([Agent run rules](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/tasks/agent-run-rules.md)).
- After shipping, Slate reads the pull request back and says whether it
  **Matches what you approved**.

A run waiting on you counts in **Needs you**.

## Autopilot

Autopilot runs the steps back to back without **Next**. It still stops at both approvals,
at a held call, and after a long chain of steps. A failed check goes back to building up
to 2 times, then stops.

It is off until you turn on **Autopilot** in the project's **Settings…**. Then a switch
under the run's last entry moves between **Step by step** and **Autopilot**. Gemini
runs step by step only.

## Finish a run

After shipping, the run waits for the merge. Slate checks the pull request every 2 minutes
with `gh` or `glab`. A merge, or the task being done, ends the run.

- **Mark done** finishes it by hand.
- A pull request closed without a merge stops the run: **Mark done** or
  **Watch for the merge again**.
- A reply or review you posted yourself: **I sent it myself**.

A finished run keeps its [receipt](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/tasks/receipts.md) in the task's timeline, keeps a lesson if
the agent reported one, and removes its folder. Its branch goes too, unless it holds work
that is nowhere else. Every run of the last 14 days is listed in
[Automations](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/automations.md).

## Stop, resume, discard

- **Stop**, the square on the run's live line, ends its session and keeps its folder and
  branch. The run says **Stopped by you**, with **Resume** and **Discard**. **Resume**
  continues the conversation in a new session.
- Typing in the run's session pauses it until **Resume**.
- **Reopen session** reopens an ended session in the run's folder.
- An agent that ends its turn without reporting its step stops the run: the task shows
  **Stopped**, the agent's last line and **Retry**. A session that never starts stops the
  run after 5 minutes.
- **Discard** asks first: **Removes the run's folder. A branch with work stays.**
  **Discard** or **Keep**. When the session cannot be stopped, **Discard anyway** keeps the
  folder.

---

# Agent run rules

Source: https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/tasks/agent-run-rules.md

An agent run keeps your agent's normal reach (shell, web, MCP servers) inside the
**agent run rules**. They make sure nothing leaves your computer before you approve it,
and that a run never merges or closes anything.

## The built-in rules

| Area | Rule |
| --- | --- |
| **Git** | Git stays on the run's branch, and nothing is pushed before you approve shipping. Force pushes, tags and removing branches are always refused |
| **MCP** | MCP tools that write somewhere else ask first; reading is allowed |
| **Shell** | Shell commands that send data out, publish or deploy ask first |
| **Files** | Files are written only inside the run's folder, and nothing changes while it plans |

**Writes to the code host, a tracker or a chat** (a pull request, a review, a comment, a
push, a ticket update, a message):

- Before **Approve to ship**, every write asks.
- After it, the writes you approved for the run's own item pass once. A review passes only
  with the verdict you chose.
- Anything else, such as another pull request or another project, still asks.
- Merging, closing and removing are always refused: `gh pr merge`, `gh pr close`,
  `gh issue close`, `glab mr merge`, `glab mr close`, and the same calls through the API.
- Autopilot changes none of this.

## A held call

A call a rule asks about is held, and the run shows it under
**Agent run rules held a call:**. Answer with **Allow for this step**,
**Always allow in this project** or **Deny**. An allowance names that one call: one MCP
tool, or one exact command.

## Your own rules

Open the project's **Settings…** and find **Rules** under **Done means**. It lists the
built-in rules and your own. Add **Allow**, **Ask first** or **Deny** for a call:

- an MCP tool: `mcp__jira__add_comment`, or `mcp__jira__*` for all of them;
- a command: `shell:npm publish`;
- a path: `file:` and the path.

**Allow** covers one exact call. **Ask first** and **Deny** also cover a command's first
words and everything under a folder. **Deny** always wins.

## What the rules cannot see

The rules are a guard, not a sandbox. They read the text of each call, including calls
wrapped in `env`, `$( )`, `sh -c` and heredocs. They cannot see what a program does after it
starts. So they do not stop:

- **scripts in the run's folder**, such as `npm run`, `make` or a script the run writes and
  then runs;
- **plugins and modules** a command loads from the project's packages;
- **what is inside** a `.tar` or `.zip` file or a patch;
- **reading your secrets**: reading is not guarded, so `cat ~/.ssh/id_rsa` is allowed;
- **git changes inside the run's folder** that can lose unpushed work, such as
  `git reset --hard`;
- **paths built while a program runs**, in most forms;
- **a `GH_REPO` or `GH_HOST`** set before the session started.

Two locks hold even when the text is misread. A git hook in the run's folder holds every
push before you approve shipping, and every push to another branch after. After shipping,
Slate reads the pull request back and says whether it matches what you approved.

To close one of these gaps for a project, add a **Deny** rule, such as
`shell:git reset --hard`.

---

# Which automation runs

Source: https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/tasks/workflow.md

A run on a task is a run of one of your [automations](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/automations.md). The
automation holds the process; Tasks only picks the automation and the item.

## Which automation fits

Each automation takes one kind of input, and each task is one kind of input. The
**Run <automation>** menu lists the automations that take this item: yours first, then
each of Slate's starters below that none of yours came from.

| The task is | Starter | Its steps |
| --- | --- | --- |
| An issue (a bug) | **Fix a bug** | Reproduce, find the cause, a failing test and the fix, a pull request |
| A ticket | **Implement** | Plan, build in small steps, test, a pull request |
| A pull request asked of you | **Code Review** | Read it, check the rules, run the checks, write the review |
| Your own pull request | **Answer review** | Read each comment and failing check, change the code or reply, run the checks, push |
| A question, or an issue to look into | **Research** | Look it up, write the finding, change no file |
| A message | **Draft a reply** | Look it up, draft, send only when you approve |

The first run of a starter adds it to Automations, where it stays. You can change a
starter or make your own ([Automations](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/automations.md)).

Your own pull request that waits for reviewers or checks has nothing to run yet. A run
never merges.

## How each kind runs

| Kind | What is different |
| --- | --- |
| **Code Review** | The pull request's head is fetched into a folder of its own. It never pushes. You approve the comments as **Post comments**, **Request changes** or **Approve**, and the run posts exactly that |
| **Answer review** | Your branch is fetched into a folder of its own, and it is the only branch the run may push. A pull request from someone else's copy of the project is refused |
| **Research** | Reports the cause and the options. Changes no file |
| **Draft a reply** | Reads the project you pick, then drafts. Slate sends it when it can, or hands it to you |

**The check.** A run checks its work with the project's **Check** command, set in its
**Settings…**. With none, it uses one found in the project's files (`package.json` scripts,
`Makefile` targets, `pyproject.toml`, `Cargo.toml`, `go.mod`), or else the agent finds the
tests.

## A project skill can replace the steps

When your project keeps a skill for the same work, the automation can follow it instead of
its plain steps. Pick it in the automation, under **Do**. Slate suggests one by its name,
best first:

| Work | Names Slate looks for |
| --- | --- |
| Fix a bug | `fix-bug`, `bugfix`, `fix`, `hotfix`, `debug` |
| Implement | `dev-flow`, `development`, `feature`, `implement` |
| Code Review | `code-review`, `review`, `pr-review`, `review-pr`, `review-architecture` |
| Answer review | `address-review`, `address-comments`, `pr-feedback`, `fix-pr`, `respond` |

Skills are read from every skill folder your agents read, such as `.claude/skills` and
`.agents/skills`, in sub-packages too. A folder with no `SKILL.md`
is not a skill. If the skill leaves the project, the automation says so and the plain steps
run until you pick another.

**The approvals stay.** A skill runs inside Slate's steps: each step opens the skill and
follows it for that step only. The plan still waits for your approval, and nothing ships
before it. A run keeps the skill it started with; a change to the automation applies to the
next run.

---

# Receipts

Source: https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/tasks/receipts.md

A receipt shows what an agent session really ran, checked against what it said, so you can
trust a "the tests pass" without reading the transcript. Slate writes one from the
session's transcript when a turn ends, in any captured agent, with no model and nothing
leaving this computer. A session that only talked (no check, no changed file, no commit)
gets none.

You find a receipt on a finished agent run's task, as **Receipt**, and on a session in
[Sessions](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/sessions.md).

## What it shows

- **It said**: the first paragraph of the last reply.
- **Checked against the transcript**: where what it said and what it ran disagree, with the
  evidence. Otherwise: **What it said matches what it ran.**
- **What it ran**: every test, gate, lint, typecheck and build, in order, with the passed
  and failed counts or the exit code.
- **What changed**: the files it edited.
- **Outcome**: the commits it made, and whether they are **On the default branch**, were
  **Reverted on the default branch** within 30 days, or are
  **Not on the default branch yet**.

Checks are found in `package.json` scripts, `make` and `just` targets, and the pre-push
hook, which always counts as a gate. Cursor records commands but not their results, so its
runs show **not recorded**.

## Flags

| Badge | Flag |
| --- | --- |
| **Flagged** (red) | **A test failed, then passed on a re-run with no change in between** |
| **Flagged** (red) | **The last run failed, and nothing passed after it** |
| **Flagged** (red) | **It said the checks pass, but no test or gate run passed** |
| **Worth a look** (amber) | **A run ended without a result**: it was stopped before saying how it went |
| **Worth a look** (amber) | **It edited a file outside the project**. Temporary folders and the agents' own folders do not count |
| **Worth a look** (amber) | **A test's expected value was changed** |

A receipt with no flag shows **Matches**.

## Actions

- **Mark reviewed** clears it from the count. New runs, edits or commits in that session
  ask again.
- **Open session** opens the session's tab.
- **Copy as Markdown** copies the whole receipt, for a pull request.
- **Share as artifact** publishes the same text as an [artifact](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/artifacts.md).

## What is stored

One receipt per session that ran a check, changed a file or made a commit, in the workspace
that holds the project's folder: the session, its title and branch, the first paragraph of
the last reply, each run's command and result, the edited paths, the flags, the commits,
and when you marked it reviewed. Never a run's output beyond its counts, and never the text
of an edit. It stays on this computer and is never shared.

---

# Projects

Source: https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/projects.md

**Projects** is where the work of each project lives: the plans, designs, reviews, bugs and
notes written in it, and its code. A project is one folder you open, usually a
git repository. A group is a set of projects you name.

## Docs and Code

The side panel has two tabs:

- **Docs** lists each project's docs in a tree, by type ([The doc tree](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/projects/tree.md)).
- **Code** lists each project's files and the changes waiting to be committed
  ([Files and changes](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/projects/code.md)).

Every launch starts on **Docs**. The choice lasts while the app is open.

With nothing open, Projects opens something for you: the doc you read last in the
picked project, or its README the first time ([Nothing open](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/projects/tree.md#nothing-open)).

## Narrow to one project

The **project picker** under the panel's tabs narrows the list to one project. It reads
**All projects** at rest. A picked project shows its name with **×** to go back. The
choice lasts while the app is open, and every launch starts on **All projects**.

## Make a project

- The **+** in the panel's title row: **New project…**. Choose a folder; the name comes
  from it.
- The workspace mark at the top of the rail: **New project…** and **Manage projects…**.
  **Manage projects…** lists the workspace's projects by group, with **Rename**,
  **Show in Projects** and **Move to Trash**.
- **Import**, the down arrow beside the **+**: on its **Code** tab, the folders your
  editors opened lately (VS Code, Cursor, Windsurf, JetBrains IDEs); on its **Docs** tab,
  docs you keep in other apps. Slate shows what it found before it adds anything
  ([Import](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/connect/import.md)).

To put two or more projects in a group, shift-click them and choose **Group…** on the
⋯ menu ([Order, move and group](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/projects/tree.md#order-move-and-group)).

## A project's menu

A group or a project is a folder in the list. Clicking its row opens or closes it; only a
doc opens in the main area. Its **⋯** menu (or a right-click) offers:

| Item | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| **Start session** | Starts a session in the project. In a git project it starts in a new worktree ([Worktrees](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/sessions/worktrees.md)) |
| **Open a Terminal here** | Opens a terminal in its folder |
| **Show code** | Switches the panel to **Code** with this project's files open |
| **Link a folder** / **Change folder** | Sets the folder on this computer |
| **Settings…** | A group's, or a project's that is in no group ([Group and project settings](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/projects/settings.md)) |

A project in a group uses its group's settings.

## Favorites

**Add to Favorites** on a doc's menu puts it in **Favorites** at the top of the Docs list.
**Remove from Favorites** takes it off.

## What a workspace holds

A doc stays in the workspace it was made in. No doc, project or memory moves between
workspaces. Which workspace holds a doc decides whether it is shared
([Working in a shared workspace](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/workspaces/sharing.md)).

A project's sessions are in [Sessions](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/sessions.md), its memories in
[Memory](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/memory.md).

## More

- [The doc tree](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/projects/tree.md): what the Docs list shows, adding, moving and grouping.
- [Write a doc](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/projects/editor.md): the editor, images, diagrams and saving.
- [Doc types](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/projects/typed-docs.md): Plan, Design, Review, Bug and Note.
- [Files and changes](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/projects/code.md): the Code tab.
- [Group and project settings](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/projects/settings.md): agents, worktree commands, checks and memory.

# Write a doc

Source: https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/projects/editor.md

A doc is a piece of writing you and your agents keep: a plan, a design, a review, a bug or a
note. The editor is kept quiet. It offers the few blocks docs are written with, and the
keyboard does the rest. It has no AI of its own: ask your agent in a session to write or
change a doc.

## An open doc

An open doc shows its title once, then its body. Under the title is one line: what the doc
links to (a branch, a pull request, a ticket), the line its type keeps
([Doc types](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/projects/typed-docs.md#the-line-under-the-title)), and **Shared · <workspace>** in a
shared workspace.

An empty doc shows **Write here, or ask your agent to fill it.** That line is never stored.

## Blocks

Type **/** for the menu of 14 blocks: Text, Heading 1–3, Bullet, Numbered and Check list,
Quote, Code, Table, Image, **Callout**, **Check item** and **Link to doc**.

- **Selected text** gets four controls: Bold, Italic, Code and Link.
- **Tab** and **Shift-Tab** nest and unnest a block.
- **⌘⇧↑** and **⌘⇧↓** move a block. Select one and press Backspace to remove it.
- Markdown shortcuts work: `#`, `-`, `[]` and ```` ``` ```` turn a line into its block.
- Pasted Markdown becomes real blocks.
- **@**, or **Link to doc** in the **/** menu, links another doc. Type to filter; recent docs
  come first.
- A **Callout** is a plain note. Only the ⚠️ emoji draws it in the warning colour. Click
  the emoji to change it.

A doc that already holds an older block (a heading 4–6, a toggle, a divider, a video,
audio or file block) still opens and draws it. The menu no longer offers them.

## Check items

A **check item** is one line of a review or a test that carries a result: open (grey
circle), pass (green tick), fail (red cross) or blocked (amber sign). Click the mark to
step to the next result. Put a test's steps, expected result and evidence under the item
with **Tab**. In a doc you cannot edit, the mark only shows.

In Markdown a check item is a list line with its result in the box: `- [pass] Sign in`,
or `[fail]`, `[blocked]`, `[open]`. `- [ ]` and `- [x]` stay ordinary to-dos.

## Images

Paste or drop an image, or pick **Image** in the **/** menu. PNG, JPEG, GIF, WebP, AVIF
and BMP are kept, up to 8 MB. Any other file is refused with the reason. Slate saves each
image once, in the workspace's own folder on this computer; the same image placed twice
is one file. In a shared workspace, images travel with the docs that use them
([Working in a shared workspace](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/workspaces/sharing.md#images)).

## Figma links

A line that holds only a link to a Figma file draws as a card: Figma's mark, the file's
name and **Open in Figma**, which opens your browser. When the next block is an image,
such as a snapshot exported from Figma, it draws inside the card. Slate never calls
Figma, so the card works offline.

## Diagrams

A code block in the `mermaid` language draws as a diagram: a flowchart, a sequence, a
state chart and the other kinds [Mermaid](https://mermaid.js.org) knows. Type
```` ```mermaid ```` and a space to start one. The code button at its top right shows the
source to edit, and the drawing follows once you stop typing. A source Mermaid cannot read
stays as text under one line: **This diagram did not draw. Its source is below.**

## Right-to-left text

A doc in Hebrew, Arabic or another right-to-left script lays out right to left. The
direction is read from the text; there is nothing to set.

## Saving

Typing saves within half a second.

- **Not saved** replaces **Edited …** in the header when a save does not reach Slate.
  Slate tries again on your next edit, every 5 seconds, and at once when Slate answers
  again. Unsaved edits live only in the open window, so they do not survive quitting.
- **Slate isn't responding** shows in a red strip while Slate's server is down. After a
  minute it reads **Still trying. Restart Slate if this stays.**
- **Changed elsewhere.** When an agent writes to the doc you are typing in, your text is
  kept and a notice offers **Copy my text**, **Keep my version** (asks once, then
  overwrites the newer copy) and **Reload doc**. A retry never overwrites a newer copy.

When an agent changes a doc you are only reading, the screen updates within seconds.

---

# The doc tree

Source: https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/projects/tree.md

The **Docs** tab lists your groups and projects, and inside each project its docs, one
folder per type. Use it to find a doc, add one where it belongs, or reorganise projects.

## Nothing open

Projects never opens on an empty screen. With nothing open, it opens, for the picked
project (on **All projects**, the first project in the tree):

1. the doc you read last there; on **Code**, the file you opened last;
2. the first time, the project's doc titled README, or else its newest doc; on **Code**,
   the `README.md` at the root of its folder;
3. when there is nothing to open, one action: **New doc** for a project with no docs,
   **New project…** for a workspace with none, **Link a folder** on **Code** for a project
   with no folder on this computer.

A link that names a project, such as a breadcrumb, opens that project's README rather than
the doc read last.

## A project's docs

An open project shows one folder per doc type it holds, with a count, in this order:
**Plans**, **Designs**, **Reviews**, **Bugs**, **Notes**. A folder appears once it holds a
doc.

- Inside a folder, the 10 newest docs, then **Show N older**.
- One project is open at a time. Opening a project closes the one that was open. Folders
  inside it stay as you left them.
- The doc on screen is always shown in the tree, however you opened it: its folders open
  and its row is marked. A folder you close afterwards stays closed.
- Hover a doc to see the branch it was written on. Every doc written in the project is
  there, whichever branch, even after the branch is gone.
- Notes an agent wrote are not rows. A **Notes** row with a count lists them in the main
  area, newest first, with a filter.
- Captured sessions are in [Sessions](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/sessions.md), and decisions are in
  [Memory](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/memory.md). Neither is a row here.
- Two projects with the same name show the end of each folder path, and a hint:
  **Another project has this name**.
- A project that holds docs from an older version of Slate may show one more folder
  for its oldest kind of doc. No new ones are made.

The breadcrumb above an open doc says where it sits, such as
`Group / Project / Plans / Title`. It is text, not links.

## Add a doc

A doc is always made inside a project, and its type is fixed once made
([Doc types](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/projects/typed-docs.md)).

- The **+** on a project's row lists Plan, Design, Review, Bug and Note.
- The **+** on a type folder, on hover, makes an empty doc of that type. **Notes** has
  none.
- **⌘N** makes a note in the picked project. On **All projects** it makes nothing and
  says: **A doc lives in a project. Pick one at the top of Projects first.**
- **⌘K** offers **New doc**, a command for each type, and **Generate a doc** (⌘⇧G), where
  an agent drafts from your description.

A doc row has no **+**: a doc is never made inside another doc.

## Order, move and group

- **Reorder**: drag a row. Docs keep your order.
- **Move**: drag onto a new place, or **Move to project…** on a doc's ⋯ menu
  (**Move to…** on a group's or project's). A doc goes only into another project. A
  project goes into a group or to the top. A group stays at the top. A drop anywhere else
  shows no target.
- **Group**: shift-click two or more projects that are in no group, choose **Group…** on
  the ⋯ menu, and name it. They move into the new group.
- Nothing moves to another workspace. To work on a project in a shared workspace, open its
  folder there.

**Move to Trash** on a doc's menu closes its tab and says so, with **Undo**. Restore it
from [Trash](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/trash.md).

A move, rename or Move to Trash that fails (the doc is gone, the workspace is read-only for
you) shows a message at the bottom naming the doc and the reason. The tree stays as it was.
The message closes after 8 seconds, or with **✕**.

---

# Doc types

Source: https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/projects/typed-docs.md

Every doc has a type, so a project's docs sort themselves into folders and an agent knows
what shape to write. You write five types: **Plan**, **Design**, **Review**, **Bug** and
**Note**. A plain doc is a note. A test pass is a review.

## Choose a type

You choose the type when you make the doc, and it never changes after. For another type,
make another doc.

- the **+** on a project's row, or on a type folder in **Docs** ([Add a doc](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/projects/tree.md#add-a-doc));
- **⌘N** makes a note; ⌘K has **New Plan**, **New Review** and the others;
- **Generate a doc** (⌘⇧G) picks the type from what you ask for.

Every new doc starts empty. You write it, or ask your agent to. A project holds any number
of docs of each type, from any branch.

| Type | What it holds |
| --- | --- |
| **Plan** | What will be built, in what order, and why: goal, phases, decisions, risks, out of scope |
| **Design** | How it will work and look, and what was decided: the need, the screen, the approach, options considered, the decision |
| **Review** | What was found and decided: what was reviewed, what holds, what must change, the decision. One check item per finding or test case ([Check items](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/projects/editor.md#check-items)) |
| **Bug** | What is broken and why: what happens, steps to reproduce, expected and actual, the cause, the fix and the test that guards it |
| **Note** | Anything else: findings, a write-up, meeting notes, research |

These shapes are what agents are told to write. Slate never puts them into your doc.

## The line under the title

Some types show one line under the title. It says what the doc decided, or how bad a bug
is. It is read-only on screen: an agent writes it, and you change it by asking your agent.

| Type | The line |
| --- | --- |
| **Design** | **Decision:** and one line, or **Decision: not decided yet** |
| **Bug** | Its severity: **S1 · broken, no way around it**, **S2 · wrong, with a way around it** or **S3 · minor** |
| **Review** | Its decision: **Approved** or **Changes needed** |

A plan and a note have no line. A bug or a review shows nothing until an agent writes it.

## Docs your agent saves

Slate never makes a doc without asking. When your request names a milestone (a plan, a
review or test pass, a bug report, a design), Slate tells your agent to ask in the chat
whether to keep it as a doc. The agent asks with its own question tool, so in most agents
you click an answer.

- **Yes**: the agent saves the doc in the project, labelled with the branch. If the branch
  already has a doc of that type, it adds to that doc and keeps what is there.
- **No**: nothing is saved.

**A plan from plan mode** is kept as the project's Plan doc for that branch. A later plan
on the same branch replaces the one Slate saved. A Plan doc you wrote is never changed.

To have an agent change an existing doc, ask it in a session. It reads and writes docs
through Slate's tools ([MCP tool reference](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/mcp-server/tools.md#docs)). The doc's header
shows the sessions working on it; click one to open it.

---

# Files and changes

Source: https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/projects/code.md

The **Code** tab shows the code of every project with a folder on this computer (the picked
project, or all). Use it to read a file, see what changed, and commit. It has two views on
its left edge: **Files** and **Changes**. **Changes** carries a count of the files waiting
to be committed (99+ past 99).

Open it from the panel's **Code** tab, or with **Show code** on a project's ⋯ menu in
**Docs**. The doc icon at the end of a project's row in **Code** goes back to its folder in
**Docs**.

## Files

A tree like an editor's file explorer.

- A project with one folder is one row, its name and branch, with its files under it.
  With one project picked, the files start at the top under a bar with the branch.
- A project with two or more git worktrees is a group, such as **slate · 2 worktrees**,
  with a row per worktree named by its branch. Hover a row for its folder. One project and
  one worktree are open at a time.
- Files changed since the last commit show **M**, **A** or **D**, with a dot on their
  folders. Find a file by name with ⌘K.
- Hover a folder's row for **New file**, **New folder**, **Refresh** and **Collapse all**.
- Right-click a file, a folder or the space below for **New file**, **New folder**,
  **Open a Terminal here**, **Start session here**, **Copy path**, **Reveal in Finder**,
  **Rename** and **Move to Trash**. Names are typed in place. These wait while an agent
  works in that project. **Start session here** in a git project starts in a new worktree,
  in the same subfolder ([Worktrees](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/sessions/worktrees.md)).
- A rename or a move to Trash can be undone from its message. A trashed file also goes to
  the system Trash (the Recycle Bin on Windows). A file on another disk than the Trash, or
  on a Windows network share or removable drive, is refused and stays where it was.

## Changes

One source-control panel for each folder with files waiting to be committed. Each is named
by where it is, `group / project / worktree`, then the branch it commits on.

1. Type a one-line message.
2. Untick any file you want to leave out. Every file listed is committed unless unticked.
3. Press **Commit**, or **Commit & Push** in its ▾ menu.

It works the same as a session's Changes ([Review the branch](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/sessions/review.md#source-control)).
A worktree removed in a terminal leaves the list within about half a minute, or at once
when you return to the window.

## A file in a tab

A file opens in a tab, and the rail stays on Projects. A file picked in ⌘K opens here with
its folders unfolded.

- The line under the cursor shows, after its end, when it last changed and in which commit.
  **Blame** shows this for every line.
- **Show changes** appears when the file differs from where its branch began.
  **Back to the file**, or Esc, leaves.
- The bottom bar shows the branch, **worktree** when it is one, and the path from the
  project's folder.

A branch waiting for review opens here too, from Sessions: its worktree is selected in
**Files** and the whole branch opens in a tab with **Merge into <base>**, **Keep** and
**Discard** above it ([Branches waiting for review](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/sessions/review.md#branches-waiting-for-review)).

---

# Group and project settings

Source: https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/projects/settings.md

A group's or project's settings decide how agents work there: which agents, which commands
a new worktree runs, and when an agent run's work counts as done. Open **Settings…** on the
⋯ menu of a group, or of a project in no group. A project in a group uses its group's.

The settings are saved on this computer, because they name accounts and commands on it.
They never travel with a shared workspace. Only the **Memory** section is saved in the
workspace.

| Section | What it sets |
| --- | --- |
| **Folder** | Shows the folder on this computer. Change it with **Change folder** on the ⋯ menu |
| **Agents here** | Which agents this project uses. None ticked: the workspace's. **Save agents** saves. Accounts and models are set in Connect → **Agents** |
| **New worktrees** | **Set up**, **Preview**, **On remove** and **Carry over** commands ([Worktrees](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/sessions/worktrees.md)) |
| **Done means** | The **Check** command that decides an agent run's work is done, **Autopilot**, and the **Rules** agent runs follow here ([Agent runs](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/tasks/agent-runs.md#autopilot), [Agent run rules](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/tasks/agent-run-rules.md)) |
| **Work from** | The sources whose tasks start here ([The start dialog](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/tasks/agent-runs.md#the-start-dialog)) |
| **Project hooks** | Shown when the project's own agent settings run commands at the start of a turn. Until you press **Allow this project's hooks**, turns below Full auto are refused here. A change to those settings asks again |
| **Memory** | What Slate keeps from this project ([What a project keeps](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/memory/decisions-and-facts.md#what-a-project-keeps)) |

Fields save when you leave them.

---

# Memory

Source: https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/memory.md

Memory is what Slate remembers from your agents' work: decisions, lessons, preferences,
lasting knowledge and where things stand. Every agent you connect shares it, so what one agent learns
reaches the next session in any agent.

## How memory fills

- **Agents save it.** A session saves one memory at a time with Slate's `remember` tool
  ([Search and save](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/memory/recall-remember.md)).
- **Slate captures sessions.** It reads the conversation files your agents already write
  and keeps each session ([Session capture](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/memory/session-capture.md)).
- **Slate reads your agents' own memory.** Claude Code and Gemini each keep a memory
  folder the other agents do not read. Slate reads them for the folders you added as
  projects, so one agent's learning reaches the rest.
- **You import it.** **Import**, the down arrow in the Memory panel's title row, reads
  Claude Code, Codex, Gemini, claude-mem, agentmemory, mem0, Basic Memory and Cline
  Memory Bank. It shows what it would add before it adds anything. A memory from a folder
  that is no project in this workspace is left out ([Import](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/connect/import.md)).

## How memory reaches a session

1. **At the start**, a session gets a short brief with the project's most useful memories
   ([What a session is given](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/memory/session-start-brief.md)).
2. **While it works**, it searches with `recall` for what its task needs
   ([Search and save](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/memory/recall-remember.md)).
3. **On a tool call**, a lesson about that command or file arrives with the call
   ([Lessons](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/memory/recall-remember.md#lessons)).

When the session uses a memory, it names it. That is how Slate learns which memories help.

## Read and fix it

The **Memory** place shows every memory on a map of the files it is about, with a list
beside it to read, search, correct and retire ([The Memory screen](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/memory/map.md)). Fix a wrong
memory there and the next session reads the correction.

## Where it is kept

Memory lives in the workspace on this computer that holds the project. `recall` reads it
there and does not leave the computer. What you put in a
[shared workspace](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/workspaces.md) is readable by its members and their agents.

## In this section

| Read | What it covers |
| --- | --- |
| [The Memory screen](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/memory/map.md) | The map, the list, a memory's card, review and rules |
| [Session capture](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/memory/session-capture.md) | How Slate keeps your agents' sessions |
| [What a session is given](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/memory/session-start-brief.md) | The brief, the index, and choosing what agents get |
| [Search and save](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/memory/recall-remember.md) | `recall`, `remember`, lessons and citing |
| [Kinds of memory](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/memory/decisions-and-facts.md) | The five kinds, decisions, shelf life, and what a project keeps |
| [Tidying memory](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/memory/tidy-and-measure.md) | Tidy proposals, AI memory care, lessons from what you decline |

---

# The Memory screen

Source: https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/memory/map.md

**Memory** shows everything Slate remembers. The map in the main area shows where your
memories sit and which ones sessions use. The list in the side panel is where you read,
search, correct and retire them.

With nothing saved, Memory says **Nothing saved yet** and offers **Connect an agent**.

## The side panel

From the top:

- the **project picker**, which narrows the map and the list to one project. Memory opens
  on the project you picked last;
- **Map**, with the count of memories: the whole map;
- **Rules**, with its count: what your agents get ([Rules](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/memory/session-start-brief.md#rules));
- **To review**, with a count, when something waits for you ([To review](#to-review));
- the search box, **Search memories, files, m: refs**;
- **Kinds**: one row per kind of memory that has any, with its count, and **Retired**
  last ([Kinds of memory](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/memory/decisions-and-facts.md)).

Click a kind to open it and draw only that kind on the map. Its memories are listed one
line each, newest first, with **Show N older** past the newest 10. One kind is open at a
time. Click a memory to open its card.

**Retired** lists what was retired in the last 30 days that nothing replaced, up to 50.
Open one for **Bring back**. With none, it says **Nothing retired in the last 30 days.**

## The map

Each folder of the project is a region with its name, its memory count and the share
sessions used, such as `server 213 · 3% used`. Each memory is a dot near the file it cites.

- A solid, bright dot was used this month or is new this week. A faint hollow ring was
  never used. A region full of hollow rings is worth cleaning up.
- Folders with fewer than 12 memories share **Other**. Memories that cite no file sit in
  **General**.
- On **All projects**, each project is one region.
- Click a region to go into it. The list then shows only its memories. Go back with the
  path above the map (`slate › server`), a click on empty space, or Esc.
- The map and the list are one selection: a list row opens its card on the map, and a dot
  scrolls the list to its row.

A session in Sessions says how many memories it was given, used and wrote. Click that line
to see exactly those: **Showing “…” — 3 given · 1 used · 2 written**. **Clear** shows all.

## Search and filters

Search needs every typed word in the memory's text, tags, cited file or `m:` ref. The map
lights the matches. Region, search and likely duplicates show as chips on one **Filters:**
line. Click a chip to drop it, or **Clear all**. With no match the list says
**No memory matches these filters.** and, inside one project, offers
**Search all projects**.

**N possible duplicates**, above the map, lists the likely duplicates. Open one for
**Merge**, which keeps it and retires the other.

## A memory's card

The card shows how the memory travelled (**Given to 57 sessions, used in 3**), the file it
cites, who wrote it, which agents confirmed or used it, what it replaced, and other
memories about the same file. It also shows what your own acts said about it: a merge
that confirmed it, a revert or discard that contradicted it, an edit to the cited lines.
Each has an undo.

| Action | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| **Edit** | Change the text. **Save** (⌘Enter) or **Cancel** (Esc) |
| **Pin** | Every session in its project starts with it |
| **Hide from sessions** | Keeps it in this list, but no agent is given it. **Give to sessions again** undoes it |
| **Protect** | AI memory care never reads it, and **Retire session** never takes it |
| **Retire** | Takes it out of the list and out of every session. **Bring back** undoes it |
| **Retire session** | Retires everything the session that wrote it saved, after a preview. Pinned and protected memories stay |

A memory whose cited file is gone shows **cited file gone** and is not given to sessions.

## To review

Only what Slate may not decide alone waits here:

- a claim that disagrees with a surer memory: **Keep existing**, **Replace it** or
  **Keep both**;
- a tidy change the save rules refused, a lesson from what you declined, or a memory the
  two readings of AI memory care disagree on: **Merge**, **Retire** or
  **Make it a lesson**, or **Keep as is**.

Each item needs its own choice. Click the **To review** row to open them one by one.

At the top sit two lines about the last 7 days:

- **Learned this week**: memories you accepted, new skills, decisions an agent run
  closed, the noes Slate kept, and what your merges, reverts and discards confirmed or
  contradicted.
- **Tidied this week**: what tidies merged, retired and turned into lessons, with one
  **Undo** ([Tidying memory](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/memory/tidy-and-measure.md)).

A quiet week draws neither line.

---

# Session capture

Source: https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/memory/session-capture.md

Slate keeps every session your agents run, so you can find it later and so Activity and
Memory know what happened. It reads the conversation files your agents already write on
this computer. It sends nothing to the network.

## Turn it on

An agent is read once you turn it on, in setup or in Connect → **Agents**. Its sessions
appear within a few minutes. An agent turned on in any workspace is captured for all of
them: [Sessions](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/sessions.md) covers the whole computer.

## Which agents

- **From their transcript files**: Claude Code, Codex, Gemini, Cursor and GitHub
  Copilot.
- **From their own database, read-only**: OpenCode, Hermes Agent, Goose, Kilo Code and
  Kiro.

Which agents are verified is in [Features by agent](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/agents/features-by-agent.md).

Every profile a workspace or project names is watched, wherever its folder is. Slate also
suggests any other agent that writes conversation files under your home folder.

## What a captured session holds

Each session is kept with its first request, a one-line summary, the agent and model that
ran it, the tokens it used and the git branch it ran on. Its body is a digest: every turn
you typed, where your requests and corrections live, and the final outcome.

A captured session opens read-only, with **Session — read only** under its title. It is
listed in [Sessions](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/sessions.md), never in the Projects tree.

**A cloud session brought back.** A [cloud session](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/sessions/cloud.md) runs on the
vendor's computer, out of Slate's sight. When you bring a Claude Code cloud session back and
send a message, its whole conversation is written on this computer and captured. Nothing is
captured before that first message.

## Agents' own memory

Claude Code and Gemini each keep a memory folder of their own. Slate reads them, so one
agent's learning reaches the others:

- A file is read once its folder is inside a project or group you added.
- Each file becomes one memory written by that agent, citing the file.
- A changed file replaces its memory, and a removed file retires it.
- Slate never writes to these folders.

Codex keeps its memory per user, with no project folder, so Slate does not read it. Bring
it in with [Import](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/connect/import.md) instead.

## Turn capture off

- **Everywhere**: **Auto-capture** in Automations › **Built-in**. Off stops capture at once
  and stays off after a restart. Capture also stops when you quit Slate; at the next launch
  it picks up the sessions run in between.
- **For one project**: in the project's **Settings…** → **Memory**, turn
  **Capture sessions** off. Sessions in its folder are not saved, the agents' memory files
  there are not read, and an import skips what it would file into that project
  ([What a project keeps](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/memory/decisions-and-facts.md#what-a-project-keeps)).

---

# What a session is given

Source: https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/memory/session-start-brief.md

Every session starts knowing where it is and what matters most in this project, without
reading all of memory. The rest it looks up for its task with `recall`
([Search and save](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/memory/recall-remember.md)).

## The brief

Agents with Slate's hooks get a short brief when a session starts, in this order:

1. **Scope**: the project, the branch, and the branch's goal when one was written down.
2. **Open**: the branch's open items, the pull requests and issues waiting on you in this
   project (from [Tasks](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/tasks.md)), and on the main branch the other branches
   that still hold uncommitted work.
3. **Others**: other sessions working in this project now.
4. **Rules**: up to 5 of your own rules for this project ([Rules](#rules)).
5. **Memory index**: up to 12 memories, each with its ref (such as `m:7f3a2b1c`). First the
   ones you pinned, then the decisions and lessons sessions here used most. A session
   outside any project gets no index.
6. One line telling the session to call `recall` once it knows its task.

Agents with no start hook get the same index from Slate's MCP server when they connect.

A hidden memory, a status note past its shelf life and a memory whose cited code changed
never reach a session ([Kinds of memory](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/memory/decisions-and-facts.md#shelf-life-and-resting)).

## Look it up first

- **The first prompt** asks the session to call `recall` with its task before it starts,
  unless the request is trivial.
- **Before its first read or edit**, a session that got that ask and has not called
  `recall` is held: the call is refused with one line asking it to look first. After one
  `recall`, nothing is held again. A session that cannot reach Slate's tools is never
  held.
- **At the end of a turn**, a session that changed files without calling `recall` is sent
  back once to look. A session that did look but did not say which memories it used is
  asked once to name them.

**One session in four is held out.** It gets the brief without the memory index, and none
of these asks, so Slate can compare sessions with and without memory
([Does memory help?](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/memory/tidy-and-measure.md#does-memory-help)).

Text a widget wrote reaches a session in quotes, marked as data and never as an
instruction.

## A session started from a task

**Run <automation>** on a task starts a session whose goal Slate knows from the start
([Agent runs](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/tasks/agent-runs.md)). Instead of the brief it gets a card of up to 4,000
characters:

- **Scope**: the task's title, the note you typed when you started it, the project and the
  branch.
- **Open** and **Others**: as in the brief.
- **Connected**: the integrations connected for this workspace, by name only, such as
  *GitHub (acme/app)*. Never what they hold, and never a token.
- **Rules**: up to 5 of your rules for this project.
- **Memory**: up to 5 memories. First those that cite a file the task names, then the ones
  you pinned. A line points at `recall` for more.

## Where else memory is given

| Place | What it gets |
| --- | --- |
| An [automation](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/automations.md) run | The memory index as `@memory` in its first step |
| Home's AI and Ask AI | The memory index of the project you are in |

## Choose what each one gets

- **What it gets from memory**, on an automation's **What it knows** tab and in Home's
  composer, lists the lines the next run gets and why. **Always give this here** puts one
  first. **Not relevant here** keeps it out.
- A memory's card in [Memory](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/memory/map.md) lists every such choice, each with an undo.

## Rules

A rule decides which memories your agents get. Open **Rules** in Memory's side panel to
see them; pick one to edit it, turn it off or remove it. The **+** in the panel's title
row opens **Add a rule**: choose **For** (all projects or one), then a **Ready rule** or
**Write your own**.

| Ready rule | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| **Leave out what nobody used for a while** | Leaves out memories not used for N days (60 to start) |
| **Keep only lessons that proved useful** | Keeps only memories used in at least N sessions (2 to start) |
| **Keep only decisions from work that shipped** | Keeps only memories from agent runs whose pull request merged |
| **Drop what came from work that was undone** | Leaves out memories from work reverted after it merged |

A ready rule shows how many memories it would leave out. **Write your own** is a sentence
every agent that saves memory here reads under "Rules". Slate cannot check it.

A rule only decides what is given out. Nothing is removed, and what a rule leaves out comes
back when you turn the rule off.

---

# Search and save

Source: https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/memory/recall-remember.md

Agents read and write memory through Slate's MCP tools. You do not call these yourself;
this explains what your agents do with them, so you know what to expect. Every
argument is in the [MCP tool reference](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/mcp-server/tools.md#memory).

## Search: `recall`

`recall` searches the project's memories, its docs in Slate, and the project's own
Markdown files (`AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `README.md`, `CONTRIBUTING.md` at its root, and
the `.md` files under `docs/`, `doc/`, `adr/` and `decisions/`). It returns a shortlist of
15, one line each, best first. The agent picks the ones that answer its task.

- **Ranking is local.** Words are matched by how rare they are among your memories. No
  model is called and nothing is downloaded. Recent memories rank slightly higher.
- **Nothing found is an answer.** A question nothing covers gets no memories, and a
  one-line note naming up to three docs worth reading.
- **A changed citation is flagged.** `citation: changed` means the cited code changed since
  the memory was written; `citation: gone` means the file is missing. The agent reads the
  code before relying on it.
- **About the branch.** When the question names the branch, or asks what is open or in
  progress, the first result is the branch's brief: its goal, open items, recent sessions
  and commits.
- **The past.** With `as_of` and a date, `recall` answers from what memory believed at the
  end of that day.

`get_memory` reads memories in full: why each was written, the file it cites, who
confirmed it, and what it replaced.

## Save: `remember`

A session saves one memory per call, as one sentence, with a kind: `decision`,
`preference`, `state` (where something stands), `fact` or `lesson`
([Kinds of memory](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/memory/decisions-and-facts.md)).

- **Filing.** The memory belongs to the project the session works in. With no project it is
  global and reaches every session.
- **Duplicates.** A near-duplicate strengthens the memory already there. The reply lists up
  to 3 close memories, so the agent can replace one that is wrong.
- **Pinning.** `index: true` pins the memory into the project's index, up to 25 per project.
- **Secrets.** Recognised keys, tokens and passwords are saved as `[secret]`.
- **Disagreement.** A claim that contradicts a surer memory never overwrites it. It waits
  for you under [To review](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/memory/map.md#to-review).

**What is worth saving**: a correction you made, an approach you confirmed, a decision and
its reason, something true that is not obvious. Agents are asked to save at most two per
task. After real work with nothing saved (5 changes or 10 of your turns), or after you
corrected the agent, the session's end asks it once to save what the next session needs.

**What is refused**, each with the reason: passing status ("currently editing X"), a
progress note or a git snapshot, a decision with no reason, an agent's memory with three
or more numbers, a `state` with no `subject`, and anything the project's memory settings
turn off ([What a project keeps](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/memory/decisions-and-facts.md#what-a-project-keeps)).

**Correcting.** The agent writes the true claim and names the wrong one in `replaces`. The
wrong one is retired.

## Lessons

A lesson says what to do in a situation. Give it a `when`, and it arrives with the
matching tool call:

| `when` | Arrives with |
| --- | --- |
| `{ tool: "shell", match: "<regular expression>" }` | A command that matches, such as `git push` |
| `{ tool: "read", path: "<glob>" }` | Reading a matching file, such as `packages/db/**` |
| `{ tool: "edit", path: "<glob>" }` | Editing or writing a matching file |

A memory that cites the file being read or edited arrives the same way. At most 2 memories
arrive per call, each once per session. The call is never blocked or changed. A pattern that
matches everything is refused.

| Agent | When the lesson arrives |
| --- | --- |
| Claude Code | Before a shell, read or edit call |
| Codex | Before a shell or patch call, once you trust Slate's hook under `/hooks` |
| Gemini, Cursor | After a shell, read or edit call, in its result |
| OpenCode | After a shell, read, edit or patch call, in its result |

## Progress on a branch

`log_mission_progress` reports a session's work on its branch. Its goal and open items
become what the next session on that branch is told. Each decision becomes a memory. The
summary is kept with the project's sessions. On `main`, `master` or `develop` the goal is
not changed.

## How Slate learns what helped

An agent names the refs of the memories it used, in `used` on its next tool call, never in
its reply. Your own acts on the code count too:

- your merge of a branch confirms the memories its sessions used;
- a revert or a discard contradicts them;
- saving an edit on cited lines asks whether the memory still holds
  ([What agents know about the file](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/sessions/files.md#what-agents-know-about-the-file)).

Each shows on the memory's card with an undo. A memory contradicted twice and never
confirmed leaves the index unless pinned. A memory nobody uses or restates for 30 days
rests: it leaves the index but stays searchable.

---

# Kinds of memory

Source: https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/memory/decisions-and-facts.md

Every memory has one of five kinds. The kind decides how it is used: a decision explains
why, a lesson arrives on a tool call, a status note expires.

| Kind | Holds |
| --- | --- |
| `decision` | A choice and its reason: "chose X over Y because Z" |
| `preference` | How you like to work |
