| `state` | Where a piece of work stands. Memory calls it a status note. Expires after 14 days |
| `fact` | Lasting knowledge about the project. Memory calls it a general memory |
| `lesson` | What to do in a situation, and why. Can arrive on a tool call ([Lessons](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/memory/recall-remember.md#lessons)) |

## Decisions

A decision must carry its reason, or it is refused. Saving one also writes a decision doc
with the full reasoning, the options turned down and how sure it is. `recall` ranks a
decision first for a "why" question.

**A decision learns what came of it.** When an [agent run](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/tasks/agent-runs.md) relied on
a decision, Slate adds a line under the doc's **Outcome**:

| What happened | The line |
| --- | --- |
| The pull request merged | **Shipped in “Fix the invoice rounding” (link), 2026-10-14.** |
| It closed without merging | **Not shipped: “…” closed without merging (link), …** |
| A merged GitHub pull request was reverted within 30 days | **Reverted: “…” was undone in (link), …** |

Pull requests are checked through your own `gh`. GitLab merge requests are not checked.

## One memory replaces another

A preference or a status note has one value at a time. When an agent saves one with a
`subject`, a dotted key such as `ui.theme`, it retires the older memory with the same key.
A status note saved by an agent must have one. Decisions, lessons and `fact` memories add up instead.

## Shelf life and resting

- **Status notes expire.** 14 days after it was last confirmed, a status note is no longer
  given to any session. It stays in the list. Restating it starts the 14 days again. A
  status note about a branch that landed or was removed is retired.
- **Unused memories rest.** A memory nobody used or restated for 30 days leaves the index.
  It stays stored and searchable, and using or pinning it wakes it. Pinned memories and
  preferences never rest.

Slate also keeps one status note for each branch that holds uncommitted work, so the next
session knows about it.

## What a project keeps

Open a group's or project's **Settings…**, then **Memory**:

- **Keep**: **The workspace default**, **Decisions and lessons only**, or
  **Every kind, from every writer**.
- **Advanced**:
  - **Kinds**: which kinds are kept.
  - **Written by**: which writers may save. Agents, Slate's automations and tasks, widgets,
    and agents' own memory files.
  - **Never about**: words a memory may never mention, separated by commas, up to 50.
  - **Capture sessions**: off, and sessions in this project's folder are not saved.
- **Inherit everything** resets it.

Each setting shows where it comes from: **set here**, **from** a group, **from the
workspace**, or **default**. A word banned higher up stays banned here. A refused memory
is not saved, and the agent is told why. What you save yourself is always kept. A new
setting applies from now on; kept memories stay.

## Hide from sessions

**Hide from sessions** on a memory's card keeps it in your list but gives it to no one: no
session, no teammate (one already shared is withdrawn), no widget and no AI memory care.

- Where its words were copied into a doc (a decision doc, a note), they stay as you wrote
  them for you. Wherever the doc leaves your hands, to an agent, a widget or a teammate,
  they become `[held memory]`.
- In a shared workspace the hide reaches your other computers on the same account at their
  next sync. In a workspace never shared, it stays on this computer.
- A teammate sees a hidden memory as removed.

**Give to sessions again** undoes both.

## Is memory still reachable?

The **Are memories reachable?** card on [Activity](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/activity.md) (add it while arranging
the board) finds three faults and can repair them:

- a memory filed under a removed doc, which `recall` can no longer reach;
- a memory filed under a group when its cited file sits in exactly one project of it;
- a citation that no longer points at a file. The citation is dropped and the claim kept.

**Show what would change** lists every change before you repair. Nothing runs on its own.

---

# Tidying memory

Source: https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/memory/tidy-and-measure.md

Memory grows with every session, so Slate keeps it small and right without a model of its
own. Your agent proposes tidies, AI memory care can check memories each night, and every
change can be undone.

## A tidy

When a project's memory needs it, a session offers to tidy it, at most once a week. If you
agree, the agent reads the project's memories and proposes:

- a **merge**: several memories become one;
- a **retirement**: a memory that is wrong or outdated;
- a **lesson**: several memories become one rule with a `when`
  ([Lessons](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/memory/recall-remember.md#lessons)).

The change applies at once. **Tidied this week**, at the top of [To review](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/memory/map.md#to-review),
says what tidies changed in the last 7 days, with one **Undo**. A memory you pinned or
protected is never touched. A change the save rules refuse waits under **To review** for
you instead.

## AI memory care

**AI memory care** checks your memories each night with your own agent. Turn it on at the
end of **Built-in** in [Automations](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/automations/built-in.md). It applies to this
workspace only.

- At 03:00, when the computer is awake and Slate is open, it reads up to 50 memories of one
  project or group, with the code each cites. A missed night is skipped.
- It reads each memory twice, separately, and retires only what both readings call wrong.
  When the readings disagree, the memory waits under **To review**.
- Before you turn it on, it shows what the first month will cost in tokens. It stops for
  the month at the **Monthly cap** you set.
- A memory it retired can be brought back from **Retired** for 30 days.
- While it is on, an agent's new memory must say in its reason why it changes what a future
  agent does.

For your own schedule instead, add the **Tidy memories** starter in
[Automations](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/automations.md#the-starters).

## Lessons from what you decline

Slate keeps your no to an AI proposal: an automation's held call answered **No**, a step
sent back, a widget card declined, a Home tool call skipped. A no becomes a proposal under
**To review** when you wrote a reason in **Why? (optional)**, or when you declined the same
action twice in 30 days in the same place. Accepting it saves a lesson. At most 5 such
proposals wait per project.

## When a lesson becomes a skill

A lesson used in at least 3 sessions is a way of working. Slate proposes it as a skill in
**Toolkit › Suggestions**, at most 3 a day. **Make it a skill** writes the skill into the
project's folder, where every agent loads it, and the lesson leaves the memory index. A
dismissed proposal is not asked again. A lesson with no project folder on this computer
is never proposed.

## Does memory help?

The **Does memory help?** card on [Activity](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/activity.md) (add it while arranging the
board) compares sessions given memory with the one session in four held out. It counts
the turns where you corrected the agent ("no, …", "wrong", "I told you"), per session, in
each group. It shows a result once each group has 50 sessions. You can turn the holdout
off there.

Two more cards read the memory layer: **Do sessions save memory?** and
**Is memory used?**.

---

# Activity

Source: https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/activity.md

**Activity** shows your agent sessions over time: what you did today, which projects you
worked in, and how your work is trending. It is built from data already on this computer.

With no sessions yet it says **No activity yet** and offers **New session**.

## The side panel

- the **project picker**: **All projects**, or one;
- **Range**: **7d**, **30d**, **90d**, **1y** or **All**;
- **Saved views**: a range, a filter and a project kept under a name. The view on screen
  is marked. **Remove view** offers **Undo**.

## The summary

One sentence sums up the range, such as **You ran 12 sessions over 6h, mostly in slate
(8 of 12). Busiest at 14:00.** "Mostly in" shows only when one project holds half the
sessions or more. A second line names the change worth a look, such as
**Look at: more sessions than the 30 days before (21) …**.

Four cards compare the range with the same number of days before it: **sessions**,
**session time**, **memories learned** and **active days**. **All** has no days before it,
so it shows no change.

## The board

At first the board holds:

| Card | What it shows |
| --- | --- |
| **Timeline** | The last 7 days, newest first: sessions, memories learned, finished agent runs, automation reports and artifacts. Today and yesterday are open; older days are one line. An open day lists up to 6 sessions and 4 memories, then **+N more** |
| **Sessions over time** | The trend over the range. Drag across it to zoom |
| **Last 13 weeks** | A calendar of your activity, always 13 weeks whatever the range. Click a day to see it in the Timeline. Arrow keys move between days; Enter opens one |
| **Time of day**, **Weekday** | When you work. **Peak** names the busiest hour |
| **By agent**, **By project**, **By branch** | Sessions ranked. Project and branch show the top 8. Click a row to filter the board to it |

**Show records**, under the Timeline, adds your busiest day, best week, longest focus,
favorite agent and top model. **Hide records** removes them.

Your [widgets](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/widgets.md) made for Activity join the board once built, in the side
column. A widget not drawn within 10 seconds says so, with a link to Widgets.

## Arrange the board

Click **Arrange the board**, the grid icon in the side panel's title row.

1. A dashed spot at the top of each column lists the cards you can add: the ones you took
   off, and **Sessions** (the full list), **Momentum**, **By model**, **Memories**,
   **Quick stats**, and four readings of memory: **Do sessions save memory?**,
   **Is memory used?**, **Does memory help?** and **Are memories reachable?**
   ([Tidying memory](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/memory/tidy-and-measure.md#does-memory-help),
   [Kinds of memory](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/memory/decisions-and-facts.md#is-memory-still-reachable)).
2. Move cards up or down, or **Hide widget**. **Reset layout** restores the first board.
3. Press **Done**.

**Momentum** lists up to 6 projects with their sessions in the range and the change
against the days before, such as **+3**. It shows nothing on **All**.

Agent runs have no card of their own. They are listed in
[Automations](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/automations.md), and the Timeline shows a finished run on the day it
ended.

## Where the numbers come from

Slate reads each agent's own files: the transcripts of Claude Code, Codex, Gemini,
Cursor and the others that write them, and the databases of OpenCode, Kiro, Hermes Agent,
Goose and Kilo Code ([Session capture](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/memory/session-capture.md)).

- A session is one conversation, counted once however many files or branches it touched.
  It counts when you typed into it and the model answered. Runs nobody typed into, such as
  `claude -p`, and Slate's own runs are not sessions.
- Days are your local calendar days. Session time is the time between your turns, leaving
  out any pause over 15 minutes.

What Slate reads is kept on this computer, even after the agent removes its own files, and
is never shared, even from a shared workspace.

**History from before Slate.** Claude Code removes transcripts after 30 days but keeps the
prompts you typed. For a session whose transcript is gone, Slate reads those prompts: the
session, its day, its folder. Tokens, cost and session time are not in them, so such a
session shows **not recorded** for tokens, and **session time** compares with the days
before only when both stretches have full records.

---

# Artifacts

Source: https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/artifacts.md

An **artifact** is something an agent made for you to look at: an HTML page, such as a dashboard, chart or report, or a deck of slides. Any connected agent publishes one with Slate's `publish_artifact` tool, and it stays in your workspace with every version. Writing you will keep editing belongs in a [doc](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/projects.md) instead.

## Make or change one

You never edit an artifact by hand. You ask.

1. **Ask for one**: "make me a dashboard of this data as an artifact". Agents are also told to publish a chart, table or report this way on their own.
2. **Open it**: click the `slate://artifacts` link the agent gives you. It names the workspace, so Slate switches to it first.
3. **Ask for a change**: "make the bars blue", to any agent, or to **Ask AI** while the artifact is open. Ask AI works on the open artifact, in the project it was made in. Each change adds a version; older versions stay.

An agent can publish HTML it wrote, or a file by its path. Slate reads a file only from the agent's working folder or a temp folder, and never a hidden file or folder such as `.env` or `.ssh`.

**Import** at the top of the side panel brings in a folder of HTML files, or your claude.ai artifacts ([Import](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/connect/import.md)).

## Find one

- **The side panel**: **Filter artifacts** narrows by title and description. Below it, **Overview**, then **Pages** and **Slides**, each with its count.
- **Overview**: **Recent**, the 4 newest as cards with a picture, and a link to each type's full list; then **Earlier**, the next 10 as one line each.
- **Pages** or **Slides**: every artifact of that type as a card, newest first, 24 at a time.
- **⌘K** finds an artifact by title or description, under **Artifacts**. It does not search the HTML.
- **On a doc**: **Artifacts made here** lists the artifacts an agent made on that doc.
- **Your agents**: `recall` returns up to 2 artifacts whose title matches every word of the question, so a session can find last week's dashboard and change it.

## An open artifact

The artifact fills the main area. Its toolbar has:

| Control | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| **Preview** / **Code** | The artifact, or its HTML source laid out one block per line (read only) |
| **‹ v2 of 3 ›** | Steps through versions. An older one says "You are looking at v2. The newest is v3." with **Restore this version**, which publishes it again as the newest |
| **More** (⋯) | **Copy HTML**, **Open in browser**, **Rename**, and **Delete forever**, which asks "Delete every version forever?" |

A **deck** shows one slide at a time, scaled to fit. **‹ 3 / 12 ›** or the arrow keys move between slides. The strip below shows every slide, then the slide's **Speaker notes**. **Present** shows the deck full screen.

An HTML page uses Slate's fonts and colours and follows your theme, under its own styles. Opened in your browser, it uses plain colours and your system's light or dark mode.

## Live artifacts

An artifact published as live reads your workspace while it is open, so a dashboard stays current without being published again. It says **Reads your workspace · no internet**.

- **It reads**: docs, one doc's text, memories and sessions of its project (or the whole workspace when it was made in none), up to 5,000 of each, newest first. It cannot change anything.
- **No internet**: it cannot fetch, open forms, new windows or frames, or load images or fonts from the internet. It may load scripts from cdnjs, jsDelivr and unpkg, so chart libraries work. If it tries to leave its web page, Slate closes it.
- **Only yours**: a teammate's live artifact shows to you as a plain HTML page, and never reads your workspace.

## Where it runs

An artifact runs its own scripts in a frame kept apart from Slate and your data. It cannot control the Slate window. A deck's slides run no scripts. A teammate's artifact cannot read the browser storage of yours.

In a shared workspace every member sees every artifact, but only the person who published it can rename it or delete it forever. Their new versions reach you when the workspace syncs. Moving a group or project to another workspace takes its artifacts with it.

## Limits

- One HTML document per artifact, up to 5,000,000 characters.
- A deck needs at least one top-level `<section>`, one per slide. An `<aside>` inside a section is that slide's speaker notes.
- A [widget](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/widgets.md) is not an artifact: the artifact tools refuse one and name the widget tools.

---

# Widgets

Source: https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/widgets.md

A **widget** is a small card your agent builds for you and Slate shows on a tab: tokens per project on Activity, a review queue on Home, a session's cost beside it in Sessions. You describe it, your agent writes it, and you change it by asking again. A widget reads only what you allow, and never reaches the internet.

## Make one

1. Open **Widgets**. With no widget open you see the **Overview**: a box at the top, then **Your widgets** as cards.
2. Under **Show it on**, pick the tab: **Home**, **Activity** or **Sessions**.
3. Describe the widget ("Describe a widget for Activity…") and press Enter. The box names the agent that builds it, your workspace's agent from [Connect](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/connect.md); click it to pick another.

A card appears at once, marked **Building**. The widget then opens with its chat beside the preview, so you can watch it being built. When the build ends, the card shows its age, or **Failed**.

Your agent works in a session Slate keeps in the background, under your own account. It does not show in Sessions. If it asks something the chat cannot show as buttons, the chat says "needs an answer Slate cannot show here" with **Open in Sessions**.

## Where it shows

A widget shows only on the tab it was made for, because its code reads that tab's data. To show the same idea on another tab, make another widget.

| Tab | Widgets at most | How it looks |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Home** | 3 | On a card like the cards that need you, with no title |
| **Activity** | 2 | In the side column, under its name |
| **Sessions** | 1 | One more tab in an open session's side panel, beside **Details**, **Changes** and **Turns** |

When a tab is full, a new widget is still built but waits off the tab until you move another to Trash. **Show it on** says "Home is full — 3 of 3. Take one off or move one to Trash first."

A version shows on its tab only after it built, passed its check, and was seen to fit at its size. Until then the version before stays. A widget that does not draw within 10 seconds says "This widget did not draw." Pointing at a widget on its tab shows one button, which opens it in Widgets.

You choose where it sits and how big it is on its **Preview** in Widgets, never on the tab: [Place and size a widget](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/widgets/placing.md).

## Change one

An open widget has **Preview** and **Files**, the chat on the left (**Hide chat** / **Show chat**), the versions **‹ v2 of 3 ›** and **⋯**.

- **The chat**: ask in your own words, such as "make the buttons green". The header says **Working**, **Asking you** or **Done**. Your agent's steps show as quiet lines under its reply. **Discuss** talks a change through and changes nothing; **Build it** then makes it. Each answer ends with up to 3 ideas you can click.
- **Questions**: with Claude Code, a question or a permission request shows as a card with buttons. Other agents show **Open in Sessions** instead.
- **Preview**: the widget on its tab, live. **Reload**, **Full size**, and **Point at it**, which lets you click a part of the widget to ask the chat about it. A line says what it reads, such as "Reads Personal. No internet."
- **Files**: the widget's files in an editor. Save with **Save 2 changes** or ⌘S; **Discard** undoes your edits. **Diff** compares with the version before. Slate checks types and builds before it saves; if either fails, nothing is saved and each error opens at its line.
- **Fix with AI**: shows when a version fails its check, does not fit, or stops on an error. It sends your agent only the file, line and kind of error, never the widget's own words. **Quote it** puts the widget's error text in the chat box for you to read first.
- **Versions**: every version stays. **‹ v2 of 3 ›** steps through them, and **Restore** brings an older one back as the newest.
- **⋯**: a switch for each permission and MCP tool the widget asked for, and **Move to Trash**. Trash keeps every version; **Restore** there brings it back.

A teammate's widget opens read-only, with **Preview** and **Files** only.

## What it can read and do

By default a widget reads only its tab: on Activity, the sessions and memories for the range and project picked there; on Home, the sessions running now and receipts from the last day; on Sessions, the session open beside it. It can also keep up to 1 MB of its own data on this computer and show a toast.

Anything more needs a permission the widget names in its setup, with a reason. A new widget's first version shows one card in its chat with what it asks for and why: **Allow** or **Not now**. Later, use the switches in **⋯**. Reading always stays inside the widget's own workspace.

| Permission | What it allows |
| --- | --- |
| **Read your workspace** | Your docs, memories, sessions, usage and automations in this workspace |
| **Read your Tasks** | Every open item in Tasks, from every connected app |
| **Change your Tasks** | Add your own items, set reminders and mark them done |
| **Read your GitHub** | Your open pull requests, the ones waiting for your review, and their checks |
| **Act on your GitHub** | Approve, request changes on, comment on or label your pull requests |
| **Save memories** | Save memories in this project |
| **Write docs** | Make docs and add text to docs in this project |
| **Run automations** | Run one of your automations |
| **Open AI sessions** | Open a session with a prompt typed in |

The last five also need your OK for each call. Slate shows a card above the widget, on its tab or in the Widgets preview, with the exact words it would save, the doc it adds to, the prompt or automation, or the GitHub action and the account it acts as. The button names what it does, such as **Save memory** or **Approve on GitHub**, and works a moment after the card appears. **Not now** refuses, and nothing is written. A comment or review on GitHub posts only words you type on the card. A session opens on the project the tab shows, with the prompt typed in for you to send. One card shows at a time.

A widget can also read through an MCP tool your workspace reaches, such as Linear's, one tool at a time. Its card shows the server, the tool and the reason, and **Allow** works only after you tick "This tool only reads. It changes nothing." If the tool changes later, the card asks again, marked **Changed since you allowed it**.

## What a widget writes stays the widget's

A memory a widget saves is held: no session, teammate or agent receives it until you release it in Memory, and it is never shared with a team. When an agent does read one, it gets it as quoted data, never as an instruction. A doc a widget writes to is marked as written by a widget, and agents see its text quoted the same way.

## What it cannot do

- Reach the internet. If it tries to leave its web page, Slate closes it.
- Read another workspace, or anything of a teammate's.
- Change anything through an MCP tool.
- Type into a session, approve, or stop one.

The reference for building one is [Widget API](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/widgets/api.md).

---

# Place and size a widget

Source: https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/widgets/placing.md

You place a [widget](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/widgets.md) on its **Preview** in Widgets. The tab itself has no menu and nothing that moves a widget. Each change saves at once.

The Preview is the real tab, laid out at the width it has in your window now, then drawn small enough to show all of it. Nothing of the tab can be clicked there. Your widget shows live, outlined in blue. A line above says "Point at the widget to size or move it".

## Where it can go

A widget sits in a gap between the tab's own parts, never on one. On Home the parts are the greeting, the resume notice, what needs you, **Back to chat** and the box. On Activity they are the cards of the side column. Each gap is rows of 12 columns, and a widget takes a run of them anywhere in a row. Widgets in one row never overlap.

A new widget sits in a row of its own: under the box on Home, half the column wide; at the top of Activity's side column, the whole column wide.

## Move it

- **Drag it.** While you drag, every row shows its columns faintly, and a blue outline shows where it would land. Let go to put it there. **Esc** cancels.
- **Move here.** A dashed band sits in every gap it can move to. Click one to move it there.

## Size it

- **Width**: drag the right edge. It snaps 2 columns at a time.
- **Height**: drag the bottom edge. Until you set a height, the card is as tall as what the widget draws.
- **Both**: drag the corner. A label shows the new size, such as "8 cols × 200 px". **Esc** keeps the old size.

## The bar

Point at the widget, or focus it, and a small bar shows on it:

| Control | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| **⅓**, **½**, **Full** | Sets the width |
| The size ("6 cols × 144 px") | Its button lets the height follow the widget again ("6 cols × auto") |
| **To the left**, **To the middle**, **To the right** | Moves it within its row |
| **Move to the spot above** / **below** | Moves it to the next gap |

## Keyboard

Press Tab to focus the widget. ← and → move it one column; ↑ and ↓ move it to the gap above or below. With Shift, ← and → make it 2 columns narrower or wider, and ↑ and ↓ make it 8 px shorter or taller.

## Size limits

| Limit | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Narrowest | 160 px: a third of Home's column, half of Activity's side column |
| Widest | The whole row |
| Height | 96 to 480 px |
| Narrow column | Under 352 px, every widget takes the whole width, one under the other |

A new size is checked before it shows. Slate runs the widget once, unseen, at that size. Until it fits, the tab keeps the last size that fitted. If it does not fit, its Preview says "Doesn't fit at this size." with **Fix with AI**.

---

# Widget API

Source: https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/widgets/api.md

This is what a [widget](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/widgets.md) can import from Slate. Your agent gets the same API as TypeScript declarations from `get_widget`, and Slate type-checks every save against them, so a wrong call is an error at its file and line before the widget runs.

## Contents

- [The tools and the files](#the-tools-and-the-files)
- [Permissions and errors](#permissions-and-errors)
- [Reading](#reading) · [The tab it reads](#the-tab-it-reads) · [Lists from outside Slate](#lists-from-outside-slate) · [Your MCP tools](#your-mcp-tools)
- [Acting](#acting) · [Its own data and events](#its-own-data-and-events)
- [`@slate/sdk/react`](#slatesdkreact) · [`@slate/sdk/format`](#slatesdkformat) · [`@slate/ui`](#slateui)
- [The checks each version passes](#the-checks-each-version-passes)

## The tools and the files

An agent builds a widget with two MCP tools, both taking `widget_id`:

- `get_widget` returns the files, the `playbook` (the rules for building a widget), `sdk` (the whole API as declarations), `examples` (4 whole widgets: a sessions chart, a tasks list that adds a task, notes kept with `useStore`, a doc written from commits) and the workspace's other widgets by id and title.
- `publish_widget` sends the files and returns `render` ([below](#the-checks-each-version-passes)).

A widget is `index.html` with one `<script type="module" src="./App.tsx"></script>`, plus files ending in `.tsx .ts .jsx .js .css .json .md .svg`, in any folders, at most 300. It may import its own files and `react`, `react-dom/client`, `lucide-react`, `@slate/sdk`, `@slate/sdk/react`, `@slate/sdk/format` and `@slate/ui`.

`slate.json` says what it is and what it asks for:

```json
{
  "name": "Reviews",
  "place": "home",
  "sdk": 1,
  "permissions": [{ "use": "tasks.write", "why": "Move a review to tomorrow" }],
  "tools": [{ "tool": "linear__list_issues", "why": "Show my open issues" }]
}
```

- `place` is `"home"`, `"activity"` or `"sessions"`: the tab it shows on.
- `sdk` is the API version it was made for, now `1`. Within a version Slate only adds calls and parts.
- Every call that needs a permission must have it listed, and every listed permission must be used by a call. Either mistake is a build error at its line.

## Permissions and errors

| Permission | On screen |
| --- | --- |
| `workspace.read` | Read your workspace |
| `tasks.read` | Read your Tasks |
| `tasks.write` | Change your Tasks |
| `github.read` | Read your GitHub |
| `github.act` | Act on your GitHub |
| `memories.write` | Save memories |
| `docs.write` | Write docs |
| `routines.run` | Run automations |
| `sessions.start` | Open AI sessions |

A refused call throws `SlateError` with a `code`:

| Code | Means |
| --- | --- |
| `not_allowed` | `slate.json` does not list the permission, or the call needs the person's OK where no card can show |
| `not_granted` | Listed, but the person has not allowed it yet, or an MCP tool changed |
| `bad_request` | The arguments are wrong, or the target is not one the widget may touch |
| `failed` | Slate could not do it |
| `no_answer` | No answer came |
| `too_often` | Past a rate limit (toasts, GitHub actions) |
| `declined` | The person pressed **Not now** on the card |
| `busy` | Another card is waiting for the person's answer |

A call that needs the person's OK each time (`memories.save`, `docs.create`, `docs.append`, `routines.run`, `sessions.start` and every `github.*` action) shows Slate's card above the widget, on its tab and in the Widgets preview, and waits for the answer. It runs only on the person's yes. Where no card can show (a thumbnail, the render check), it is refused with `not_allowed`. A call needing a permission not yet allowed is refused with `not_granted`. Each message says what to do, so show it.

## Reading

Every read stays inside the widget's workspace. `since` is `"1d"`, `"7d"`, `"30d"` or `"90d"`. Lists come newest first, at most `limit` rows (default and maximum 5,000); pass the last row's time as `before` to read on.

| Call | Returns | Needs |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `slate.place.get()` | What the widget's tab shows now ([below](#the-tab-it-reads)) | — |
| `slate.project.get()` | Where the widget was made: a project, or the workspace (`kind`) | `workspace.read` |
| `slate.docs.list({ limit })` | The workspace's docs, each with its kind | `workspace.read` |
| `slate.docs.get(id)` | One doc with its text | `workspace.read` |
| `slate.memories.list({ limit })` | The workspace's memories, without those kept away from widgets | `workspace.read` |
| `slate.memories.search(text)` | The best matches, ranked like recall | `workspace.read` |
| `slate.sessions.list({ since, limit })` | AI sessions: tool, date, title, summary | `workspace.read` |
| `slate.sessions.count({ days })` | Sessions per day (default 7, at most 90) and per tool | `workspace.read` |
| `slate.sessions.live()` | Sessions running now; `status` is `working`, `needs_you` or `idle` | `workspace.read` |
| `slate.usage.list({ since, limit })` | Tool, model, time, prompts, tokens and cost per session (default 30 days) | `workspace.read` |
| `slate.receipts.list({ since, limit })` | Sessions that ran a check, changed a file or made a commit (default 7 days) | `workspace.read` |
| `slate.activity.list({ since, kinds, limit })` | Git activity (default 7 days); `kind` is `commit`, `branch.created`, `branch.switched`, `branch.deleted`, `staged` or `files.touched` | `workspace.read` |
| `slate.artifacts.list({ limit })` | The workspace's artifacts, each with a link | `workspace.read` |
| `slate.routines.list()` | The workspace's automations | `workspace.read` |
| `slate.tasks.list({ section, open })` | Items in Tasks; `open` defaults to true | `tasks.read` |

## The tab it reads

`slate.place.get()` takes no arguments; Slate fills in what the tab shows. Read again on `slate.on("place")`.

- **`activity`**: `{ place, from, to, days, project, sessions, memories }`. The sessions that started in the range and project picked in Activity, and the memories learned in the range (not narrowed to the project).
- **`home`**: `{ place, project, running, tasks, finished }`. Sessions running now, your open tasks, and receipts of sessions that finished in the last day. `tasks` is empty unless the widget lists `tasks.read` and the person allowed it.
- **`sessions`**: `{ place, session }`. The session open beside it, or `null`. `session` holds `tool`, `title`, `branch`, `status`, `lastActiveAt`, `project`, `githubRepo` ("owner/name" or `null`), and from the last week's usage `model`, `startedAt`, `activeMs`, `prompts`, `tokens` and `costUsd`, each `null` when not measured. To show the issues of the session's project, read `slate.sources.tasks({})` and keep rows whose `key` starts with `githubRepo` and `#`, ignoring case.

## Lists from outside Slate

A widget has no network. Slate reads outside lists itself, keeps the rows, and answers at once with `{ rows, fetchedAt, status, detail }`. `status` is `"ok"`, `"stale"` (Slate is reading again) or `"failed"` (`rows` are the last good ones). Hidden characters are removed from the rows. Read a source with `useSource` and show `SourceStatus` beside it.

| Call | Returns | Needs |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `slate.sources.tasks({ section, open })` | Items in Tasks, with when they last synced. `section` is `solve`, `review`, `reply` or `todo` | `tasks.read` |
| `slate.sources.reviews()` | Open pull requests waiting for your review, at most 50 | `github.read` |
| `slate.sources.pulls()` | Your own open pull requests | `github.read` |
| `slate.sources.repoPulls()` | Open pull requests in the workspace's projects, anyone's, at most 50. Slate picks the projects | `github.read` |
| `slate.sources.checks({ repo, number })` | The checks on one pull request from `reviews` or `pulls`; any other is `bad_request` | `github.read` |

GitHub is read with the workspace's `gh` sign-in. Slate keeps rows for 2 minutes, does not ask again within 20 seconds, and starts at most 12 GitHub reads a minute across all widgets; past that a read answers `"failed"` with the last rows.

## Your MCP tools

| Call | Returns |
| --- | --- |
| `slate.tools.list()` | The tools this widget may read through now: name, server, description, input schema |
| `slate.tools.read({ tool, args })` | One tool's answer as a source: `rows` holds one `{ text, truncated }` |

List each tool under `tools` in `slate.json` as `<server>__<tool>`, at most 20. The person allows each one, as read-only, with its switch in Widgets. A tool whose name says it writes (`create`, `update`, `send`…), or whose server marks it `readOnlyHint: false` or `destructiveHint: true`, is refused with `not_allowed`. If the tool's name, description, input schema or hints change, calls are refused with `not_granted` until the person allows it again.

`args` must match the tool's input schema and be at most 4,000 characters as JSON, or the call is `bad_request`. The answer is cut at 20,000 characters (`truncated: true`). Slate keeps an answer for 1 minute, does not repeat a call within 10 seconds, and allows each server 20 requests a minute from all widgets.

## Acting

| Call | Does | Needs |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `slate.tasks.create({ title, remindAt })` | Adds an item of your own; title at most 200 characters | `tasks.write` |
| `slate.tasks.remind(id, when)` | `"tomorrow"`, `"next-week"` (both 9:00) or an ISO time, for an item this widget made | `tasks.write` |
| `slate.tasks.done(id)` | Marks an item this widget made as done | `tasks.write` |
| `slate.memories.save({ text, kind })` | Saves a new memory, held until the person releases it | `memories.write` |
| `slate.docs.create({ title, text })` | A new doc in the widget's project (markdown) | `docs.write` |
| `slate.docs.append(id, text)` | Adds markdown to a doc in the widget's project | `docs.write` |
| `slate.routines.run(id)` | Runs an automation | `routines.run` |
| `slate.sessions.start({ prompt })` | Opens a session with the prompt typed in | `sessions.start` |
| `slate.github.approve({ repo, number })` | Approves a pull request waiting for your review | `github.act` |
| `slate.github.changes({ repo, number })` | Requests changes on one | `github.act` |
| `slate.github.comment({ repo, number })` | Comments on one from either list | `github.act` |
| `slate.github.label({ repo, number, label, remove })` | Adds an existing label, or removes one | `github.act` |
| `slate.ui.open(link)` | Opens `slate://doc?id=…`, `slate://task?id=…` or `slate://artifact?id=…` | `workspace.read` |
| `slate.ui.toast(text)` | A short note, at most one a second, 200 characters | — |

The calls that need the person's OK wait for their card ([above](#permissions-and-errors)). `sessions.start` opens on the project the tab shows and fails without one. A GitHub action is limited to 5 an hour per widget and 20 for all widgets, and the words are always the person's, never the widget's. Text a widget writes is `bad_request` if it holds invisible characters such as zero-width or direction-changing ones.

## Its own data and events

`slate.store.get(key)`, `set(key, value)`, `delete(key)` and `keys()` keep the widget's data on this computer, never synced, at most 1 MB in all.

`slate.on(area, fn)` calls `fn` when data changes in `"docs"`, `"memories"`, `"tasks"`, `"sessions"` or `"activity"`, or `"changed"` for any change. `"place"` fires when the tab shows another range, project or session. It returns a function that stops listening.

## `@slate/sdk/react`

| Hook | Does |
| --- | --- |
| `useQuery(load, deps, { on })` | `{ data, loading, error, refresh }`, keeping the last answer while it reads again. Rereads on `docs`, `memories` and `tasks` by default; `on` replaces that list |
| `useSource(load, deps, { on })` | For `slate.sources.*` and `slate.tools.read`: `{ rows, fetchedAt, status, detail, loading, error, refresh }`. While `"stale"` it asks again every 1.5 seconds, up to 8 times |
| `useStore(key, initial)` | `[value, setValue]` for one value of its own data |

## `@slate/sdk/format`

`dayOf(at)` and `lastDays(n)` give "YYYY-MM-DD" days, the keys `sessions.count` uses. `dayLabel(day)` gives "Mon 12". `duration(ms)` gives "45s", "12m", "3h 20m". `compact(n)` gives "940", "12.4k", "1.2M". `money(usd)` gives "$3.10" or "<$0.01". `count(n, "session")` gives "1 session" or "3 sessions". `timeZone()` gives the person's time zone.

## `@slate/ui`

### The card

The root is always `<Widget>`. It takes the look of the tab it sits on, so a widget never styles its own card. Lay it out with these; each takes `hideBelow="medium"` or `"wide"`:

- `Widget`: the root; `gap` is 1 to 4.
- `Stack`: parts one under another (`grow`, `gap`, `align`, `justify`). `Inline`: side by side (`wrap`).
- `Panel`: a quiet section. `Divider`: a line (`vertical` in an `Inline`).
- `Fit`: the focal element, scaled to the room left. Give its child a size (`<svg width={120} height={120} viewBox="0 0 100 100">`).
- `Metric` (`size` `md`, `lg`, `xl`), `Label` and `Caption`: all text.
- `useCard()`: the card's `width`, `height` and `size` (`"small"` under 260 px, `"wide"` from 420 px, else `"medium"`).

### Colours

`color` holds the theme's colours: `text`, `muted`, `surface`, `bg`, `border`, `hover`, `accent`, `accentText`, `ok`, `attention`, `bad`, and `chart` (5 colours). As CSS: `var(--text)` … `var(--bad)`, `var(--accent-text)`, and `var(--c1)` to `var(--c5)`. They follow light and dark.

### Parts

- Rows: `Card`, `Row`, `Header`, `SectionLabel`
- A read's state: `QueryView` (for `useQuery`: waiting, error with Retry, empty, or your view) and `SourceStatus` (for `useSource`)
- Charts: `BarList`, `Sparkline`, `StatCard`, `RankedList`
- Controls: `Button`, `IconButton`, `Input`, `Textarea`, `Select`, `Checkbox`, `Switch`, `Segmented`
- Display: `Badge`, `Chip`, `Avatar`, `Kbd`, `When`
- States: `Callout`, `EmptyState`, `ErrorState`, `Loading`, `Spinner`, `Skeleton`, `SkeletonLines`

## The checks each version passes

**The build** refuses, at its file and line: a colour, text size or font written by hand (hex, `rgb()`, a colour name, a raw palette step like `var(--n-500)`), a size read from the window (`vh`, `vw`, `h-screen`, `window.innerWidth`), `position: fixed`, `Page`, `Section` or `Grid`, and a root that is not `<Widget>`.

**The render check** then runs the version once, hidden, with no network. Writes and outside reads get no answer. It fails when the widget throws, when a call is refused with `not_allowed`, `bad_request` or `failed`, or when nothing shows within 10 seconds. `not_granted` does not fail it. A widget that drew is run again in 3 boxes at its height (480 px while its height follows it): its own width, the narrowest its tab allows, and the whole row. It fails as `clipped` if its content is taller or wider than a box, or cut off inside it. So lay it out with `Stack` and `Inline`, and put the focal element in `Fit`.

`render.status` is `ok`, `failed` or `pending` (no window has run it yet; call `get_widget` later). On `failed`, each of `problems` has `kind` (`threw`, `refused`, `blank` or `clipped`), `call`, `code`, `errorClass`, `file` and `line`, and for `clipped` a `fit` with `span`, `width`, `height`, `what` (`height`, `width` or `inside`), `measured` and `allowed` in px. `next` says the fix in one line.

```tsx
import { createRoot } from "react-dom/client";
import { slate } from "@slate/sdk";
import { useQuery } from "@slate/sdk/react";
import { BarList, Label, QueryView, Widget } from "@slate/ui";

function Week() {
  const week = useQuery(() => slate.sessions.count({ days: 7 }));
  return (
    <Widget>
      <Label>AI sessions this week</Label>
      <QueryView query={week} isEmpty={(d) => d.total === 0} empty="No AI sessions this week.">
        {(d) => <BarList rows={d.byDay.map((x) => ({ label: x.day, value: x.count }))} />}
      </QueryView>
    </Widget>
  );
}

createRoot(document.getElementById("root")!).render(<Week />);
```

This example needs `workspace.read` in `slate.json`.

---

# Automations

Source: https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/automations.md

An **automation** is a process you define once and let run without you: a morning brief at 8:30, a fix for an issue, a review of a pull request. Automations holds yours, the reports they write, and the things Slate runs on its own.

## The Automations place

The side panel lists, from the top:

- **Overview**: **Latest**, the newest report of each automation and every run on an item from the last 14 days, newest first. A report opens that automation's thread at that run; a run on an item opens on its task.
- **Built-in**: what Slate runs on its own, each with a switch ([Built-in automations](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/automations/built-in.md)).
- **Running**: automations working now.
- **On a schedule**: automations that take nothing, each with its time ("Daily 3 AM") or **By hand**.
- **Flows**: automations that take an item, each with what it takes ("A pull request").

With no automation yet, the main area shows **Start with Slate's automations**: the [starters](#the-starters), each with **Add**. When the project has skills that match a starter, a line offers **Use them**.

## Make an automation

1. Click **+** in the side panel and pick **From a template**, **Set it up yourself** or **Describe it to AI…**. The template gallery opens with **Describe it** first, then 15 templates such as **Standup**, **Weekly review** and **PR review prep**.
2. Fill the three parts: **When**, **Do** and **In**.
3. Press **Save**. Nothing is saved before that.

| Part | You set |
| --- | --- |
| **When** | **Takes**: **Nothing**, **A pull request**, **An issue**, **A ticket**, **A question** or **A message**. Then **Runs**: for nothing, **When you run it**, **Daily** or **Weekly**; for an item, **When you run it** or **On every new one**. |
| **Do** | The **Job** in your words, then the steps as plain lines (**Step** adds one). Type **@** to add a doc, session, memory, task, artifact, file or report. |
| **In** | The **Project** (a group or a project), the **Agent**, and which connected apps it **May use**. |

A schedule reads as one sentence: "Runs every weekday at 8 AM :30". Choose every day, every weekday (Monday to Friday), every week or every month (day 1 to 28), at :00, :15, :30 or :45. A line under it says the next run, such as "Next: Mon 7:30 AM".

An automation cannot run without a project: the project gives it its folder, account and model. Until you pick one, **In** says **Pick a project**.

## The starters

Slate offers 8 starters. Each is plain steps any agent can follow, and you can change them.

| Starter | Takes | Does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Code Review** | A pull request | Reads it, checks the project's rules, runs the checks, writes the review |
| **Fix a bug** | An issue | Reproduces it, finds the cause, writes a failing test, fixes it, opens a pull request |
| **Implement** | A ticket | Plans, builds in small steps, tests each step, opens a pull request |
| **Research** | A question | Looks it up in the code and docs, writes a finding, changes nothing |
| **Answer review** | Your pull request | Changes the code or replies to each comment, runs the checks, pushes |
| **Draft a reply** | A message | Looks up what it needs, drafts a reply, sends only when you approve |
| **Morning brief** | Nothing | Every weekday at 08:30: what moved yesterday and what waits for you |
| **Tidy memories** | Nothing | Every night at 02:00: merges repeated memories and retires stale ones |

A run on an item stops for you at **Approve plan** and **Approve to ship** where its steps have them. No starter merges by itself.

### Defaults stay

The first automation you add from each of the six item starters is a **default**: Tasks runs it. You can edit a default, but it has no **Delete forever**. A second copy of the same starter is your own and has **Delete forever**, and so do **Morning brief** and **Tidy memories**.

You do not have to add the defaults first. A task's **Run** menu offers the starters that take it, and the first run adds that starter here ([Tasks](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/tasks.md)). An edited starter says **Slate's starter · edited by you**.

### A project skill can replace the steps

If the project keeps a skill for the same work (for example `fix-bug` or `code-review`), the automation can follow it instead of Slate's steps. Under **Do**, press **Use a skill instead** and pick it. Every step then opens the skill's file and follows it. **Use Slate's steps** switches back. If the skill leaves the project, the plain steps run until you pick another.

## What starts a run

| Starts | How |
| --- | --- |
| **By hand** | **Run now** on an automation that takes nothing. You can type what it starts with first. |
| **On a schedule** | At its time, while Slate runs. A computer asleep at that time runs it once on waking. |
| **On an item** | **Run** on a task in Tasks or Home, or your agent naming the item. |
| **On every new one** | New items arriving in Tasks, of the kind the automation takes: a pull-request automation does not start on a new issue. |

A flow (an automation that takes an item) runs only on an item. It has no **Run now** and no on/off switch. Opened, it shows its steps with their stops, the skill it follows, and **Runs**: each run with its item, where it stands and when.

Your agent can also start an automation from any tool, with Slate's `run_automation` tool ([MCP tool reference](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/mcp-server/tools.md)). Making or changing one happens only here.

An automation runs on the computer where it was made, in its project's folder. Automations do not sync, so in a shared workspace a teammate has no copy to run. One automation runs one run at a time.

## The preflight check

Before **Save** and before every run, Slate checks that the run can start: it has a project, its agent is added in Connect, the project's folder exists, and you allowed the project's own hooks. When something blocks, one sentence and a button that fixes it show in the editor and under **Run now**, and the run does not start.

## What it may do

An automation uses the tools its agent reaches, such as your Jira, GitHub or Slack MCP servers, and the apps you connected in [Connect](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/connect/integrations.md).

- **Reading goes on without asking**: searching, listing, opening a ticket or pull request.
- **A call that changes something asks first**: posting a message, commenting, creating an issue.
- **Merging, removing things and writing files are refused.**

### When it asks first

A held call does not stop the run: the run carries on and says what it wanted. When the run ends, the call waits as an **Ask first** card under that run and on [Home](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/home.md). **Yes, do it** starts one short run allowed exactly that call, and the card then says "Done: …" or "Not made: …". **No** closes it. On Home, **Later** sets it aside.

Next: [The thread and reports](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/automations/thread.md) · [Recent tasks](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/automations/recent-tasks.md) · [Built-in automations](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/automations/built-in.md)

---

# The thread and reports

Source: https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/automations/thread.md

Every run of an automation that takes nothing writes one **report**, and the reports collect in the automation's **Thread**. Open an automation under **On a schedule** to read it. Above its tabs sit **Run now**, **Edit**, **Turn off** or **Turn on**, and **Last run**.

It has three tabs: **Thread**, **Setup** and **What it knows**.

## Read the thread

The thread lists every run, oldest first. Words you typed sit above the answer they started. Under each run, one line says what it used ("Used jira ×2, github") and how many calls wait for you. A report over 1,600 characters shows its opening; **Read the whole report** opens it.

## Answer the last run

Type in the box under the thread and press **Send**. Slate runs once more on the same agent and folder, with your words, the last 4 turns, and each earlier report cut to its first 3,000 characters.

Before the first run the box holds what the run starts with, and the button says **Start**. **Run now** starts with nothing typed. The box is off while the automation runs or when it cannot run.

## The receipt

Each report carries a receipt: what the run really did, read from the run's own output, never written by the agent. It says **Proved**, with the checks, changed files and commits it counted, or **No evidence**, with the reason.

## Setup and What it knows

**Setup** shows how the automation is set up: its **Job**, when it starts and runs next, where it works, its **Agent**, what it **May do**, and its **Steps**. Change it with **Edit**.

**What it knows** shows:

- **What it wrote to memory**: the memories its runs wrote. A run writes to memory only when its first step is [Recent tasks](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/automations/recent-tasks.md) with writing back on.
- The memories it will be given on the next run, each of which you can pin or keep out.
- **What each run reads**: its job, sessions from the last 7 days (or the days its first step sets), the memories of its project or group, its own last 3 reports, and your replies in this thread.

## When a run ends

- A finished run sends a system notification with the report's opening line, cut at 180 characters, and a **Report ready** toast.
- A failed run shows an **Automation failed** toast, and the error stays under **Last run**.
- If your agent is signed out, the toast says so; sign in again from the automation.

Delete a report with **Delete forever**. Reports do not go to Trash. An automation removed with **Delete forever** keeps its reports in Automations. Press **⌘K** to search reports by title and text.

## Limits

Every background run keeps these limits:

| Limit | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Spend per run | $5, shared by all its turns |
| Turns, for an agent that does not report spend | 12 |
| Tool turns inside one Claude Code turn | 30 |
| Silence before a turn gives up | 4 minutes (any output restarts the clock) |

If Slate stops in the middle of a run, the run is marked failed, and a scheduled one runs again soon after.

---

# Recent tasks

Source: https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/automations/recent-tasks.md

**Recent tasks** is the first step of a scheduled [automation](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/automations.md) such as **Standup**, **Weekly review** or **Memory pass**. It gathers what happened in your sessions, then checks it against your live tools, so the report says what is true today.

Only the first step can be Recent tasks, because every later step reads its report. **Setup** shows it as "Recent tasks · looks back 7 days".

## What it reads

| Source | What comes in |
| --- | --- |
| Sessions | The newest 80 captured sessions in the look-back window (7 days unless the step sets 1 to 365), each tagged with its project and summed up in one line of at most 280 characters |
| Memories | Up to 30 memories, the same ones **What it knows** previews. Never a hidden memory |
| Docs | The titles of up to 100 docs in its project or group, newest change first |
| Its own reports | Its last 3 reports, the first 600 characters of each |

## Checking your live tools

A stored record shows what was true when it was written, so Recent tasks asks your tools first. It picks up to 3 of the folders the period's sessions worked in, and runs one short pass of your agent in each, so the project's own MCP servers load. Each pass checks, in order:

1. Jira or Linear: the issues assigned to you that are not done.
2. GitHub: your pull requests for those issues, with their state, checks and who the review waits on.
3. Calendar: today's meetings, unless Slate already read them.
4. Slack: who is waiting on what for those issues and pull requests, over about the last 3 days.

A pass asks only for keys, states, names and times. It never asks for issue text, comments or message text.

## The report

A Recent tasks report opens with three columns: **Assigned to me**, **Pull requests** and **Today's meetings**. A pull request shows its full name, such as `acme/api#12`.

- A tool that needs you to sign in shows a sign-in button, then runs the automation again.
- A tool it could not reach says so, instead of "Nothing assigned."

The text then lists what was checked in this run and which tools could not be reached.

## Writing to memory

When the step has writing back on, as **Memory pass** does, the run can save up to 5 new memories, and merge or retire the memories it was shown. Each change shows in Memory with an **Undo**. Only an automation that works in a project or group can merge or retire.

## Prompt variables

Type these in the Recent tasks prompt. Slate fills them in just before the run. Another step cannot use them, and Save says so.

| Variable | Becomes |
| --- | --- |
| `@sessions` | The sessions above |
| `@memory` | The memories above, each with its kind and reason |
| `@docs` | The doc titles above |
| `@date` | Today's date |
| `@prior_outputs` | Its own last reports |

---

# Built-in automations

Source: https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/automations/built-in.md

**Built-in**, the second row in the [Automations](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/automations.md) side panel, lists everything Slate does without being asked, each with a switch. Every row says what it does, and an "Off." line says what you lose while it is off.

Every switch holds for the whole app, in every workspace on this computer, except **AI memory care**, which holds for the open workspace only.

## The switches

| Switch | What it does | Off means | Starts |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Scheduled automations** | Starts your automations at their times and files each report under its group or project | Nothing starts on its own; you can still run automations by hand | On |
| **Shared workspace sync** | Every 2 minutes, pushes the docs you wrote in a shared workspace and pulls other people's | Shared workspaces stop updating both ways | On |
| **Automatic updates** | Checks for a new version, downloads it, and installs it when you quit | You keep your version until you check in Settings → About | On |
| **Tell me when a session needs me** | One notification when a session starts waiting on your answer and Slate is not in front | No notification; the amber dot and ⌘⇧J still show it | On |
| **Show Slate in the menu bar** | A menu bar icon lists the sessions working or waiting on you, with a count while one needs you | The icon leaves; Sessions and ⌘⇧J still show every session | On |
| **Start Slate at login** | Starts Slate in the menu bar at login, with no window | Slate starts only when you open it, and your agents cannot reach it before | Your choice at setup |
| **Auto-capture** | Watches your agents' transcripts and your projects, and files what happens into the workspace that owns the folder | Nothing is captured on its own; agents can still write through Slate's MCP server | On |
| **Agent runs** | Lets you start an agent run on a task, and every 2 minutes checks whether a shipped run's pull request merged | A task offers only **Just open a session** | On |
| **Reminders** | Rings when a task you set a time on comes due | Nothing rings; the times stay on their tasks | On |
| **Keep the computer awake** | Stops the computer sleeping while a session or automation works | The computer sleeps on schedule, and running work pauses | Off |
| **AI memory care** | [Below](#ai-memory-care) | Only the free rules tidy memory; nothing is spent | Off |

**Auto-capture** has a card at the top as well as its row; both are one switch. Each agent also has its own **Capture** switch in [Connect → Agents](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/connect.md).

A switch takes effect within about a minute; **Auto-capture** at once.

## AI memory care

Each night at 03:00, while the computer is awake and Slate is open, your agent reads up to 50 memories the free rules cannot judge. It reads each one twice, separately, against the code the memory cites.

- A memory both readings call wrong is retired. You can bring it back from Memory.
- A memory they disagree on waits for you in Memory → **Needs review**, at most 10 at once.
- A missed night is skipped.

Its card shows what it reads, which agent and profile it runs on, and what the first month costs. Choose a **Monthly cap** of 1 million, 4 million or **No cap**, then **Turn on**. It stops for the month at the cap. It uses your agent's tokens; on a plan, the same allowance as your own sessions. It runs as an automation named **AI memory care**, so **Scheduled automations** must be on.

## Starting at login

Your agents reach Slate's memory, skills and connections only while Slate runs. Starting at login keeps it reachable.

- **Only if you choose it.** Setup offers it ticked on the **Agents** step. If you skipped that step, Slate asks once, in a strip at the top of the window: **Turn on** or **Not now**.
- **It is a macOS login item**, listed under Slate's name in **System Settings → General → Login Items**. If macOS waits for your approval, the row says so, with **Open Login Items**.
- **No window.** A login start shows only the menu bar icon. The Dock icon, the menu bar panel or a `slate://` link opens the window. If you are signed out, the window opens at once.
- **Managed Macs.** When your organization sets it, the row says **Managed by your organization** and the switch is locked ([Managed Macs](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/privacy-and-security/security-details.md#managed-macs)).
- **Updates still arrive.** With **Automatic updates** on, Slate checks 10 minutes after a login start, then every 4 hours, and installs when it quits or you log out.

## Keeping the computer awake

The computer stays awake only while there is work: a session that is working, a running automation, or a turn of Slate's own agent. A session that only waits on you does not count. The screen can still turn off, and you can still put the computer to sleep yourself.

The **coffee cup** in the top bar is the same switch. While it holds, it says why, such as "Holding now — 1 session working, 1 automation running".

## What reaches the network

- **Slate's own account**: the update check and shared workspace sync ([Privacy and security](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/privacy-and-security.md)).
- **Your agent, under its own sign-in**: scheduled automations, runs on an item, agent runs and AI memory care.
- **Your own `gh` or `glab`**: the agent run merge check.

Turning a switch off removes nothing: captured sessions stay, and shared docs stay shared.

---

# Toolkit

Source: https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/toolkit.md

**Toolkit** shows everything your agents read in a project: skills, commands, subagents, rules, instructions, MCP servers, hooks, plugins, output styles and config files. Each agent keeps these in its own folders and formats. Toolkit puts them on one screen, says which agents read each one, and suggests what to fix.

## Pick what to look at

The picker at the top of the side panel offers:

- **All projects**: Toolkit's **Overview**. A card for **User** and for every project, with what its agents read and how many [suggestions](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/toolkit/suggestions.md) wait there. A card opens that project.
- **User** `~`: what your agents keep in your home folder and load in every project ([User](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/toolkit/edit-and-remove.md#user)).
- **Each project with a folder**: a project by its name, a group's projects under the group's name.

## The tabs

A project opens on **Suggestions** while some wait, and on **Skills** otherwise. Each tab shows its count, and an empty one keeps a **New …** button.

| Tab | Loaded when |
| --- | --- |
| **Suggestions** | Changes to your AI setup, from what your sessions did ([Suggestions](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/toolkit/suggestions.md)) |
| **Skills** | The task matches what the skill says it is for |
| **Commands** | You type `/name` in a session |
| **Subagents** | A session hands work to one |
| **Rules** | The file an agent works on matches the rule |
| **Instructions** | The start of every session, always |
| **MCP servers** | One row per server, across your agents |
| **Hooks** | Your agents run them on an event |
| **Plugins** | The project turns them on |
| **Output styles** | They set how Claude Code answers |
| **Config files** | Each agent's own config file |

Slate reads each agent's own folders in the project, sub-packages included, so a skill in `.claude/skills` and one in `.agents/skills` show on one list.

## Suggestions

**Suggestions** lists changes to the project's AI setup, worst first, each with one button: a server that keeps failing, a skill one of your agents cannot see, one nobody runs. Nothing changes until you click. The rail shows how many wait. See [Suggestions](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/toolkit/suggestions.md).

## Read a row

- **Agent marks**: each agent that reads the item, in the same order on every row. An agent this workspace is not connected to is greyed and says **not connected in this workspace**. **No agent reads it** shows when none does.
- **this computer only**: a personal file, such as `settings.local.json`.
- **Usage**: how often the item ran in the last 30 days, such as **ran 4×** ([Usage, changes and sync](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/toolkit/usage-and-sync.md)).
- **A broken file**: a config file that does not parse is listed with the reason and what its agent does, such as "Gemini refuses to start in this project."

Click a row to open its file ([Editing and removing](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/toolkit/edit-and-remove.md)). Press **+** in the side panel to add one ([Adding items](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/toolkit/adding.md)).

## Write once with `.slate/`

A project can keep its skills and instructions once, in `.slate/`, and let Slate publish them to every agent you pick:

- `AGENTS.md` holds the instructions every agent reads. `CLAUDE.md` becomes a link to it.
- `.slate/skills/` holds one folder per skill. Slate links each agent's skills folder to it.
- `.slate/config.toml` lists the agents and the MCP servers to publish.

Slate writes each agent's files in its own shape, such as `.claude/skills/` and `.mcp.json` for Claude Code, or `.cursor/rules/slate.mdc` for Cursor, and lists them in a Slate block of `.gitignore`. A generated file opens read-only: edit `.slate/` instead. Its first comment says to change it in Toolkit, then press **Sync now**. The **sync pill** in the toolbar says whether every agent matches ([Usage, changes and sync](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/toolkit/usage-and-sync.md#the-sync-pill)).

Slate never writes through a link that leads out of the project, and never replaces a real file where a link should go. It skips that file, names it, and still writes the rest.

When `.slate/` lists MCP servers, **Sync now** also writes them into the Claude Desktop config and `~/.cursor/mcp.json`, which every project shares. Taking a server out of `.slate/` removes it from every file on the next sync, unless you changed that entry yourself.

A project without `.slate/` offers **Start using .slate** ([Start using .slate](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/toolkit/start-using-slate.md)).

Edits made in Toolkit are committed in **Projects → Code → Changes**. The accounts your agents run under are set in Connect ([Project environments](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/toolkit/project-environments.md)).

---

# Adding items in Toolkit

Source: https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/toolkit/adding.md

Press **+** in the [Toolkit](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/toolkit.md) side panel to add an item. On a tab it opens that kind's form, such as **New skill** on **Skills**. From **All projects**, it first asks where the item goes: **User** or one project.

Where an item can live in several places, the form shows a card for each place with the agents that read it. Tick one or more. A line under the cards names every agent that will read it. **Create** writes the files; **Cancel** writes nothing.

## Skill

Give it a name (lower case letters, digits and dashes, such as `review-pr`), what it does and when an agent should use it, and where it goes.

- With `.slate/` in the project, **Every agent: written once, published to each** puts it in `.slate/skills/`, with a group and a blank file or a copy of another skill to start from. The other places are then already covered.
- Without `.slate/`, pick the agents' folders, such as `.claude/skills` or `.agents/skills`. The skill is written once and the other folders link to it.

**Who starts it**: **You or the AI**, **Only you** or **Only the AI**. Claude Code reads this; the other agents let both start a skill.

## Command, subagent, rule, output style

Each takes a name, a few fields, and the agents' folders. The **Writes** box shows each file's header in its agent's own format before you press **Create**.

- **Command**: a description, and an **Argument hint** for Claude Code.
- **Subagent**: **When to hand work to it**, a **Model** (**Same as the session**, **Fast** or **Strongest**), and **Tools it can use** (**All**, **Read only**, or picked from **Read files**, **Search**, **Edit files**, **Run commands** and **Web**). Each agent gets its own model name, such as Claude Code's haiku or opus. OpenCode keeps the session's model.
- **Rule**: **When it applies**: **Always**, **When files match** (patterns such as `packages/server/**`), **When relevant** or **Only when mentioned**. Claude Code reads a rule only always or by files, so the last two leave it out. A Codex rule is a command policy: its first words, a **Decision** (**Allow**, **Ask first** or **Forbid**) and **Why**.
- **Output style**: a description and **Keep coding instructions**. On, the style adds to Claude Code's coding instructions; off, it replaces them.

## Instructions, MCP server, hook, plugin

- **Instructions**: the instructions files the project does not have yet.
- **MCP server**: a name, a **Command or URL**, environment variables (one `NAME=value` a line), and the agents to **Add it to**. Each ticked agent shows the file it goes in. The variables are stored as plain text in files at the project's root, which are often committed, so keep real keys out of them.
- **Hook**: the **Agent** (Claude Code, Gemini, Cursor or Qwen Code), an **Event**, an optional **Matcher** such as `Bash|Edit`, the **Command**, and a timeout (seconds or milliseconds, as the agent counts). A Claude Code hook can stay **Only on this computer**.
- **Plugin**: its name as the agent names it (`name@marketplace` for Claude Code and Codex, an npm name for OpenCode), and the agents to **Turn it on for**. Installing it stays the agent's own command.

---

# Edit and remove

Source: https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/toolkit/edit-and-remove.md

Part of [Toolkit](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/toolkit.md). Click a row to open its file.

## Edit a file

A markdown file opens drawn: its header fields on top, its text below, with a **Preview** / **Markdown** switch. A rule, subagent, command or output style shows the same fields as its New form.

- A choice saves at once. Text saves when you stop typing, on ⌘S, or when you quit. A failed save says **Not saved** with the reason.
- Only the keys a field writes change. Other keys, comments and their order stay.
- A header that does not parse hides the fields until you fix it in the text.
- A config file that would no longer parse for its agent is not saved.
- A file Slate generates from `.slate/` opens **Read-only**: edit `.slate/` instead.
- A file that is a link out of the project is neither shown nor saved.

## A `.slate/` skill

A `.slate/` skill opens with its name, the agents that read it, and a **More** (⋯) menu: **Rename…**, **Duplicate…**, **Copy to project…**, **History** (restore the file from any commit) and **Remove…**. A skill can hold more than one file; **Add a file** adds one.

The agents control says **Published to 3 of 5**. It opens **Choose the agents that read this**: **All installed agents**, then **Installed** and a folded **Not installed** group, with a search box. An agent with no skills folder is greyed and says so. A new skill goes to every installed agent.

When two agents keep different files under one skill name, the row says **2 copies**. Open it to compare them, then press **Use this copy for all agents**.

## Remove an item

The trash button asks first: **Remove {name}?**, with **Keep it** or **Remove {name}**, and names the files and agents it reaches.

| Kind | Removing it |
| --- | --- |
| Skill | Removes it from every agent folder that keeps it, links included. A `.slate/` skill can be brought back with **Discard** in **Projects → Code → Changes** until you commit |
| Subagent, rule, output style, command | Removes its file |
| MCP server | Removes its entry from every agent's file; the files stay |
| Hook | Removes every hook with that name; the file stays |
| Plugin | Turns it off |
| Instructions, Config files | Never removed here |

## An MCP server's dialog

An **MCP servers** row opens a dialog that lists every agent with the server, with **Remove from {agent}**, and every connected agent without it, with **Add to {agent}**. It also says when a server will not load yet: Claude Code waits for your approval, and Codex reads it only in a project it trusts. Slate never approves a server for you. When the other agent has no place for a setting, the copy says which ones it left out. Environment variables and headers never show on screen.

## User

**User** `~` lists what your agents keep in your home folder and load in every project, on the same tabs.

- Chips at the top of each tab pick one profile, such as `~/.codex`, or one plugin, with its count.
- **New skill** goes into the skills folder of the Claude Code profile this workspace uses, into `~/.agents/skills` (read by Codex, Gemini, OpenCode and Cursor), or both.
- **+** adds to the picked profile on every tab where its agent keeps that kind.
- Removing an item says that every project on this computer stops seeing it. A removed file goes to the Trash.
- A skill or command that a plugin supplies has no trash button: remove the plugin.

Toolkit reads only the profiles the workspace uses, or every profile on this computer when it names none. Claude Code's own user MCP servers live in a file that also holds its sign-in, so Toolkit never opens it; add them with `claude mcp add --scope user`.

---

# Usage, changes and sync

Source: https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/toolkit/usage-and-sync.md

Part of [Toolkit](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/toolkit.md).

## How often each item ran

Rows on **Skills**, **Commands**, **Subagents** and **MCP servers** show how often the item ran in this project's sessions in the last 30 days, such as **ran 4×**, then **1 failed** or **1 stopped by you**. Point at it to see the runs per agent.

| The row says | When |
| --- | --- |
| **not run in 30 days** | Nobody used it |
| **not run since** a date | Slate has fewer than 30 days of sessions |
| **not recorded yet** | No session in this project has ended since |
| **not measured** | The agents that read it do not record when it runs |

| Kind | Counted for |
| --- | --- |
| Skills | Every agent |
| Commands | Claude Code |
| Subagents | Claude Code |
| MCP servers | Claude Code and Codex |

Slate counts from each session's transcript when the session ends, on this computer, with no model call. A session in a worktree counts for its project.

After you accept an **Improve** suggestion, pointing at the row compares the 30 days before with the 30 days after, such as "The 30 days before: ran 6×, 4 stopped by you."

## The changes chip

When Toolkit changed files that are not committed, the toolbar says **3 changes to commit in Code**. Click it to open **Projects → Code → Changes** on that project. Files that can hold secrets or local paths, such as `.mcp.json` or `.claude/settings.json`, are listed unticked; tick one only to commit it. **User** has no chip, because your home folder is not in git.

## The sync pill

In a project with `.slate/`, the toolbar pill says whether every agent matches it: **In sync**, or **1 agent behind**. Click it for the agents that need a sync and what is off, such as **Skills changed**, with **Check again** and **Sync now**.

Slate syncs by itself shortly after `.slate/`, `AGENTS.md` or `CLAUDE.md` changes, whoever changed it: you, an agent, a terminal or `git pull`. Editing a skill needs no sync, because the agents read it through links. Adding, removing or renaming a skill, or changing the config or the instructions, does.

This automatic sync writes only inside the project, and only in a project you added or set up with `.slate/`. A project Slate only found inside a group's folder syncs when you press **Sync now**. **Sync now** also writes `.slate/`'s MCP servers into the Claude Desktop and Cursor configs every project shares.

A sync or check that has not finished after 60 seconds is stopped, with everything it started, and Toolkit says it timed out.

---

# Suggestions

Source: https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/toolkit/suggestions.md

**Suggestions** in [Toolkit](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/toolkit.md) lists changes to a project's AI setup, drawn from what your sessions did in the last 30 days, worst first. Nothing changes until you click.

Each suggestion says what was counted and has one button, plus **Dismiss** (**Keep** for a removal). A dismissed suggestion never comes back. An accepted **Fix** or **Improve** can come back after 30 days.

Toolkit's **Overview** (under **All projects**) shows how many suggestions wait in each project, and Toolkit's rail entry shows the total.

## The five kinds

| Kind | Suggested when | The button |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Fix** | An MCP server failed 3 of its last 5 calls. It shows the last error | **Open server** |
| **Copy** | A skill or MCP server ran here, and an agent you used in 3 or more sessions here cannot see it | **Add for {agent}** links the skill into a folder that agent reads, or copies the server into its file |
| **New** | You gave a general subagent the same task in 3 sessions, or typed a `/command` with nothing behind it in 3 sessions | **Create it** opens the New form |
| **Improve** | You typed a skill's `/name` 3 times and the agent never picked it by itself, or you stopped it 3 times | **Open it** |
| **Remove** | It did not run in 20 or more sessions of the agents that load it, counted from when its file was made | **Remove** takes it out of every folder and file that keeps it |

A lesson that Memory proposes as a skill also waits here, as **New**, with **Make it a skill**. Accepting it in either place writes it once.

## How it counts

- Slate counts when you open Suggestions, at most once an hour per project, and adds at most 3 new suggestions a day. No model runs.
