- **Remove** shows only when every agent that loads the item records when it runs, so an item an agent cannot measure is never called unused.
- **Copy** and **Remove** of a skill are not suggested in a project with `.slate/`, which decides each skill's agents.

## From an agent

An agent can propose a change with Slate's `propose_setup_change` tool: a fix, copy, new item, improvement or removal of a skill, command, subagent or MCP server, with a reason. It waits here beside Slate's own, outside the 3-a-day limit, and nothing is written until you accept it. An instructions file such as `CLAUDE.md` is never removed by a suggestion.

---

# Start using .slate

Source: https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/toolkit/start-using-slate.md

A project without `.slate/` offers **Start using .slate** at the top of its [Toolkit](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/toolkit.md) tab: "Write each skill once, for every agent." With `.slate/`, each skill is kept once and published to every agent you pick.

Press it, and Slate first says what it will do:

- create `.slate/config.toml`, listing the agents and every skill;
- move each skill from the agents' own folders, such as `.claude/skills` and `.agents/skills`, into `.slate/skills/`, and link each agent's folder back to it. Where two agents keep different copies, you pick which one stays;
- make the instructions one file:
  - with neither file, it creates `AGENTS.md`, the instructions every agent reads;
  - with `AGENTS.md` and a `CLAUDE.md` of its own, it adds `CLAUDE.md`'s text to the end of `AGENTS.md` and makes `CLAUDE.md` a link to it;
  - with only `CLAUDE.md`, that stays the real file and `AGENTS.md` becomes the link;
- leave each MCP server where it is, in its agent's own file.

Under **Publish to**, pick the agents.

## What it protects

- **Nothing is committed.** **Projects → Code → Changes** shows every file, and **Discard** brings any of them back.
- **A copy before removing.** Before it removes a skill folder or a `CLAUDE.md` that git does not track, Slate copies it to `slate-adopt/` in the project's git folder. That copy is never committed.
- **Nothing outside the project.** A link inside a skill folder is skipped and listed, never followed, so a file such as a key in `~/.ssh` is never copied in. A skill whose folder is outside the project is not moved, and a `.slate` that is a link is refused.
- **Links become files first.** An `AGENTS.md` that is a link becomes a real file with the same text.

---

# Project environments

Source: https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/toolkit/project-environments.md

Each agent keeps a config folder with its sign-in, settings and history. The folder a session uses decides whose account touched the code. Slate sets that account per **workspace**, and a group, or a project on its own, can override it.

## Set the account

In **Connect → Agents**, choose for each agent the account this workspace runs it under ([Connect](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/connect.md)). A group or project can choose another; most never need to. The same switch installs Slate into that account, so its sessions are captured. A config folder exists once per computer, so workspaces that name the same one share its sign-in.

- A project inside a group uses the group's account.
- A project that joins a group takes the group's.
- A project that leaves a group keeps a copy of the group's.

A group or project covers its own folder and every project folder in it. A session belongs to the deepest folder that holds it.

## What it governs

- **Sessions started from Slate** run under the account of the workspace their project belongs to, whichever workspace the window shows.
- **Automations and skills** that belong to it, scheduled runs included.
- **Sessions you start in a terminal.** Slate installs a hook into each account that refuses the first prompt of a session running under the wrong account. The message names the right one, such as "Work runs claude under Work."

Only an account that another workspace or project on this computer uses is refused, so a Personal sign-in in a work folder is stopped. An account no workspace names still runs. An agent the workspace does not list is never refused.

A group or project can also set a default model per agent. It is a starting point; any model can still be used.

## Limits

- **OpenCode** has no setting for its config folder, so it cannot be held to one account. It is captured, not governed, and its row says so.
- **A group or project with no folder** cannot govern terminal sessions, which are matched by folder.
- **If the check itself fails**, an unreadable setting or a crashed hook, the prompt goes through.

---

# Connect

Source: https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/connect.md

**Connect** decides which agents a workspace runs on and which apps it reads your work from. It sits at the bottom of the rail and has two tabs, **Agents** and **Integrations**. Each workspace keeps its own choices.

## Agents

The tab opens with **Connect an agent**, the filters **All**, **On this Mac** and **Connected** with their counts, and **Find an agent**. Below is one row for each of the 16 agents, always in the same order, starting with Claude Code, Codex, Cursor and GitHub Copilot. A row never moves when you click it.

A row shows the agent's logo and name, and **Beta** for an agent nobody has yet checked end to end with Slate. A second line shows only when something is not normal, or when you chose a profile or model. A warning has a small amber dot in front of it.

| The agent is… | The row shows | Its **⋯** menu offers |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Connected | A small green dot | **Disconnect** |
| On this Mac, not connected | "not connected" | **Connect** |
| Not on this Mac | "Not on this Mac", greyed | **Install** |
| Slate installed, but not turned on here | "Not turned on · sessions not recorded" | **Connect**, **Remove Slate** |
| Turned on here, but Slate not installed | "Runs here, but Slate is not installed — sessions are not captured" | **Connect** |
| Installed for another workspace on the same profile | "Slate is installed here for Work" | **Connect** |
| Config could not be read | "Slate could not read this agent's config" | Nothing until it can be read |

Every action sits in the row's **⋯** menu, so the right edge of every row stays still. The agent marked **default** is the one used when nothing more specific is named.

**Install** shows the command to paste into Terminal, a second way when there is one, how to sign in, and the vendor's guide. Then press **Check again**. Slate never runs the command for you.

Click an agent's logo or name to open its dialog: its MCP servers, the profile it runs under, and its model ([An agent's dialog](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/connect/dialog.md)).

## What Connect does

**Connect** does two things: it installs Slate into the agent's config folder, so its sessions are captured and it can use Slate's memory and tools, and it records that this workspace runs on that agent. **Disconnect** undoes both ([How Slate installs into an agent](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/connect/how-slate-installs.md)).

- **Remove Slate** takes Slate out of an agent this workspace does not run.
- **Capture**: most agents have a switch in their dialog. Off, that agent's sessions are not recorded, and it stays connected. Cursor has **Capture sessions** / **Stop capturing** instead. OpenCode, Cline, Kilo Code and Auggie have no switch yet. **Auto-capture** in [Built-in automations](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/automations/built-in.md) stops capture for all.
- **A profile exists once per computer.** If another workspace runs the same agent on the same profile, disconnecting only stops this workspace, and the row offers no **Remove Slate**.
- **Claude Desktop** connects together with Claude Code: it gets Slate's tools and instructions, but nothing is captured from it. The Codex desktop app follows the Codex config.
- **VS Code chat** is captured through the GitHub Copilot connection, and shows in Sessions as **VS Code**.

## With no agent connected

A workspace with no agent cannot chat on Home, run automations, build widgets or learn memories. **Memory**, **Activity**, **Widgets**, **Automations** and **Toolkit** are dimmed on the rail, and pointing at one says why. Memory, Activity and Widgets open anyway once they hold something. Tasks, Projects and Artifacts work without an agent. Connect one and everything works at once, with no restart.

## Which agent runs

The workspace's agent runs everything, unless a group or a project on its own picks another. Home, Ask AI, New session and automations show which agent will run. With several agents in a project, Home and New session let you pick one per turn. **Make default** in an agent's dialog sets the one used when nothing else is named. The account each agent runs under is set the same way: [Project environments](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/toolkit/project-environments.md).

## Integrations

**Integrations** connects the apps you work in, such as GitHub, Jira, Linear or Notion. Press **Connect** and approve Slate on the app's own sign-in page, and what waits for you there shows in Tasks. Your agents can read these apps too, through Slate ([Integrations](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/connect/integrations.md)).

Importing projects, docs, memories and artifacts happens in Projects, Memory and Artifacts, from their **Import** button ([Import](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/connect/import.md)).

---

# Import

Source: https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/connect/import.md

Import brings in what you already have, so Projects, Memory and Artifacts do not start empty. Each has an **Import** button (a down arrow) in its header, before the **+**:

- **Projects › Import** has two tabs. **Docs** brings in docs you keep in other apps, as docs in a project. **Code** brings in the folders your editors opened, as projects.
- **Memory › Import** brings in what other tools remember, as memories.
- **Artifacts › Import** brings in HTML pages and decks you made elsewhere.

Slate reads a source only after you pick it, shows what it would add before adding anything, and never changes the other tool's files. Past chats from ChatGPT or claude.ai are not imported.

## The dialog

The dialog shows one tile per source, each with one short line: what Slate found, **Already in Slate**, **Not on this Mac**, or that Slate cannot read it yet. Pick a tile, then press **Preview** or **Pick folder** / **Pick file** under the tiles.

## Projects from your editors

| Editor | What Slate reads |
| --- | --- |
| **VS Code**, **Cursor**, **Windsurf** | The folders the editor opened lately |
| **WebStorm**, **IntelliJ IDEA**, **PyCharm**, **GoLand**, **Rider**, **CLion**, **PhpStorm**, **RubyMine**, **RustRover**, **DataGrip** | Each JetBrains IDE's recent projects |
| **Zed** | Not yet |

**Preview** lists the folders that are still on your computer, are git projects, and are not in Slate yet. Tick the ones you want and press **Add 3 as projects**.

## Docs from other apps

Each source asks for its folder or file and the project the docs go **Into**:

| Source | What you pick |
| --- | --- |
| **Markdown folder** | A folder of `.md` files; its folders stay folders |
| **Obsidian** | A vault's folder |
| **Notion** | Its export (Settings › Export, Markdown & CSV, a `.zip`) |
| **Google Docs** | A Google Takeout Drive folder, or `.docx` files |
| **Excel and CSV files** | `.xlsx` or `.csv` files; each sheet becomes a table in a doc |

Importing the same export into the same project again adds nothing.

## Memories from other tools

| Tool | What Slate reads |
| --- | --- |
| **Claude Code memory** | Its memory files. Most are in Slate already, because Slate reads them on its own |
| **Codex memory** | Its memory notes |
| **Gemini memory** | The memories saved in its `GEMINI.md` |
| **claude-mem** | Its observations and session summaries |
| **agentmemory** | An export file you make with its `memory_export` command |
| **Basic Memory**, **Cline Memory Bank** | Their markdown notes |
| **mem0** | A JSON file you download from mem0's dashboard (Memory Exports) |

**Memories with no folder go to** picks a project, or **Global memory**. A memory kept in a project's folder goes to that project; one from a folder that is not a project in this workspace is left out. **Preview** counts what is new, what waits for review because it repeats a memory you have, and what is left out, before anything is written. Imported memories start less sure than your own.

## Artifacts from elsewhere

- **HTML files**: pick a folder. Each `.html` file becomes an artifact, Slides when its body is a deck, an HTML page otherwise, with the file's date. A file already in Slate is left out.
- **claude.ai**: Slate cannot reach claude.ai itself. **Copy prompt** and paste it into Claude Code, which brings each artifact in with its real date.

A project's rules, skills and MCP servers are not imported here: open the project in [Toolkit](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/toolkit.md) and use **Start using .slate**.

---

# An agent's dialog

Source: https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/connect/dialog.md

Click an agent's logo or name in [Connect → Agents](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/connect.md#agents) to open its dialog. It shows the MCP servers the agent reaches, the profile it runs under, its model, and at the bottom the config file Slate writes into.

## MCP servers

The list shows the servers the agent declares, read from the profile this workspace runs it under. An agent that is not turned on here says "Turn it on for this workspace to see the servers it reaches." With none, it says "Nothing besides Slate itself." and **Add an MCP server** opens Toolkit's form.

- A **gateway**, one server that carries many integrations, is one row. Its chevron shows what it carries.
- **Your Claude account**'s connectors are one row under Claude Code, the only agent that can use them.
- A server declared for every folder says **every workspace**.

| Server | How it stands |
| --- | --- |
| **Read by Slate** | **Live**, **Needs sign-in**, **Not turned on**, **Unavailable** or **Not read yet**, with **Turn on** and **Let an agent read it** |
| **Not read by Slate** | What the agent last said: **Connected in Claude Code**, **Needs sign-in in Claude Code** or **Claude Code could not connect**. When it said nothing yet: **Set up, not checked** |

**Sign in** uses the same sign-in as Tasks for a server Slate reads, and the agent's own login for the others. **Refresh** asks your agents again.

## Profile

A profile is one login of an agent on this computer: its config folder, with its sign-in, settings and history. Pick the **Profile** this workspace uses, or **Add** one with a name and a **Config folder**.

- The add form offers config folders it finds in your home folder, such as `~/.claude-work`, under **Found here**. **Choose folder…** picks any other. A folder that does not exist yet is fine: the agent creates it when you sign in.
- Pick the profile before you connect, because it decides where Slate is installed.
- **Its usual settings folder** is the agent's own default, such as `~/.claude` or `~/.codex`.
- Some agents, such as OpenCode, Antigravity, Auggie and Kilo Code, read a single configuration, so there is no profile to choose.

A config folder exists once on this computer, so every workspace that names it shares its sign-in ([Project environments](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/toolkit/project-environments.md)).

## Model

The **Model** list shows once this workspace runs the agent. **Its usual model** lets the agent choose. **Make default** makes this the agent used when nothing more specific is named, and its row shows **default**. A group or a project on its own can choose differently.

## Capture

**Capture** turns recording of this agent's sessions on or off. Off, the agent stays connected and other agents are not affected.

---

# How Slate installs into an agent

Source: https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/connect/how-slate-installs.md

Pressing **Connect** in [Connect → Agents](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/connect.md#agents) installs Slate into that agent's config folder, once. The agent then reaches Slate's memory and tools, and Slate captures its sessions. The dialog's last line names the file Slate writes into.

## What it writes

Slate goes in one of two ways, never both:

- **A plugin**, for Claude Code, Codex, Gemini (as an extension) and Cursor. The plugin carries Slate's hooks and four commands, and the agent's own uninstall removes it. The plugin needs Node 24 or newer.
- **Hooks in the agent's config**, for the other agents that take hooks, and for the four above when the plugin cannot run. These config files apply to every project on the computer. Codex takes no config hooks: without its plugin it keeps only Slate's MCP server.

Every agent also gets one `slate` entry in its MCP config, which starts Slate's MCP server inside the app. Each session starts its own copy, so Slate's tools work whether or not the Slate window is open.

Each time Slate starts, it checks every connected agent and puts back what is missing, so Slate is installed exactly one way. Only **Disconnect** keeps it off. Slate installs no plugin while it runs from the disk image; it waits until Slate is in Applications.

## What you see in a Claude Code session

Claude Code prints one line when Slate loads or saves memory, at most once per session each:

| When | What prints |
| --- | --- |
| The session starts | `Slate · <branch> · 5 memories, 1 parked branch, 3 sessions` |
| The session saves memory | `Slate · saved 3 memories from this session`, and a notification |
| The session did work but saved nothing | `Slate · this session did real work but saved nothing yet.` |
| You made a plan | `Slate · you made a plan.` The agent then asks whether to save it |

Other agents get the same reminders in the form each one reads.

## Four commands

The plugin adds these to the agent's `/` menu:

| Command | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `/slate:brief` | What Slate knows about this project, in a few lines |
| `/slate:recall <what>` | Search your memory |
| `/slate:remember <fact>` | Save one memory, in your words |
| `/slate:open` | Open this project in Slate |

## What Disconnect puts back

Before its first write, Slate keeps what each file held. On **Disconnect**, a file only Slate changed goes back to exactly that, and a file Slate created is removed. If you or the agent edited the file since, only Slate's parts are removed.

If Disconnect fails, it says which part did not come out. For a stuck plugin it gives the command to run, such as `codex plugin remove slate@slate`.

## Check that it works

An agent whose hooks do not run looks like an agent nobody used. To check, run this in Terminal:

```
"$HOME/Library/Application Support/app.slate.workspace/hooks/slate-hook" doctor
```

It prints one line per agent:

| Line | Means |
| --- | --- |
| `3 hook(s) OK · last session <when>` | Working |
| `1 BROKEN of 3` | A hook cannot run. The lines under it say why and name the file |
| `3 hook(s) OK · no session recorded yet` | Slate's part is sound. The agent was not used since, its hooks wait for your approval, or it cannot sign in |

Two common causes of silence:

- **Codex runs no plugin hook until you trust it.** Until then `codex plugin list` says `installed, enabled` while nothing runs.
- **Gemini cannot sign in with a personal Google account.** Use an API key or a Gemini Code Assist licence.

The dialog also shows what the agent's last session ran: this Slate and when, or another Slate install, named, behind an amber dot.

---

# Integrations

Source: https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/connect/integrations.md

The **Integrations** tab in [Connect](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/connect.md) connects the apps you work in to this workspace. Press **Connect**, approve Slate on the app's own sign-in page, and what waits for you there shows in [Tasks](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/tasks.md). No agent is involved.

## Connect an app

Under **Connect an integration**, the chips **All**, **Issues**, **Reviews** and **Messages** narrow the list with their counts, and **Find an integration** searches it.

- **Sign in on the app's sign-in page**: **GitHub** (through your `gh` sign-in), **Jira**, **GitLab**, **Notion**, **Trello**, **ClickUp**, **Linear**, **Mattermost** (on your own server), **monday.com**, **Basecamp**, **Plane**, **Shortcut** and **Todoist**.
- **Paste a token**: **Bitbucket**, **Gitea** (Forgejo too), **Gerrit**, **YouTrack**, **Zulip** and **Rocket.Chat**. The form says where to make the token and which read-only permissions to tick. Slate checks the token with the app before keeping it.
- **Another integration**: any MCP server, by its https address.
- **Coming soon**: Slack, Microsoft Teams, Discord, Google Chat, Gmail, Outlook and Asana, each "Needs Slate's own" app; Azure DevOps and Zoom, "No server Slate can sign in to yet".

A sign-in or token stays on this computer, in a file only you can read, and survives restarts and updates.

## Read a row

A connected app that works is one line with a green dot. Point at it to see what Slate reads and when it last synced. Every action sits in the row's **⋯** menu: **Connect**, **Sign in again**, **Paste a new token**, **Choose what Tasks shows** and **Disconnect**.

A second line shows only when something needs you:

| The row says | What it means |
| --- | --- |
| **Needs sign-in** | The sign-in ended, for example after a new password. Choose **Sign in again** |
| **Unavailable** | Slate could not reach it, or the app blocks reads until you change a setting. The line says which |
| **Not read yet** | Slate has not found your tasks in it yet. Tasks shows its logo, never a 0 |
| **Learning** | Slate is working out where your tasks are, for an app like Notion that keeps them in its own database. If it fails: "Could not find your tasks in Notion." with **Try again** |
| Your admin may need to allow Slate first | Jira and Trello can require an admin to allow new apps |

An app you hide from Tasks moves under **Hidden from Tasks**, with **Show**.

## Notes per app

- **GitHub**: **Connect** turns on reading through your `gh` sign-in. A signed-in `gh` alone reads nothing.
- **Mattermost**: **Connect** asks for your server's address, such as `https://chat.example.com`. Your admin must turn on its AI plugin's MCP server first.
- **Zulip** and **Rocket.Chat** show only messages that name something this workspace works on.
- **Disconnect** forgets the sign-in or token. Its tasks leave at the next sync.

## Your agents read it too

An app connected by sign-in (not a pasted token) can be read from any session in this workspace while Slate is open, with no setup in the agent: Slate's `connected_tools` and `read_connected` tools use Slate's sign-in. Only tools that read are offered. See [Connected MCP tools](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/connect/connected-tools.md).

---

# Connected MCP tools

Source: https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/connect/connected-tools.md

When an agent works in Slate, on Home or in an automation, it reaches the MCP servers its own config declares, plus the apps you connected in Slate. Here, Slate reaches other servers. For the other direction, your agents reaching Slate, see [Slate as an MCP server](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/mcp-server.md).

## Servers from the agent's config

Slate keeps no server list of its own. The agent's command-line tool loads the servers in its config, for the profile it runs under and the project's folder, and reports which ones connected. [Connect → Agents](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/connect.md#agents) sets the profile; an agent's dialog lists its servers and how each stands ([An agent's dialog](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/connect/dialog.md)). Change a server in [Toolkit](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/toolkit.md) or in the agent's own config.

## Apps you connected in Slate

An app connected in [Connect → Integrations](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/connect/integrations.md), such as Linear, Notion or Jira, can be read from every session, even when the agent's config has no server for it, while Slate is open. Slate's `connected_tools` tool lists the apps and their reading tools, and `read_connected` reads through one with Slate's own sign-in. Tools that change anything are never offered ([MCP tool reference](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/mcp-server/tools.md)).

---

# Workspaces

Source: https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/workspaces.md

A workspace holds projects, docs, memory, activity and artifacts, in one file on your Mac. Switch into one and the whole app works inside it. A workspace is shared or private as a whole: in a shared one, everything is readable by its members, and nothing is marked doc by doc.

## Personal

**Personal** is the workspace you start with. It starts private. It cannot be left or removed, and it keeps its name.

## Switch workspaces

The **workspace tile** at the top of the workspace's icons on the rail opens the switcher. It lists every workspace on this Mac, each with its colour, and says whether the one you are in is **Private · only you see it**, **Shared · its members read everything in it**, **Shared, but not syncing** or **Read-only**. **Manage workspaces…** at the end opens **Settings → Workspaces**.

**⌘\`** goes to the next workspace and **⌘⇧\`** to the previous one. Going back to a workspace brings back the doc, the tabs and the rail icon you left. A workspace you have not opened in this window yet opens on Home.

What stays with each workspace: open tabs, favourites, recents, and its automations. What is the same in every workspace: the theme, the sidebar width, the live sessions, and which accounts your agents use.

## Share a workspace

Sharing needs the **Team** plan, which is coming. On Free, the **Sharing** switch is off and greyed out, with **Tell me when it's ready**; private workspaces are free, as many as you want. An account with early access can share now. Turning sharing off always works.

1. Open **Settings → Workspaces** and click the workspace.
2. In **General**, turn on **Sharing**.
3. Slate counts the docs, memories, activity rows and artifacts it would publish. Press **Share it** to agree.

From then on, everything in the workspace, and everything you add later, is readable by its members. To invite them, see [Workspaces and invites](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/workspaces/workspaces-and-invites.md).

## Bring a project in

Open the project's folder in the shared workspace, as you would anywhere. Its sessions, docs and memories from then on belong to that workspace. Nothing moves between workspaces: work done earlier in another workspace stays there. See [Working in a shared workspace](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/workspaces/sharing.md).

Your agents can search every workspace you belong to with `recall` and `scope: "workspaces"`, and read a shared doc with `get_doc`. See [Slate as an MCP server](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/mcp-server.md).

## How a shared workspace stays up to date

Slate syncs every two minutes and at launch. It sends only what changed since the last sync. **Sync now** in Settings → Workspaces syncs at once and says what moved. You can work offline: you are the only writer of your docs, so nothing conflicts when you come back.

## What actually leaves your machine

Everything in a shared workspace goes to its members, except what describes your Mac: folder paths, the text of AI sessions, and the memories you kept private. The exact list is in [Workspace sharing, precisely](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/privacy-and-security/sharing.md).

## Stop sharing, leave, or take back your work

| Action | What happens |
| --- | --- |
| **Stop sharing** | Slate counts what you published first; the button reads **Stop sharing and erase my work**. Publishing stops, and what you published is removed from the cloud and from every member's copy on their next sync. Your copy stays here. Share it again and the next sync publishes it as it is then |
| **Leave** | For a shared workspace: **Leave “…” and end my access** ends your access in the cloud, then removes this Mac's copy. What you published stays for its members; **Erase my work** takes it back. Offline or signed out, Leave is refused and nothing changes |
| **Remove from this Mac** | Keeps your access and removes only the copy on this Mac |
| **Delete workspace forever** | For a workspace that was never shared, this Mac holds the only copy: confirm **Delete “…” forever, with everything in it**. Export it from **Storage** first |
| **Erase my work** | Removes everything you published in the workspace, from every member's copy, while you stay in it. Sharing again does not bring it back. Editors and owners only |

If a connected agent still has the workspace open, Leave and Delete forever change nothing; quit the agent and try again.

If you are removed from a workspace, or its owner deletes it forever, your copy becomes read-only. You can still read and export it.

See also: [Working in a shared workspace](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/workspaces/sharing.md), [Workspaces and invites](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/workspaces/workspaces-and-invites.md), [Privacy and security](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/privacy-and-security.md).

---

# Working in a shared workspace

Source: https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/workspaces/sharing.md

Everything in a shared workspace belongs to its members. There is no "publish this doc" button: a doc you create there is shared at once, and so is a decision your agent saves there. Keep private work in a workspace you have not shared. A captured AI session's doc is never published.

## Bring work in

Nothing moves between workspaces. A doc, project or memory stays in the workspace it was made in, so private work never lands in a shared workspace by a menu click. To work on a project in a shared workspace, switch into it and open the project's folder there. Its sessions, docs and memories from then on belong to that workspace.

**One folder, one workspace.** A folder decides where the work done in it goes, so it belongs to one workspace on your Mac. Adding a folder another workspace already holds is refused, with the workspace's name: open it there, or move its project to Trash there first.

## A teammate's doc is read-only

Each doc has one writer, its author. A teammate's doc opens read-only, with a line that says why:

* *{Name} wrote this doc, so only they can change it.* Their edits reach you on the next sync.
* *This workspace is read-only*: it no longer exists, or you were removed from it. You can still read and export everything in it.

Who wrote what shows in three places: a teammate's picture at the end of their doc's row in the sidebar, *Written by you* or *Written by Sam* under a doc's title, and the author's name on a memory. A member Slate has not looked up yet shows as *A teammate*.

**You on two Macs.** Each Mac takes the newer version of your doc from the workspace and never sends an older copy over it. If you changed the same doc on both Macs before either synced, the later change wins, and the other is kept beside it as *{title} (copy from this Mac)*. Memories and artifacts work the same way.

## Removals

When you move your doc to Trash, it leaves every member's copy on their next sync. A teammate's doc under yours stays where it is. When you delete yours forever, theirs moves up to your doc's parent.

## Memory

A memory is filed under a doc. If that doc is in a shared workspace, the memory belongs to the workspace. What travels with it is in [Workspace sharing, precisely](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/privacy-and-security/sharing.md).

## Images

An image in a shared doc goes to the workspace's private storage in Slate's cloud, once. A teammate's Mac fetches the images its docs name. Until an image has arrived, its block shows no image. Only members can read the images; only owners and editors can add one, and nobody can change one.

## Artifacts

An artifact published in a shared workspace belongs to it, and every member sees it in **Artifacts**. Only its author can publish a new version, rename it or delete it forever. Only the newest version travels.

## Find a teammate's memory from your own copy

You and a colleague clone one git project into different folders. Slate matches the two by the project's git remote address, so your sessions find the memories your colleague's sessions saved.

* Only the remote counts: a folder with no remote matches nothing.
* Two unrelated projects with the same folder name share nothing.
* Every way of writing the address matches: `git@github.com:Acme/Site.git` and `https://github.com/acme/site` are the same project.

See also: [Workspaces](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/workspaces.md), [Workspaces and invites](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/workspaces/workspaces-and-invites.md).

---

# Workspaces and invites

Source: https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/workspaces/workspaces-and-invites.md

This guide covers making a workspace, inviting people, roles, and removing people or a whole workspace. All of it is in **Settings → Workspaces**.

## Create a workspace

Press **New workspace**, give it a name and a colour, and choose whether to share it. Press **Create workspace**.

* **Shared**: people you invite can read everything in it, and so can the agents they connect. Sharing needs the Team plan, or early access.
* **On this machine only**: nothing in it goes to the cloud. You can share it later.

Either way it is one file in Slate's data folder.

**Colour** marks the workspace in the switcher and in Settings, always beside its name. The colour is yours alone: each member keeps their own. See [Themes](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/theming.md#workspace-colours).

## Roles

A workspace belongs to an account: a company, or one person. Being in a workspace does not make someone part of your account; they see that workspace and nothing else.

| Role | Read | Write docs | Invite, remove, rename | Make an owner, delete the workspace forever |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **owner** | yes | yes | yes | yes |
| **editor** | yes | yes | no | no |
| **viewer** | yes | no | no | no |

The account's owner can do everything a workspace owner can. A role never lets anyone change someone else's doc: each doc is changed only by its author.

A viewer's copy is read-only on their own Mac too. A write there, including a memory an agent saves, is refused with a line saying an owner or editor can change the role. A role change reaches a Mac on its next sync.

## Invite someone

1. In **Settings → Workspaces**, click the workspace and open **Members**.
2. Type their email in **Invite by email** and press **Create invitation**. They join as an editor.
3. Tell them. Slate sends no email. The pending row has three buttons: email the invitation from your own mail app, copy a link that opens it in Slate, or copy it as text.

The invitation is tied to that exact email address. They join when they sign in to Slate with it and accept. Signing in with another address finds nothing.

**Accepting.** A banner at the top of the app names the workspace and offers **Accept** and **Decline**. Accepting adds the workspace to the switcher. A declined invitation stays declined until they are invited again. Nobody can be added to a workspace without accepting an invitation.

Pending invitations are listed with the members, and you can revoke one before it is accepted.

## Remove someone

Press remove on their row in **Members**. Their access ends on their next request. Their Mac marks its copy read-only on its next sync, about every two minutes: they can still read and export what they have, and nothing more arrives. The docs they wrote stay in the workspace.

## Delete a workspace forever

**Delete workspace forever** is in the workspace's **General** tab. Only a workspace owner or the account's owner can use it, and it asks twice. It removes every doc anyone shared there, for every member, without asking or telling them. Each member's Mac learns of it on its next sync: what they wrote themselves stays on their Mac, and the copy becomes read-only.

## Another Slate account on the same Mac

Each shared workspace belongs to the account that joined it on this Mac. Signed in with another account, Slate does not list or sync it. Sign in with its account again and it is back. Personal belongs to the Mac, whoever is signed in.

See also: [Workspaces](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/workspaces.md), [Working in a shared workspace](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/workspaces/sharing.md).

---

# Search and command palette

Source: https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/search.md

Press **⌘K** anywhere to open the command palette. One box runs a command, jumps to a doc, a session or a file, or searches your workspace: docs, tasks, memories, reports and artifacts. Search runs on your Mac and searches only the workspace you are in.

## What ⌘K shows

With nothing typed, the palette lists **Open tabs**, **Live sessions** (up to 5, the ones that need you first), **Recent**, **Favorites**, and 5 places under **Quick navigation**.

When you type, the results come in this order:

1. **Actions**: commands whose name holds what you typed
2. **Open tabs**
3. **Go to**: places, and a few Settings tabs
4. **Sessions**: live sessions, matched by title, project, branch or agent
5. **Files** from the open workspace's projects
6. **Docs**, **Tasks**, **Memories**, **Reports** and **Artifacts**
7. **In Trash**: a doc in Trash opens read-only, with **Restore**
8. **More actions**: looser command matches

If a project's files do not answer within 5 seconds, the palette names that project under the results; the others still answer.

## Search inside files

**⌘⇧F** (**Search docs and files**) searches doc text, then the text inside the files of every project and worktree in the open workspace. A file match shows the line, with its file and line number. Enter opens the file at that line.

The search is plain text and ignores case. It skips ignored and binary files, and includes new files an agent wrote that are not committed yet. It finds at most 200 lines and shows the first 30.

**⌘P** (**Go to file or doc**) jumps to a file or a doc by its name.

## Open a web page

Type a web address and the first row is **Open in Slate**. It opens in a tab inside Slate. It takes a full address (`https://example.com/docs`), a local server with its port (`localhost:3000`), a bare domain (`example.com`) or the full path to an HTML file (`/srv/site/index.html`). Ordinary words, file names such as `index.html` and versions such as `v1.2` search as usual.

The tab has back, forward, reload, an address bar, and a button that opens it in your browser. Your browser's sign-ins do not carry over.

## The rail and the sidebar

The **rail** is the column of icons on the left edge. It is always there. From top to bottom:

* **Sessions**, on its own: every AI session on this Mac, in any workspace.
* The **workspace**: its tile, then Home, Projects, Tasks, Memory, Activity, Artifacts, Widgets, Automations and Toolkit, with **Connect** and **Trash** at its foot. All of these belong to the open workspace.
* **Settings**, then **you**. These are the same in every workspace.

Rest the pointer on an icon to see its name and shortcut. In a short window, places that do not fit fold into **More**.

Beside the rail is the **sidebar**, the list for where you are. **⌘B** shows or hides it, and so does clicking the rail icon you are already on. With the sidebar hidden, resting the pointer on an icon shows its list on top until you move away.

## Tabs

The main area is one strip of tabs: docs, sessions, terminals, files, changes and web pages.

**A click opens a temporary tab**, shown in italics. The next thing you open replaces it. A tab stays when you edit the doc, double-click the tab, choose **Keep open** or **Pin** from its right-click menu, or open it beside the current tab with ⌘-click. A doc you create and a session you start open as kept tabs.

**⌘W** closes a tab, but a pinned tab stays until you unpin it. Closing a session's tab asks whether to end the session or keep it running. Open tabs come back after a restart, up to 20, for each workspace. All tab keys: [Keyboard shortcuts](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/shortcuts.md#tabs-and-the-mouse).

## Back and Forward

The two arrows in the top bar take you back to the screens you came from, and forward again, like a browser. **⌘[** and **⌘]** do the same, and so do a mouse's back and forward buttons.

A step is a screen you went to: one on the rail, a doc, a session or other tab, an artifact, a Settings tab. A filter or a view change on the same screen is not a step. Slate keeps the last 50 screens, and each workspace has its own list. An arrow with nowhere to go is greyed out.

---

# Trash

Source: https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/trash.md

**Trash** holds the docs and widgets you moved there, until you restore them or delete them forever. Open it from **Trash** on the rail, at the foot of the open workspace's icons. Each workspace has its own Trash.

## What goes to Trash

* **A doc**, with every doc inside it. Use **Move to Trash** in the doc's **⋯** menu in the Projects tree, or in the doc itself.
* **A widget**, with every version. Use **Move to Trash** in its **⋯** menu. See [Widgets](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/widgets.md).

Each row says when it moved and where it came from, such as *Moved to Trash 5 minutes ago · from Acme*. A doc that held others shows **N inside**; expand it to see them. Click a title to read it.

## Restore or delete forever

Point at a row, or move focus to it, to see **Restore** and **Delete forever…**.

* **Restore** puts the doc back where it was, with every doc that went to Trash with it. A doc inside it that you moved to Trash on its own, earlier, stays in Trash.
* **Delete forever…** asks first and cannot be undone. Docs nested inside go too. A widget loses every version and the data it kept. Memories filed under a doc deleted forever are kept, as global memories.

To act on several rows, tick them and press **Restore (N)** or **Delete forever (N)**. **Select all** ticks every row shown.

**Empty Trash**, beside the title, deletes everything in Trash forever after one question. **Filter by title** narrows the list; with a filter on, the button reads **Delete forever · N shown** and removes only the rows you see.

## In a shared workspace

Moving a doc you wrote to Trash removes it from every member's copy on their next sync. A teammate's doc inside yours stays. When you delete yours forever, theirs moves up to your doc's parent. See [Working in a shared workspace](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/workspaces/sharing.md).

---

# Themes

Source: https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/theming.md

Slate has two themes: **Mint**, which is dark, and **Forest**, which is light. Choose one in **Settings → Appearance**. Mint is the default.

## Switch between light and dark

Press **⌘⇧L**, or choose **Toggle light / dark theme** in the command palette. It switches between Mint and Forest, and the **Active** card in Settings → Appearance follows.

## What the colours mean

Most of Slate is neutral grey. The brand green marks only a few things: Slate's mark, the main button, what is selected, and the rail place you are on.

* **State keeps its own colours.** Amber means something needs you. Red means it failed, or the next step cannot be undone. Green means done or connected. A state always has a word or an icon too.
* **The running light is lime.** A session or a run that is working shows a lime dot.
* **Terminal output stays in colour.** A command's red still means a failure.

## Workspace colours

A workspace wears one of nine colours: **Cobalt**, **Lagoon**, **Iris**, **Silver**, **Orchid**, **Fjord**, **Heather**, **Wisteria** and **Graphite**. Choose one under **Colour** in the workspace's dialog in **Settings → Workspaces**. The colour marks the workspace in the switcher and in Settings, always beside its name. It is yours alone: other members keep their own.

## Make Slate bigger or smaller

**⌘+** and **⌘−** zoom the whole app in steps of 10%, from 80% to 140%. It starts at 110%. The size is saved on this computer, for every workspace. In a terminal the same keys change only that terminal's font.

There is no custom theme and no colour picker for parts of the app.

---

# Slate as an MCP server

Source: https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/mcp-server.md

Slate runs an MCP server, so every agent you connect works from the same workspace and the same memory: what one agent saves, the next one recalls. All 16 [agents](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/agents.md) can connect. To connect one, see [Connecting your agents](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/mcp-server/connecting.md).

## What an agent is asked to do

Every connected agent gets one short standing instruction. The details are in each tool's own description.

* **At the start of a task**, call `recall` with the question *current branch goal and context* and the working folder. It returns the brief for the branch, the project's conventions and its memories. An agent that Slate already briefed skips this.
* **During the task**, save a decision with `remember`, with its reason and what it turned down. Ask you before saving a plan, review, bug report or design with `create_doc`. If a memory's citation says `changed`, read the code first, and correct the memory if it is wrong.
* **At the end**, call `log_mission_progress` once, and save at most two memories: only what will change how a later agent works.

To check the connection, an agent calls `slate_capabilities`. It only reads, so it changes nothing. How `recall` ranks results and how `remember` avoids duplicates is in [Search and save](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/memory/recall-remember.md).

## Your workspace and your team's

`recall` searches the workspace that holds the agent's working folder, on this Mac. In a shared workspace, that includes your teammates' work your copy holds.

`recall` with `scope: "workspaces"` searches what was shared in every workspace you belong to, read from the cloud, including workspaces this Mac has not added. `get_doc` reads a shared doc whose id is not on this Mac. Both only read, and a shared result is marked `shared: true`, so your own knowledge and your team's never mix. See [Workspaces](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/workspaces.md).

## What an agent can and cannot do

Each part of Slate is one of three kinds:

* **The agent does it** with a tool: recall and save memory, read and add to docs, publish artifacts and widgets, read your Tasks list, start workers.
* **You decide it in Slate**: accepting a memory proposal or a suggested setup change. An agent can propose; only you accept.
* **Only in the app**: Home, Trash, Settings and your account.

The [tool reference](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/mcp-server/tools.md) lists all 27 tools and their arguments. [Tool rules](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/mcp-server/tool-rules.md) says which workspace a call reaches and what an agent may not do.

## See also

* [Connected MCP tools](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/connect/connected-tools.md): the other direction, where Slate reads the MCP servers your agents already have.

---

# Connecting your agents

Source: https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/mcp-server/connecting.md

Any agent that speaks MCP can connect to Slate and share its memory. What it can then do is in the [tool reference](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/mcp-server/tools.md).

## From Connect

Open **[Connect → Agents](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/connect.md)**, pick the agent and its account, and switch Slate on. Slate adds itself to that account's setup, so it holds for every project. [Toolkit](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/toolkit.md) can also write MCP setups for every agent.

The entry starts `slate-mcp`, a program inside the app. It opens your workspace itself, so the agent has Slate's tools whether or not the Slate window is open. The entry holds no key.

Three tools need the Slate app open: `connected_tools` and `read_connected` (Slate holds those integrations' sign-ins) and `run_automation`. With Slate closed they answer `slate_not_running`. Every other tool works.

**Sessions Slate starts itself**, from Sessions or Tasks, reach the running app over a port on this computer instead: 47366 for the first user account on the Mac, then 47367 and up. If another program holds that port when Slate starts, a red line at the top of the window names the port. Run `lsof -i :<port>` to find the program, quit it, and restart Slate.

## One click in VS Code or Cursor

Install Slate first. These links only add an entry that runs the app's `slate-mcp`, so they do nothing without the app.

[Install in VS Code](vscode:mcp/install?%7B%22name%22%3A%22slate%22%2C%22command%22%3A%22%2FApplications%2FSlate.app%2FContents%2FMacOS%2Fslate-mcp%22%2C%22args%22%3A%5B%5D%7D) · [Install in Cursor](cursor://anysphere.cursor-deeplink/mcp/install?name=slate&config=eyJjb21tYW5kIjoiL0FwcGxpY2F0aW9ucy9TbGF0ZS5hcHAvQ29udGVudHMvTWFjT1Mvc2xhdGUtbWNwIiwiYXJncyI6W119)

## By hand

Connect is the supported way. To write the entry yourself, run the program inside the app, with no arguments. For Claude Code, in `~/.claude.json`:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "slate": {
      "type": "stdio",
      "command": "/Applications/Slate.app/Contents/MacOS/slate-mcp",
      "args": []
    }
  }
}
```

Other agents spell it their own way: OpenCode `{type: "local", command: [path]}`, Codex `command` and `args` under `[mcp_servers.slate]`. Claude Desktop, VS Code and other clients take the same command.

A client started with no folder, such as Claude Desktop's chat, is asked to call `recall` with the conversation's topic, naming the project if there is one, instead of with a working folder.

## Check that it works

Ask your agent:

> "Use the slate_capabilities tool to check the Slate contract, then use recall with query 'test' to check if Slate is connected."

An answer that mentions your workspace means it works. Empty results are fine.

## The contract

Each tool, whether it reads or writes, and where a write lands:

<!-- slate-contract:start -->
| Tool | Access | Write target |
|---|---|---|
| `slate_capabilities` | read | — |
| `create_doc` | write | — |
| `get_doc` | read | — |
| `append_to_doc` | write | id, target.kind:branch, target.kind:knowledge_doc; ambiguity=refuse |
| `remember` | write | — |
| `recall` | read | — |
| `get_memory` | read | — |
| `log_mission_progress` | write | — |
| `list_memories` | read | — |
| `propose_memory_change` | write | — |
| `get_artifact` | read | — |
| `publish_artifact` | write | — |
| `get_widget` | read | — |
| `publish_widget` | write | — |
| `activity` | read | — |
| `handoff` | write | — |
| `live_sessions` | read | — |
| `propose_setup_change` | write | — |
| `get_agent_run` | read | — |
| `report_agent_run_step` | write | — |
| `start_agent_run` | write | — |
| `wait_for_runs` | read | — |
| `run_automation` | write | — |
| `my_tasks` | read | — |
| `update_my_task` | write | — |
| `connected_tools` | read | — |
| `read_connected` | read | — |
<!-- slate-contract:end -->

A tool can save a typed doc and add to a doc. Saving a doc of a type the branch already has rewrites that doc. Every tool carries the standard MCP labels, so a client can skip asking before a read. See [Tool rules](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/mcp-server/tool-rules.md).

A refused `remember` is not an error: the answer says `saved: false`, with the reason. Memory lands in the workspace that holds the call's working folder: Personal, unless a shared workspace holds it.

## Error codes

A failed call answers with `error.code` and `error.message`:

| Code | When |
| --- | --- |
| `invalid_arguments` | An argument the tool's schema refuses, such as a missing `id` or a wrong type |
| `unknown_tool` | A tool name Slate does not have |
| `approval_required` | `create_doc` without `user_approved: true` |
| `content_required` | `create_doc` for a typed doc with no `markdown` |
| `target_not_found`, `target_archived`, `ambiguous_target` | A doc target that does not resolve to exactly one live doc |
| `invalid_request`, `not_found` | A bad `update_my_task` call, or an item that is not there |
| `proposal_refused` | A `propose_memory_change` the project's memories cannot take |
| `not_a_project`, `invalid_proposal`, `already_offered` | A refused `propose_setup_change` |
| `artifact_not_found`, `invalid_artifact`, `is_a_widget` | The artifact tools |
| `widget_not_found`, `invalid_widget`, `build_failed`, `not_a_widget`, `version_conflict` | The widget tools. `version_conflict`: someone published a newer version meanwhile; publish again |
| `wrong_workspace` | The working folder belongs to another workspace than the session's ([Tool rules](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/mcp-server/tool-rules.md#which-workspace-a-call-reaches)) |
| `no_agent_run` | `get_agent_run` outside an agent run |
| `stale`, `closed`, `invalid` | A refused `report_agent_run_step` |
| `slate_not_running` | A tool that needs the app, while Slate is closed |
| `run_not_startable` | A `run_automation` id that names no automation, or one with no steps |
| `store_unavailable` | The workspace needs an update that only the Slate app makes. Open Slate once |
| `internal_error` | Anything else, with its message |

## If it does not work

- **"command not found" or "no such file"**: Slate is not in `/Applications`. Install it as in [Install and first ten minutes](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/overview/getting-started.md#install).
- **The tools appear but calls fail**: open the Slate app once, so it creates your workspace.

---

# MCP tool reference

Source: https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/mcp-server/tools.md

Slate's MCP server exposes 27 tools to your agents, grouped below by the part of Slate they belong to. An app that can draw views gets two more ([Views](#views-in-apps-that-draw-them)). Which workspace a call reaches, and what an agent may not do, is in [Tool rules](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/mcp-server/tool-rules.md).

Almost every tool takes an optional **`cwd`**, the agent's working folder. Slate uses it to find the workspace that holds the folder. Only `slate_capabilities` takes none. Every tool carries the standard MCP labels: its title, whether it only reads, and whether a write can replace something.

## Docs

| Tool | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `create_doc` | Create a typed doc: `title`, `doc_type`, `user_approved:true`, `markdown`, optional `parent_id`, `source_ref`. Without `parent_id` it files under the project holding `cwd`, labelled with the checked-out git branch. Refused without `markdown` or unless the user said yes first. In `markdown`, `- [pass] text` (or `[fail]`, `[blocked]`, `[open]`) writes a check item with that result. A second call for the same type on the same branch rewrites that doc. |
| `get_doc` | Read one doc by `id` or `target`: title, icon, breadcrumb path, Markdown body. An `id` this workspace does not hold is looked up in the workspaces you belong to: a doc shared there comes back with `shared: true`, its author and `updated_at` (needs a cloud sign-in). Old name `workspace_doc` still answers for one release. |
| `append_to_doc` | Append Markdown to a doc, by `id` or `target`; a check item is written as in `create_doc`. Replies with id, title and path. A ```` ```mermaid ```` fence, here or in `create_doc`, shows as a diagram ([Docs](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/projects/editor.md#diagrams)). |

Find docs with `recall` and `kind: "docs"`. Plain docs, rename, move and trash are app-only ([why](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/mcp-server/tool-rules.md#what-an-agent-cannot-do-over-mcp)).

## Memory

| Tool | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `remember` | Save one typed memory (`kind`: `decision`, `preference`, `state`, `fact`, `lesson`), filed by `cwd`. With `kind: "decision"` it also takes `rejected` (the options turned down) and `confidence` (`high`, the default, `medium`, `low`: 0.95, 0.8, 0.6), and writes a decision doc with the full reasoning under the project; the reply's `id` is that doc. Old name `record_decision` (`title`, `reasoning`, `alternatives`, `confidence`, `outcome`) still answers for one release. A near-duplicate strengthens an existing memory; a new claim on the same slot replaces the old. `replaces`: refs this corrects and retires. `when` makes a lesson fire on a matching tool call: `{tool: "shell", match}` or `{tool: "read" \| "edit", path}` (a match-everything pattern is refused). `index: true` pins it into the project index; `unindex` removes refs. Reply: `saved`, `memory`, up to 3 `neighbours`. Refused, with reason, when: the text is passing status, a git snapshot or a tool call's markup; a `decision` has no reason; an agent memory holds 3+ numbers (put them in `reason`); a `state` has no `subject`; the project's [memory settings](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/memory/decisions-and-facts.md#what-a-project-keeps) turn off that writer, kind or word; AI memory care is on and `reason` is under 4 words; or the workspace is read-only for you. A title-like line is kept with a `warning`. A claim contradicting a firmer memory waits for review in Memory. |
| `recall` | The one search. When the query is about the branch (names it, or asks what is open or in progress) the first result is the branch brief, with the `target_doc_id` writes file under. Then memories (BM25 over sentence, tags, citation, reason, plus small recency and confidence lifts), then docs whose text matches (not title-only matches or captured session docs). A memory under 0.7 of the best memory's score is left out. Each memory is a line with `ref` (`m:7f3a2b1c`) and citation, marked `weak` for a thin match and `citation: changed` or `gone` when its code moved. Default 15 results, max 25, at most half memories. `scope: "all"` searches every project. `scope: "workspaces"` searches what others shared across your workspaces instead (see below). `also`: up to 8 other phrasings or keywords, merged by rank. Then up to 2 artifacts matching every word (`artifact_id`, title, snippet, `link`). `kind: "docs"`: docs only, up to 20 hits with snippets. `as_of` (`2026-08-01`): memories only, as believed at the end of that day, later-replaced ones marked `until`. |
| `get_memory` | Read memories in full by `refs` (max 20): claim, reason, `citation` (`same`, `changed`, `gone`, `unchecked`), `evidence` (tools that confirmed it), `history` (what it replaced and was replaced by). Unknown refs return under `unknown`. |
| `list_memories` | For a tidy the person agreed to: the project's memories, oldest first, max 100 per call from `offset`, each with ref, kind, text, whether resting. Memories hidden from sessions are left out. |
| `propose_memory_change` | Propose a `merge` (2–50 `refs` into one `text`), a `retire`, a `lesson` (`refs` into one lesson `text` with its `when`), or a `skill` (a lesson as a skill file in the project folder; Slate offers these itself). A merge, retire or lesson applies at once; the person can undo it in Memory for 7 days. One the save rules refuse, and a `skill`, waits for the person: in Memory → Needs review (a skill in Toolkit), or in the [Review view](#views-in-apps-that-draw-them) of an app that draws views. `proposal_refused`: ref outside the project (unplaced refs under `unknown`), merge or lesson with no text, lesson with no `when`, or text the save rules refuse. |
| `log_mission_progress` | Report a session's work on its branch: `cwd`, `summary`, optional `branch` (if the work was on another git branch), `goal`, `open_items`, `decisions`. The summary becomes a session entry, goal and open items feed the branch's next brief, each decision becomes a memory, all labelled with the branch. Each item passes the memory policy and admission rules; refusals come back in `refused`. Makes no doc. |

## Workspaces

`recall` with `scope: "workspaces"` searches what others published across your workspaces: `memory` (one sentence each, with author) and `docs` (title, doc type, author, excerpt). Default 8 each, max 25. `get_doc` reads one of those docs in full by its `id`. Both read the [cloud](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/workspaces.md), need a cloud sign-in and are read-only. For a workspace you are not in, Row Level Security returns an empty result. Signed out, they say so.

## Activity

| Tool | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `activity` | What you did across tools and projects. `view: "recent"` (default): sessions newest first over `days` (default 1, max 90); one session is one conversation the tool gave an id; each row has a `docId` (its session doc, else its project's). `view: "parked"`: branches left with UNCOMMITTED changes and not revisited; `stale_after_hours` default 48. `limit` default 10, max 50. |

## Your Tasks list

| Tool | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `my_tasks` | Your [Tasks](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/tasks.md) list. `view: "today"` (default): your overdue or due-today to-dos, grouped as the Tasks tab does, plus the first 10 open items from your tools, each with its key (`PROJ-12`, `acme/api#412`). `view: "all"`: every open to-do and up to 100 items. Omitted counts: `more_tasks`, `more_items`. No meetings. Old name `my_work` still answers for one release. |
| `update_my_task` | Add a line to your list (no `id`, with `title`) or change one (`id`): tick (`done: true`), reopen (`done: false`), rename, or set/clear a reminder (`in_minutes` or `at` ISO instant; `clear_reminder: true`). Pass one of the three: two at once is refused, not resolved. A reminder notifies when due. Jira, Linear and GitHub items are refused, naming where to change them. Old name `update_my_work` still answers for one release. |

## Apps you connected in Slate

| Tool | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `connected_tools` | Apps this workspace connected in [Connect → Integrations](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/connect.md#integrations) (Linear, Notion, Jira…) and each one's read-only tools. `app` lists one. An app whose tools cannot be listed says why (for example, sign in again). |
| `read_connected` | Read through an app: `tool` is `<app>__<tool>` as `connected_tools` lists it, `args` are its own. Slate calls with its own sign-in, so your agent needs no MCP server for the app. Reads only; writing tools are refused. The answer is the app's text, marked `trust: "outside"`, cut at 20,000 characters; the same read within a minute answers from the last call. |

Both need Slate open (else `slate_not_running`) and read only the apps of the folder's workspace. Your rules treat a read through Slate as a call to the app: a Deny of `mcp__linear__*` holds here too.

## Other agents

| Tool | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `handoff` | Leave one note for the other agents in the project, or for one with `to`. Each sees it once at the start of its next turn. Notes that only narrate work in progress are refused, with the reason. |
| `start_agent_run` | Start a worker: an agent run in its own branch, worktree and terminal, with the tool you name (`claude`, `codex`, `cursor`…), on one task (`title`, `task`, `kind` bug or feature) in the project at `cwd`, or at `repo` when the session stands outside it ([Ask Slate](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/sessions/ask-slate.md)). The open Slate window opens its terminal; with Slate closed it waits. At most 3 open workers per session, and a worker cannot start workers. The worker's plan, questions and permissions go to the person. See [Workers](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/sessions/workers.md). |
| `wait_for_runs` | Wait until one of your workers stops (a plan or ship waiting for the person, a block, done) or `timeoutSeconds` pass (1–240, default 120), then get every worker's state. It never moves a worker. |
| `live_sessions` | Every AI session running now: tool, status (working / needs_you / idle), project, git repository, branch, title, last thing said, last active, goal and next unchecked item, doc id (`targetDocId`), folder (`cwd`). Read a session's doc by passing that doc id and `cwd` to `get_doc`. `cwd` limits to your project; your own `sessionId` leaves you out. |

When another agent works in the same project, Slate says so once at the start of a turn, with that session's own words and a doc id. Agents talk by notes: `handoff` with a `to` is a message, and a reply is another `handoff` addressed back. A note with no `to` is for everyone working here. There is no channel, inbox or queue.

## Artifacts and widgets

| Tool | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `publish_artifact` | Publish a doc in the **Artifacts** tab. Send `content` (whole doc), `file_path` (a file the tool wrote, inside its `cwd` or the system temp folder) or `edits` (`{old, new}` changes to the newest version; each `old` must appear exactly once). Dot files, files in dot folders below home (such as `.ssh`) and a `cwd` of home or `/` are refused. A new artifact needs `title` and `kind` (`html` or `markdown`); a new version passes the earlier `artifact_id` and keeps both unless given. Optional `description` and `live: true` (the artifact reads this workspace with `slate.query`: docs, a doc, memories, sessions of its project, read-only, up to 5,000 rows each; served with no network, scripts only from cdnjs, jsDelivr, unpkg). Changing `live` adds a version; identical content adds none. Returns `artifact_id`, `version`, `link` (a `slate://` address). `invalid_artifact`: empty title or content, over 5,000,000 characters, file outside the two folders, dot file, too-wide `cwd`, or an edit whose old text is missing or repeated. |
| `get_artifact` | Read before changing: `artifact_id`, optional older `version`. Returns title, kind, description, version read, newest version number and full `content`. Without `artifact_id`: every artifact, newest first. Unknown id: `artifact_not_found`. |
| `publish_widget` | Build and publish a [widget](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/widgets.md) (React files Slate builds and runs in **Widgets**). New: `files` (`[{path, content}]`) and `title`. New version: `widget_id`, only changed files (the rest kept), `delete_paths` to remove. A build error answers `build_failed` with each error's file, line, text and saves nothing. Optional `description`. Returns `widget_id`, `version`, `built_ms`, `published` (false if no file changed), `link`, and `render`: whether the window ran the new version without error (`status` `ok`, `failed`, `pending`; on failure `problems` and a one-line `next`). |
| `get_widget` | Read before changing: `widget_id`, optional older `version`. Returns title, description, version read, newest version, `files`, `render`, `playbook` (build steps and rules), `sdk` (TypeScript declarations every build is checked against) and `examples`: `curated` (Slate's) and `yours` (other widgets in the workspace as `{ widget_id, title, description }`, quoted as data). Without `widget_id`: every widget. Unknown id: `widget_not_found`. |

A widget's id given to `get_artifact` or `publish_artifact` answers `is_a_widget` ("This is a widget. Use get_widget / publish_widget."); a doc's id given to the widget tools answers `not_a_widget`, naming the artifact tools.

## Project setup

| Tool | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `propose_setup_change` | Suggest a change to the project's AI setup: `kind` (`fix`, `copy`, `create`, `improve`, `remove`), `item_kind` (`skill`, `command`, `subagent`, `mcp`), item name, `evidence` (the sentence the person reads). Optional `tool` (for `copy`), `file`, `draft` (whole file, for a skill or subagent `create`). Waits in Toolkit › Suggestions; writes nothing until accepted. Refused: `not_a_project` (`cwd` not a folder here); `invalid_proposal` (a `copy` without `tool`, a `draft` on anything but a skill or subagent `create`, a name not lower-case letters, digits, `-`, `_`); `already_offered` (same suggestion waiting or answered). |

## Automations

| Tool | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `run_automation` | Without `id`: this workspace's [automations](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/automations.md), each with `id`, `name`, `description`, `trigger`, `enabled`, `last_run`, `last_error`. With `id`: start that automation now, as **Run now** does, and get `run_id`; a run already going is joined (`started: false`). The run shows in Slate and asks before it acts, as any run does. Needs Slate open (else `slate_not_running`); an automation that cannot start answers `run_not_startable` with the reason. An automation that takes an item (a flow) starts only with `item`, on that item; without one, or on an item it does not take, it answers `invalid_request` with Slate's reason. Making or changing an automation is done in Slate. |

## Agent runs

Only for a session a Slate agent run started (first prompt "Slate task … (token)"). Listed in every session; outside a run `get_agent_run` answers `no_agent_run`.

| Tool | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `get_agent_run` | The run's current step, attempt and instructions; on the first step, the task's [card](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/memory/session-start-brief.md#a-session-started-from-a-task). Takes `cwd` and the `token` from the first prompt, or an `agent_run_id`. A blocked run returns why and tells the agent to wait. |
| `report_agent_run_step` | Report the step `get_agent_run` gave: `agent_run_id`, `step`, `attempt`, an `outcome` (done, blocked, needs_input, failed), a short `summary`, optional `body` as JSON text. A report for an old step is refused and names the current one. |

## Views in apps that draw them

Some apps can draw a small view inside their chat: Claude Desktop and VS Code today, and Cursor and Goose by their own docs (the MCP Apps standard). When an app says so at connect time, three answers are drawn as a view in Slate's own look, light or dark:

* `live_sessions` as **Needs you**: the sessions waiting on you, and a count of the rest.
* `my_tasks` as **Tasks**: your list, with a box to tick a line done (it calls `update_my_task`).
* `memory_proposals` as **Review**: the memory proposals waiting for you, drawn as Memory's own review.

Only such an app also gets these two tools:

| Tool | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `memory_proposals` | The memory proposals waiting for you: merges, retirements and lessons, with the memories each one touches. No arguments. Says so in a sentence when none wait. |
| `resolve_memory_proposal` | Accept or reject one proposal: `id`, `accept`. Only the Review view calls it, when you click. The app keeps it from the model, so an AI cannot accept a proposal by itself. |

An agent in a terminal cannot draw a view. It gets the same tools as text, without the two above. A view loads nothing from the network; it reaches Slate only through the tools the app calls for it.

## Contract

| Tool | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `slate_capabilities` | Contract version, every place in Slate with its tools (or `view`: the person decides it in Slate, or `app-only`) and why, each tool's access level and approval policy, schema hash. Read-only, no arguments. A tool's access level is its `readOnlyHint`, so they cannot disagree. |

## See also

* [Tool rules](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/mcp-server/tool-rules.md): which workspace a call reaches, secrets, targets
* [Slate as an MCP server](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/mcp-server.md)
* [Connecting Your Agents](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/mcp-server/connecting.md)
* [Search and save](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/memory/recall-remember.md): the memory tools in depth.
